6660dd9e7606f22f.title: RBI starts 3 surveys to capture inflation expectations, consumer confidence
6660dd9e7606f22f.summary: Reserve Bank on Tuesday announced three key surveys to capture inflation expectations of households and gauge consumer confidence in the country- the studies that provide input for bi-monthly monetary policy. The central bank has announced the launch of the November 2026 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH). "The November 2026 round of the survey is being launched. The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments on price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets," it said. The study will be conducted across 19 cities -- Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi and Thiruvananthapuram. In another statement, the RBI said the Urban Consumer Confidence Survey seeks qualitative responses from households regarding their sentiments on the general economic situation, employment scenario, price level, households'

The overall action of the RBI conducting such surveys is highly plausible.

075de34ce2677a23.title: DVAC conducts drone survey of irrigation tank in illegal sand mining charge against DMK’s E.V. Velu
075de34ce2677a23.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:50 am IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI The drone survey was conducted in coordination with the Revenue Department, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, and the police to assess the extent of damage done to the water body. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Officials of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted a drone survey of an irrigation tank in Malappambadi village near Tiruvannamalai in connection with allegations of illegal sand mining by former PWD and Highways Minister and senior DMK leader E.V. Velu for the party’s Northern Zone Youth Wing Conference held on December 14, 2025. DVAC sources said that the drone survey was conducted in coordination with the Revenue Department, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, and the police to assess the extent of damage done to the water body. It will also provide total depth and width of the tank that was mined for the purpose. by illegal sand mining. The survey was monitored by Ganesan, Deputy SP, DVAC (Ranipet), K.Selvam, Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO), Tiruvannamalai, and K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner. The assessment comes in the wake of a complaint filed by Arappor Iyakkam , an NGO, with the DVAC at its headquarters in Chennai on August 13 this year. The complaint alleged that large volumes of sand was illegally mined from the irrigation tank reportedly based on directions by the then PWD and Highways Minister Mr. Velu. The sand theft has reportedly incurred a loss to a tune of ₹8 crore to State exchequer, the complainant claimed. The sand was mined to reportedly level an open land of 124.56 acres, to organise the DMK’s conference. The conference was attended by former Chief Minister and DMK president M.K. Stalin and his son and former Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin. cb6a087f49e6adf0.title: RBI eases forex rules for services exports and imports
cb6a087f49e6adf0.summary: The changes form part of the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) which came into effect from October 1, 2026. Under the amended regulations, a resident individual exporting services will be deemed to have submitted the Export Declaration Form, or EDF, once the individual provides the authorised dealer bank with the information required to credit the payment to the exporter's account. No transaction-value threshold has been prescribed for resident individuals.

b076dd70c49e380d.title: In Tehran, a search for the future of West Asian security
b076dd70c49e380d.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 01:26 am IST ‘Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan travelling to Iran for this exchange came as a surprise to many given that Tehran had struck several Arab countries in response to American and Israeli aggression’ | Photo Credit: AP More than eight months after the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran , West Asia remains on tenterhooks, as the United States, Israel, and Iran continue to flirt with a resumption of military hostilities. Elections in Israel as well as the U.S. midterm polls offered an interesting pause, even as war rhetoric remained high. Amid these tensions, an alliance of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan, known as the “Mecca Agreement”, arrived in Iran’s capital in October to discuss regional security. A large part of Iran’s response since the U.S. and Israel began bombing the country in February 2026 has been to target American interests, including data centres, and military installations across the Gulf states. This forms part of Tehran’s strategy of asymmetric warfare, shaped by its view of the conflict as an existential threat to the Islamic Republic, particularly following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an airstrike. 0341b26a696066b0.title: On the Arunachal frontier, silence is not a strategy
0341b26a696066b0.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 01:18 am IST ‘Candour will strengthen New Delhi’s hand in dealing with Beijing’ | Photo Credit: THE HINDU/RITU RAJ KONWAR For some time, reports have circulated of transgressions by China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) in the Asaphila, Taksing and Longju areas of Arunachal Pradesh. The facts are neither clear nor officially acknowledged. Yet, there are signals that something out of the ordinary is happening along this stretch of the border. The matter warrants close attention. The clearest signal came on October 22, 2026. Speaking at an Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) function, Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor said: “In the past few days, a situation arose where face-off happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues.” This was the first official confirmation of the scale of the problem. This daily reported, citing “government sources”, that the two sides had been in a stand-off at Asaphila, near Taksing, since late July. 34e842c22574f838.title: BJP leaders criticise Mamata-Congress bonhomie
34e842c22574f838.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 01:58 am IST Former West Bengal Chief Minister and leader of the Trinamool Congress (TMC), Mamata Banerjee with Congress Leader Sonia Gandhi. | Photo Credit: Shashi Shekhar Kashyap The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leadership continued to criticise and raise questions about the bonhomie between the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress and the Congress party for the second consecutive day on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and accused the former Chief Minister of joining forces in Delhi to create anarchy in the country. BJP president Nitin Nabin made a similar charge against Ms. Banerjee during a procession in Kolkata on Monday (November 2, 2026). fd0d1593764da810.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
fd0d1593764da810.summary: Updated - November 04, 2026 12:58 am IST The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack. So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. I

The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. District teams have also begun physically verifying the proposed premises. The North District received around 25 applications as of Tuesday evening. Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Niharika Bhatt said verification had begun and licences were expected to be issued from Tuesday night. “The Central District has six permanent licence holders and has not received any applications for temporary licences so far. It received three applications for temporary licences in 2025,” said DCP Rohit Rajbir Singh. The police, along with Delhi Fire Services officials, are inspecting the proposed premises, verifying applicants’ credentials and checking ownership or tenancy documents. The checks also cover applicants’ criminal antecedents and compliance with prescribed safety conditions. Officials said the verification process usually takes a few hours. Fire Chief A.K. Malik said Fire Department officials would assess whether the premises were accessible to firefighting vehicles and complied with fire safety requirements. “Temporary sheds must be made of non-flammable material, with at least three metres between sheds and 50 metres from protected works (such as residential buildings, educational institutions, hospitals, places of worship, markets and other public spaces). A maximum of 50 shops is permitted in one cluster. We also check for firefighting equipment, safe electrical fittings and access for emergency vehicles,” said Mr. Malik. c01f2a67a822c282.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:43 am IST - Bengaluru H.C. Balakrishna. | Photo Credit: File photo Congress leader and Minister for Municipal Administration H.C. Balakrishna lashed out at senior Congress leader and MLA K.N. Rajanna on Tuesday, saying he was free to quit the party if he so wished, and accusing him of “betraying the party while being part of it.” This comes against the backdrop of Mr. Rajanna’s son and MLC R. Rajendra recently meeting JD(S) leader and Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy. Speaking to reporters in Chitradurga, he said, “If Mr. Rajanna wants to leave the party and join another party, he is free to do so. Let him honestly answer whether his son contested the election fairly. The election process had not even concluded when he posed for a photograph with Mr. Kumaraswamy. If the Congress party does not pay attention to such issues, it may have to face serious problems in the future. Mr. Rajanna is betraying the party while remaining in it. The party does not belong to any one individual. He has engaged in anti-party activities, and strict action should be taken against him. Lyricist Kaithapram Damodaran Namboodiri, poet P.K. Gopi and other cultural activists are seen. | Photo Credit: K. Ragesh People who visited the Kozhikode Corporation office or those who strolled through the nearby beach on Tuesday morning were perhaps amused by the songs emerging from a ‘pandal’ outside the gate. The activists of the Kala Samskarika Samyukta Vedi, a joint forum of over 40 cultural groups in the city, were staging a protest there seeking immediate steps to reconstruct the Tagore Centenary Hall, a prominent venue for cultural performances which was demolished a couple of years ago in view of structural issues. Opening the protest, lyricist Kaithapram Damodaran Namboodiri wondered if commercial interests were behind the delay in its reconstruction. Poet P.K. Gopi, who also spoke, expressed the concerns of cultural activists. The inaugural event was followed by singers rendering popular songs. Wilson Samuel, president of the Vedi, told The Hindu that there were no proper venues for artistes, singers, and actors in Kozhikode city at present. “The Town Hall can accommodate only 200-odd people. Though the renovated Jubilee Hall is comparatively big in size, the daily rent is ₹40,000, and there is no parking space. The Tagore Hall had a capacity of 1,200 people, and the daily rent was just ₹3,000. The corporation needs to create small affordable and accessible auditoriums across the city,” he said. Pointing out that the reconstruction was getting delayed possibly due to administrative or technical reasons, James Lazar, functionary of the Bankmen’s Club, said the Corporation should not have demolished the structure before making alternative arrangements. 3d972eaddd00d5f1.title: Man undergoing de-addiction treatment dies at private clinic in Kodungaiyur
3d972eaddd00d5f1.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:36 am IST - CHENNAI A 28-year-old man undergoing treatment for alcohol addiction at a private clinic in Kodungaiyur died on Monday. His family members alleged that medical negligence at the clinic led to his death. A senior police officer said, “We have registered a case of unnatural death. Further action will be taken only after receiving the post-mortem and viscera examination reports.” The deceased was identified as Lokesh, 28, Lokesh was assisting his father in real estate business. He had recently developed an addiction to alcohol. His family admitted him to a private de-addiction clinic in Moolakadai last week within the jurisidiction of Kodungaiyur police. A staff member at the clinic administered him an injection after his health condition deteriorated. As his condition worsened, his family members rushed him to another private hospital in Madhavaram, where doctors declared him brought dead. His body was subsequently brought back to the clinic in Moolakadai. Following this, his relatives and family members staged a protest outside the clinic, accusing its staff of negligence. Police personnel intervened and pacified them after receiving a complaint. The body was sent to Government Stanley Hospital for post-mortem examination. It was at Rs 255.37 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year. d05f7360afb4ab22.title: Mobile phone, power banks seized from Kannur Central Jail
d05f7360afb4ab22.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 01:51 am IST - KANNUR A mobile phone and accessories, including two power banks, a charger and three data cables, were seized from Kannur Central Jail during a search by prison officials on Monday. The prohibited articles were found hidden beneath stone slabs behind the jail’s second block. The Town police have registered a case and launched an investigation based on a complaint lodged by jail Joint Superintendent A. Shaiju. The repeated seizure of prohibited articles from within the jail compound has raised concerns over security checks. Inadequate inspection of food items and cooking materials brought into the prison is suspected to be facilitating the smuggling of such articles. e971873e9869d8c6.title: Bengaluru: South corporation shuts 63 commercial establishments in residential layouts
e971873e9869d8c6.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:42 am IST - Bengaluru The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. | Photo Credit: Image for representational purpose The Bengaluru South City Corporation has sealed 63 commercial establishments operating “illegally” in residential areas across its jurisdiction during a special enforcement drive conducted by officials. The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation). According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations. Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement. Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed. The Corporation said commercial establishments operating on roads narrower than 40 feet in residential areas were prohibited. However, several establishments had continued operations without valid trade licences despite being issued notices and instructions to vacate. The drive was conducted simultaneously across several wards in Kumaraswamy Layout, J.P. Nagar, Madiwala, Koramangala, Ejipura, Jakkasandra, Begur, Singasandra, Yelachenahalli, Uttarahalli, Gottigere, Bilekahalli and Arakere, among others. Commissioner K.N. Ramesh warned of strict legal action against establishments operating illegally or without the necessary licences. Published - November 04, 2026 12:42 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences

2fec4d1b944ad2de.title: SRMIST to open SRMJEE applications from November 4
2fec4d1b944ad2de.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 05:30 am IST - Chennai SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) will open applications for SRM Joint Entrance Examination (SRMJEE) for all courses on November 4. Applications will be available from 2 p.m. on the website www.srmist.edu.in for Engineering and Technology, Architecture, Management, Liberal Arts and Business Studies, Law, Medicine and Health Sciences, Hotel Management, and Agricultural Sciences programmes. The SRMJEE for undergraduate and postgraduate courses in engineering will be held in over 160 centres across the country. The first phase for the B.Tech, M.Tech, and M.Tech (integrated) engineering programmes will be held on April 17 and 18, 2027, and the last date to apply is April 2, 2027. The second phase will be held on June 19 and 20, 2027, and the last date to apply is June 4, 2027. SRM Law Entrance Test will be held between January 5, 2027 and June 30, 2027 through on-demand centre-based tests. The last date for applying is June 25, 2027. Students appearing for SRMJEE for Management can take the test online between January 11, 2027 and June 30, 2027 for which the last date for applying is June 25, 2027. Similarly, students appearing for SRMJEE for undergraduate and postgraduate courses in Health Sciences can take the test online in two phases. The first phase will be held on April 9 and 10, 2027, and the last date for application is April 4, 2027. The second phase will be held on June 11 and 12, 2027, and the last date to apply is June 6, 2027. For post-PG programmes, the exam will be held on April 9 and 10, 2027, and the last date for applying is April 4, 2027. SRMJEE toppers will receive Founder’s Scholarship that entails a 100% waiver of tuition and hostel fees. Besides, students will also be offered merit scholarships of 25% to 100% tuition fee waivers based on ranks across phases, subjects, and campus-specific criteria, according to a press release. Published - November 04, 2026 05:30 am IST Terms & con

c3ef18c2e0ed82e2.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 01:10 am IST - Bengaluru A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam. | Photo Credit: K. MURALI KUMAR Taking into account the irregularities reported at the Shiggaon examination centre of Haveri district in the Village Administrative Officer (VAO) recruitment examination recently, the Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) has decided to introduce several additional security measures. A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam. Haveri police are probing the case now. To prevent such instances, from now on, two invigilators will be appointed for every examination hall. One invigilator will stand at the rear of the hall to monitor candidates, while the other will remain at the front. They will also be responsible for ensuring that the mobile signal jammer in the examination centre is functioning properly. Although candidates are required to undergo thorough frisking before entering the examination centre, it was found that this rule had not been implemented seriously. Therefore, KEA has decided to conduct a second round of checking inside the examination hall as well. All candidates must reach the examination centre at least 30 minutes before the examination begins. Candidates arriving at the last minute will not be permitted to enter, H. Prasanna, Executive Director, KEA said. “Instructions have already been issued to establish district-level monitoring systems to oversee examination centres through webcasting. Going forward, KEA has also decided to appoint a separate invigilator at each examination centre to monitor CCTV footage,” he added. f678e794988cf1e5.title: Security guard dies in fire at Peravallur warehouse
f678e794988cf1e5.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:38 am IST - CHENNAI A 54-year-old security guard died of suffocation after a fire broke out at an e-commerce warehouse on SRP Koil Road in Peravallur on Tuesday morning. The warehouse, located on the first floor of a building, had been rented by an online delivery company to store goods ordered by customers. It had been functioning for the past two years. The fire broke out around 6.30 a.m. when the warehouse was closed. Ramamoorthy, 54, a security guard on duty, noticed thick smoke billowing out and entered the premises to locate the source of the fire. However, the blaze spread rapidly, trapping him inside. He collapsed due to suffocation. Fire and Rescue Services personnel from Kolathur and Sembium rushed to the spot and put out the fire. They rescued Ramamoorthy and took him to Periyar Nagar Government Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Peravallur police have registered a case and are investigating the cause of the fire. An electrical short circuit is suspected to have triggered the blaze. ff01b48fc3db8bdb.title: RPF head constable saves passenger from being dragged by train at Perambur railway station
ff01b48fc3db8bdb.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 12:33 am IST - CHENNAI A Railway Protection Force (RPF) head constable saved a 23-year-old passenger from being dragged along by a moving train at the Perambur railway station on Tuesday. The incident occurred when Train No. 12672 Nilgiri Superfast Express was departing from Platform 1. Mohammed Kajim Alam, who realised that he had boarded the wrong train, attempted to alight while it was moving. He lost his balance, clung to the grab rails near the coach doorway, and was dragged on the platform. Noticing the danger, RPF head constable Bhagchand Meena came to his rescue and pulled him away from the moving train, averting a possible tragedy. The passenger’s brother subsequently pulled the alarm chain, bringing the train to a halt. e1174ed557d93b84.title: 7,000 kg of unhygienic, foul-smelling khoya seized, destroyed: Delhi CMO
e1174ed557d93b84.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 03:49 am IST - New Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government would not compromise on public health. File photo: X/@gupta_rekha via ANI. The Food Safety Department of the Delhi government carried out an inspection at Mori Gate Khoya Market on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and seized and destroyed about 7,000 kg of unhygienic and foul-smelling khoya, taking the total quantity of khoya destroyed by the department so far to 10,660 kg, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government would not compromise on public health, and ensuring that people have access to safe and quality food during the festive season is one of the government’s foremost responsibilities. “Those involved in food adulteration, regardless of how influential they may be, will be brought within the ambit of the law and face strict action,” she said. Also, 35 of 44 samples of khoya failed preliminary tests at the ‘Food Safety on Wheels’ mobile testing facility. Two additional samples were also collected and sent to a laboratory for detailed examination. “The preliminary tests conducted at the site also brought to light information relating to milk powder, vanaspati and substances used for binding in the suspected material. Samples have been sent to the laboratory for further investigation into these ingredients,” an official statement said. The Food Safety Department has been conducting sustained drives against food adulteration in view of the festive season. As part of the action taken so far, the department destroyed 2,830 kg of khoya on September 4, 610 kg on September 8 and 520 kg on October 23, as per the CMO. 74e5df1dfed40c77.title: Kasi, food for soul
74e5df1dfed40c77.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 04:49 am IST Kasi is often called Anna Kshetra since Goddess Annapoorani, an incarnation of Parvati, resides there permanently. Coming down to earth to undertake a penance for a playful sport with Siva leading to consequences, She chose Kasi at a time when the town was reeling under severe famine. Armed with a ladle and a pot, She brought back prosperity and stayed on, heeding the local king’s request, and continued to bless devotees, said P. Swaminathan. The sacred town attracted saints, sages and ordinary devotees as well, especially around Deepavali. Long ago, Narayana Dikshitar, a staunch devotee who resided there, often invited holy men to his home and fed them humbly. On one occasion, after inviting a group of sadhus for a meal, he reached home only to find his wife bedridden. The guests were due in a couple of hours and a harassed Dikshitar went out seeking a solution. Just outside his house he spotted a woman walking past. Richly adorned, she had a talisman around her neck and a diamond nose ring. She looked at him kindly and the man blurted out his predicament. With a smile, she offered to help prepare the meal for the sadhus. The meal was a stupendous success and all the holy men blessed him. The woman had left the place after her duties and only then did Dikshitar realise that he had not even offered a meal to the woman who came to his aid. He went to bed with that thought and had a dream wherein he apologised to her and asked to see her; the woman declared that she was Annapoorani. She affirmed that She would always remain with those who have a good heart and a supplicatory mind. Informing him that She had left a green turban on the eastern wall of the house, She instructed Dikshitar to install her idol there. “I will remain here forever,” said Annapoorani. Visiting Kasi around Deepavali is considered highly efficacious. Published - November 04, 2026 04:49 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to

04fb5c818d6ed465.summary: Published - November 04, 2026 02:54 am IST Washington, November 3: Mr. Jimmy Carter, the peanut farmer from Georgia, who was a political unknown until early this year was elected the 39th President of the United States after he defeated the White House incumbent, Mr. Gerald Ford, in a closely fought election held yesterday. It was a remarkable achievement for a “rank outsider” who had started his quest for the Presidency two years ago, without much money, without a real political base and without going through the traditional corridors of power. To the loser, Mr. Ford, who was unexpectedly and accidentally elevated to the highest place in the land after Mr. Richard Nixon resigned 28 months ago, it was the end of a long but unspectacular career in politics. 26918faa89f2d1ac.title: Ambani tops Forbes' billionaire gainers list with $6.3 bn wealth jump
26918faa89f2d1ac.summary: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani has emerged as the world's biggest billionaire wealth gainer, adding over USD 6 billion to his fortune in a single day, as shares of his flagship company surged following a stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings performance. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, Ambani's wealth increased by 7.85 per cent, or USD 6.3 billion, making him the biggest gainer globally in the latest update to the ranking on November 2. The gain was substantially ahead of the second-biggest wealth accretion on the list, with Spanish retail billionaire Amancio Ortega adding USD 1.7 billion, followed by China's Zhong Shanshan at USD 1.5 billion. The gains pushed Ambani to No.23 spot on the world billionaire list, making him the richest Indian ahead of Gautam Adani, who was ranked at No.26 with a wealth of USD 79.12 billion, according to the Forbes listing. bf5ea52deba87aaa.title: IPO fundraising rises 30% to record ₹84,400 crore in H1FY27: Report
bf5ea52deba87aaa.summary: India's mainboard IPO market witnessed a record fund mobilisation at Rs 84,400 crore in the first half of FY27, registering a 30 per cent rise over the year-ago period, with nearly 94 per cent of the funds raised during the July-September period, according to a report by Grant Thornton Bharat. As many as 71 companies made their stock market debut during April-September 2026, compared with 55 in the corresponding period a year ago. According to the report, the funds raised increased from Rs 64,900 crore in H1 FY26 to Rs 84,400 crore in H1 FY27. The average listing-day gains improved to 18 per cent from 10 per cent a year ago, while average retail oversubscription increased to 28 times from 25 times, the report titled 'India IPO Market: H1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 Review' said. Notably, September was the busiest month, with 32 IPOs collectively raising Rs 40,400 crore. In terms of sectoral contribution, financial services accounted for 43 per cent of the total capital mobilised during H1 FY

Those earning more than £50,271 per annum, doctors, nurses and teachers will be able to settle in five years, while those earning more than £1,25,140 per annum could settle in three years, as was proposed in the November 2025 draft rules. 92e91ead481f85e3.title: Amit Shah backs SIR, alleges 3 crore ‘illegal infiltrators’ identified in 13 crore deleted voters
92e91ead481f85e3.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 01:48 am IST - HYDERABAD Union Home Minister Amit Shah addresses a public meeting during the ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ campaign in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2). | Photo Credit: RAMAKRISHNA G Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday alleged that the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise had identified around three crore ‘unaccounted voters’, whom he described as ‘illegal infiltrators from Bangladesh’, among the 13 crore names removed from electoral rolls. He asserted that all such infiltrators would be expelled from the country. Addressing a public meeting at MJ Market in Hyderabad’s Old City after a ‘Save democracy-Remove anarchy’ foot march , Mr. Shah claimed that of the nearly 13 crore names deleted from voter lists during the SIR process, 4.25 crore voters were registered in two different locations, three crore were deceased, and another one crore were duplicate entries. He questioned if such names should continue to remain on the electoral rolls. “Do we need to remove infiltrators from the country’s voter lists or not?” he asked. The Home Minister accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of defending the alleged three crore ‘unaccounted’ voters. “No matter how hard Rahul Gandhi or Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy may try, the BJP is committed to driving every infiltrator out of the country,” he said. Mr. Shah alleged that the Congress and other Opposition parties were opposing the SIR exercise to protect ‘infiltrators from Bangladesh’, whom he described as their ‘vote bank’ and maintained that only genuine Indian citizens should be included in electoral rolls. Ridiculing Sunday’s joint rally of Opposition parties in New Delhi, Mr. Shah described it as a ‘Save Infiltrators’ rally and urged BJP workers to counter what he termed ‘fear-mongering’ by the former on the SIR exercise through a door-to-door campaign. The Congress was determined to halt SIR while the BJP would continue to support it

b850f1e5733062c8.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
b850f1e5733062c8.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 05:43 am IST Petronet LNG declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share. | Photo Credit: The Hindu State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia. The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share. The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore. The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year. Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year. Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year. Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure. “On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said. The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end. Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028. He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier. 63144a20885888e1.title: Fifty years ago | Soviet Cars for Malaysia
63144a20885888e1.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 04:06 am IST SINGAPORE, Nov. 2.: The Soviet Union might assemble its cars in Malaysia and was now seeking to export Moskvich cars to the country, the Soviet Ambassador in Kuala Lumpur, Mr. Bendryshev, said last weekend. All plans for import of cars were ready and only the Government’s license was required, he added. “We have got the technical equipment, diesel engines, aircraft and ships to name a few for export,” he said. The Soviet Union was keen on co-operating with Malaysia to help it to implement its Third Plan by supplying technical expertise and equipment. It was willing to help in energy producing projects, deepening fishing port construction and irrigation projects, he said. Trade expansion and economic co-operation with foreign countries were in line with Russia’s latest five-year plan to produce more goods for export. 478c19867d6818b6.title: Cyclonic storm Murasu to make landfall close to Ongole
478c19867d6818b6.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 02:42 am IST - VIJAYAWADA A satellite image of Cyclone Murasu over the Bay of Bengal on Sunday. IMD | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement As the cyclonic storm, Cyclone Murasu , moves towards the A.P. coast, the State has deployed six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams in districts likely to be affected by the cyclone. According to information from the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), the landfall point is likely to be Ongole and in this connection, two teams each have been stationed in the districts of Krishna, Bapatla, Guntur, Nellore and Prakasam, while one team each has been deployed in Markapuram, Palnadu and Tirupati districts. Additional teams are also available for deployment if required. Murasu is the second cyclonic storm to hit A.P. in less than a week. According to the 9 p.m. bulletin from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the cyclonic storm centred over Southwest and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 5.30 p.m. It was located about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai, 490 km east-southeast of Nellore, 500 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 510 east-southeast of Kavali, 530 km southeast of Ongole and 560 km south-southeast of Vishakhapatnam. The IMD said the system may intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over Westcentral Bay of Bengal in the early hours of November 2. The landfall will be close to the Ongole coast, with a wind speed of 100 to 120 kmph, in the early hours of November 3. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected at one or two locations in the districts of Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Markapuram and Nellore on Monday. NTR and Guntur districts have announced holidays for all government and private schools, junior colleges and degree colleges on Monday (November 2, 2026). People can report any cyclone-related problems to officials through the Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance service at 95523 00009. For emergenc

9c21bc940db95f10.title: US judge dismisses Trump admin lawsuit against Harvard over admissions data
9c21bc940db95f10.summary: A federal judge on Monday dismissed a lawsuit against Harvard University over its alleged failure to provide admissions records that the Justice Department had demanded to ensure the Ivy League school stopped using affirmative action in admissions. The Justice Department said Harvard had "thwarted" efforts to investigate potential discrimination. It accused Harvard of refusing to comply with a federal investigation and asked a judge to order the university to turn over the records. But US District Judge Myong Joun concluded that the Justice Department didn't take the necessary procedural steps to obtain the data before filing the lawsuit. "Before taking enforcement action under the statutory framework, the agency must advise the recipient of its failure to comply and determine that compliance cannot be secured by voluntary means," Joun wrote. 69f62dc9701a46b5.title: Craft Council of A.P. receives praise for providing platform for weavers, artisans
69f62dc9701a46b5.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 12:36 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Heritage Foods executive director Nara Brahmani examines a saree at a stall after inaugurating ‘Vasantam’ crafts and textiles exhibition in Vijayawada on Monday. | Photo Credit: K.V.S. Giri The Craft Council of Andhra Pradesh (CCAP) inaugurated ‘Vasantham’, an exhibition showcasing the rich heritage of handlooms, handicrafts and traditional crafts of India, in Vijayawada on Monday. Heritage Foods executive director Nara Brahmani visited the exhibition and interacted with the weavers and artisans, and appreciated the efforts of the Craft Council of A.P. in organising the exhibition. She also commended the initiative for providing a valuable platform to weavers and artisans to showcase their products, reach customers and promote their traditional crafts. She said that such exhibitions were extremely beneficial in supporting the weaving community and encouraging the preservation of our rich craft heritage. The two-day exhibition will conclude on November 3 (Tuesday). It remains open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. at Sesha Sai Kalyana Mandapam, Vedika in the city. e9958b1c4de528c6.title: Police foil bid to snatch smuggled gold from woman at Karipur
e9958b1c4de528c6.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 08:23 am IST File photo for representational purpose only. The police foiled an attempt to abduct a woman carrying 817 gm gold worth over ₹1.10 crore at Calicut International Airport, Karipur, on Monday. They also arrested two members of the alleged robbery gang. According to the police, the incident took place around 3 a.m. A police team noticed a group behaving suspiciously in the arrival area and kept them under watch. The group followed Abhirami, 27, a native of Vandanmedu in Idukki, after she arrived from abroad. When Abhirami reached the parking area with a man who had come to receive her, the gang blocked their way and grabbed her trolley bag. The police team intervened when the gang tried to overpower the man accompanying her. During the struggle, the accused attacked the police and bit home guard Murali Krishna. They also tried to run over a member of the police team with a car while escaping. The officer narrowly escaped from being hit. The police arrested Sayanth, 28, and Babilesh, 40, both from Kallachi, Nadapuram. Abhirami and Harshal, 40, a native of Kochi who had arrived to collect the gold, were also taken into custody. The police said the gold had been sent with Abhirami by Swalih, a native of Thamarassery. Around 10 people had reached the airport in two cars to seize the gold and abduct her. A search of Abhirami’s baggage led to the recovery of 14 gold plates concealed inside an emergency lamp. The gold weighed 817 gm after cleaning and is estimated to be worth more than ₹1.10 crore. The gold, along with ₹67,000 allegedly kept to pay Abhirami for carrying it, a car and the two people detained in connection with the gold, were handed over to the Customs Department for further action. The police said the arrested men had been involved in several similar cases. One of them had lost a hand in a blast. b7ebb6640bbe2a16.title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump admin's push to set aside California ballots
b7ebb6640bbe2a16.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump's administration claims are noncitizens, a decision that comes on the eve of the pivotal midterm elections. The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls. It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term. In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters. The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions.

ec05d0c73acf6bca.title: Netanyahu presses Trump for fresh Iran strikes after US midterm elections
ec05d0c73acf6bca.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter. A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. US President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran. The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran's ports. They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefing

Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. 6fe4e482fbc13805.title: A hundred years ago | Tutankh-Amen’s Tomb: Contents of the Second Chamber
6fe4e482fbc13805.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 03:57 am IST CAIRO, Nov. 2.: The newspaper Siasash learns from a trustworthy source that the contents of the third chamber of Tutankh-Amen’s tomb have recently been opened and while they are not so rich and fine as those of the other two chambers they are of great historical importance, because they represent everything used for the funeral ceremony. Thirty small boats of two kinds were found, one sort being that used for funerals for journeying from Luxor across the Nile to the tombs and the other sort intended to transport the body from the earth to heaven. A very interesting box of small statuettes has also been found having Tutankh-Amen’s head but the body of a bird or animal, giving the Egyptian conception after life and two chariots have been found unornamented. They were supposed to have been used during hunting. These are the first of their kind ever discovered. 729df165de669f2f.title: Mangala sloka for Rama
729df165de669f2f.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 04:50 am IST When Valmiki saw a hunter kill one of a pair of krauncha birds, he cursed the hunter through a sloka. But the sloka can also be interpreted differently, in a positive sense, said M.A. Venkatakrishnan in a discourse. Valmiki’s sloka begins with the word manishadah . If you split this as ma and nishada , then it is Valmiki addressing the hunter ( nishada ). Valmiki curses the hunter, “Oh hunter! You killed one of two birds which were making love ( kaamamohitam ). Because of that, you will never have any peace.” But if the word manishadah is not split, then it means the One who is never separated from ma , that is Mahalakshmi. So, this can be taken as a reference to Rama Himself. While the words shasvathi samah pratistham tvam agamah have a negative meaning when we take them as referring to the hunter, they also can mean ‘May you live long.’ Kaamamohitam can be seen as a reference to Ravana, who was caught in kama (lust) for Sita. So, the entire sloka can be seen as a mangala sloka for Rama, the One who is never separated from Sita and the One who killed the lustful asura. While Valmiki’s intention was to curse the hunter, it so happened that he presented the Ramayana story in a nutshell through that sloka. There are certain rules to be followed while writing a kavya . A mahakavya must have thousands of verses, and Valmiki’s Ramayana has 24,000 verses. Although many versions of the Ramayana came up later, Valmiki’s is the authentic account, because he was witness to everything that happened in Rama’s life, thanks to the divine vision which Brahma gave him. When Lord Narayana decided to take the Rama avatara, Veda Purusha decided to take an avatara as Valmiki Ramayana. So, the Ramayana is the embodiment of Vedic tenets. It has many tattvas which need deep study and analysis. Published - November 03, 2026 04:50 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 0056552907126bc0.title: Bajaj Auto's total sales during October rise 14% to 591,876 units
0056552907126bc0.summary: Bajaj Auto on Monday posted a 14 per cent year-on-year growth in its total sales during October, with double-digit growth across two-wheelers and commercial vehicles. The automaker's total wholesales stood at 5,91,876 units, against 5,18,170 units in the year-ago period, according to an exchange filing. Domestic sales rose 12 per cent to 3,51,148 units, while exports grew 18 per cent to 2,40,728 units. Total two-wheeler sales increased by 13 per cent to 5,01,194 units from 4,42,316 in the year-ago period. Total commercial vehicle sales were higher by 20 per cent to 90,682 units, compared to 75,854 units. Bajaj Auto's total sales during the April-October period rose 22 per cent to 35,79,011 units. Two-wheeler sales rose 22 per cent to 30,07,707 units, while commercial vehicle sales were higher by 23 per cent at 5,71,304 units.

6ce0c0e80e6eb1d2.title: SC says 'don't travel by air', refuses urgent hearing on airfare hike plea
6ce0c0e80e6eb1d2.summary: Don't travel by air, the Supreme Court told a petitioner on Monday while refusing urgent listing of a plea alleging nearly 700 per cent increase in airfares. An advocate mentioned the matter for urgent listing before a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh. "The aviation fare has increased by 700 per cent," the advocate said. "Don't travel by air," the bench observed. The advocate then said air travel is an essential service. "It's a violation of Article 14." Article 14 of the Constitution deals with equality before law. 114481a9559f90ba.title: US consortium pushes for $4.4 billion LNG project in Pakistan: Report
114481a9559f90ba.summary: A consortium of American companies, backed by US President Donald Trump's administration, is seeking up to USD 4.4 billion in investment for an integrated liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Pakistan, according to a media report on Monday. The proposed project will cover imports, storage, regasification, gas transmission and sales to large consumers on a merchant basis, the Dawn newspaper reported. LNG is natural gas that has been cooled to around minus 162 degrees Celsius, turning it into a liquid and reducing its volume by about 600 times. This makes it easier to store and transport by specialised ships. At its destination, the LNG is converted back into gas through a process called regasification and supplied to consumers. It is used to generate electricity, fuel industrial processes, produce fertilisers and provide energy for heating and cooking. It is also used as a fuel in some vehicles and ships. bd9e4166ce611995.title: Palaniswami expresses concern over lower growth rate in Tamil Nadu’s GST collections
bd9e4166ce611995.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:55 pm IST - Chennai AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami. | Photo Credit: R SENTHILKUMAR The AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Monday expressed concern over the previous month’s reported three per cent growth in the Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections in Tamil Nadu, which was much below the national average. In a post on his social media handle, Mr. Palaniswami referred to the State’s level of inflation which was higher than that of the all-India figure and “diversion” of industrial projects to other States, similar to what was shown in a feature film of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. “How would the GST collections go up unless industry achieved progress, which would, in turn, generate jobs; enable higher growth in Gross Domestic Production and rise in per capita income?” Mr. Palaniswami wondered. Recalling that the Guidance Tamil Nadu, the nodal agency for investment promotion and single-window facilitation, was established when Jayalalithaa was Chief Minister, the AIADMK leader accused the present TVK-led government of having “ruined” it. Stalin on Monday (November 2, 2026) said people should brace for difficult times as “Tamil Nadu was doomed” under the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government. In a social media post, he said the State’s growth rate in Goods and Services Tax (GST) revenue had fallen below the national average under the TVK government. e21b19eda890a1b1.title: Telangana plans AI-enabled transactions in agri. market yards
e21b19eda890a1b1.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:51 pm IST - HYDERABAD Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao holding a meeting with marketing officials in Hyderabad on Monday. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement The Telangana government is planning to make the agricultural markets in the State AI (artificial intelligence)-enabled for the first time in the country and also make them model markets, Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao said. At a meeting with the agricultural marketing and agriculture departments here on Monday, he said the AI technology would check for irregularities in transactions in market yards. Tenders for introduction of AI technology in the market yards’ transactions would be called within a week. He suggested them to bring into a single digital system all transactions related to farmers — from the farmer entering the market with his/her produce, its sale, payments and others till he/she leaves the market yard. Listing of farmers’ details, allocation of identity number to every lot/crop, assessing crop quality, fixing price, digital bidding/tender details, online auction, farmer’s consent, weighing, sale bills, market charges, payments to farmers, recording of gate exit, e-receipts and e-permits issuance should be done on a single platform. The management information system should also have details of commission agents, traders, price patterns, auction details and others so that they can be cross-checked in future too. The Minister told the officials to study the digital marketing systems being implemented elsewhere in the country. Even the attendance of marketing department officials, including biometric attendance registering, be also made part of the new digital system. The market yards should also have closed-circuit camera systems to monitor maintenance of godowns and daily activities. Digital screens also be arranged so that farmers could know about the prices elsewhere in the country. On the Koheda integrated fruit market, the Minister ask

Badrinath was unanimously elected president of Exnora, Tiruchi, for a two-year term at the general body meeting of the organisation held here recently. The following were the other office-bearers selected at the meeting: Alagappa Moses (secretary); Anand Gideon and Rajagopal (vice-presidents); and Ravichandran (director). It planned to plant about 25,000 trees in the next five years with the support of government agencies and organisations, he said. M.B. Nirmal, founder, Exnora, and others attended the meeting, according to a communication from Exnora. ff536a96e0fae5ce.title: CPI(M) seeks action against Pendurthi MLA over alleged irregular voting in GVMC polls
ff536a96e0fae5ce.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:45 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM The Communist Party of India (Marxist) on Monday petitioned the District Collector, seeking legal action against Pendurthi MLA Panchakarla Ramesh Babu and the concerned polling officials over an alleged irregularity in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections held on November 1. In a representation, party district secretary M. Jaggunaidu alleged that Mr. Ramesh Babu voted for the mayoral and corporator candidates at Booth No. 115/8 in Ward 115, where, he claimed, the MLA had no vote. He further alleged that the booth officials issued ballot papers to the MLA in violation of election law, and contended that such conduct would erode public confidence in the electoral process. The party leaders demanded a thorough enquiry and action against the legislator and concerned officials. According to the leaders, complaints were submitted to the State Election Commissioner and the Returning Officers of the GVMC Pendurthi zone. 88523712e648304f.title: Joint survey to resolve Revenue-Forest land disputes: Ponguleti
88523712e648304f.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:43 pm IST - HYDERABAD Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy at a review meeting with Revenue, Forest and Survey and Settlement officials at the Secretariat on Monday. The Telangana government has decided to undertake joint surveys by the Revenue and Forest departments to find a permanent solution to long-pending disputes over land boundaries, particularly those involving forest, revenue and patta lands. Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy directed officials of both departments to work in close coordination and ensure that ordinary people and farmers do not suffer because of inter-departmental boundary disputes. At a review meeting with Revenue, Forest and Survey and Settlement officials at the Secretariat, the Minister said the government, under the leadership of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, was committed to resolving land-related issues that had remained unsettled for decades. Pointing out that the erstwhile Khammam, Warangal and Adilabad districts had substantial forest areas, Mr. Ponguleti said boundary disputes between the Revenue and Forest departments had persisted for several decades. He called for scientific and technology-based joint surveys to establish clear boundaries and prevent such disputes from recurring. Officials should examine the actual ground position and comprehensively reconcile land records, maps and survey details before arriving at conclusions. Issues that could be settled at the field level should be resolved locally, while matters requiring higher-level intervention should be referred to the State government without delay, he said. Observing that prolonged disputes had caused considerable hardship to farmers and landowners, he said he would personally monitor the joint survey exercise and periodically review its progress. ecee93d69cbdb6d7.title: One held in Keralam for securing job in panchayat with fake mark list
ecee93d69cbdb6d7.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - PALAKKAD Representational image. | Photo Credit: Getty Images A former Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) unit secretary was arrested for allegedly securing a contractual job at Puthukkode grama panchayat here by submitting a fake BCom mark list. The arrested person, K.V. Ganapathy, a native of Puthukkode Kizhakke Gramam, worked as an accountant-cum-IT assistant in the panchayat’s employment guarantee scheme section. The Vadakkenchery police arrested him in connection with the case on Monday. Mr. Ganapathy joined the panchayat on a contractual basis in July 2021, when the Left Democratic Front (LDF) was in power. He continued in the post until July 2026. He had submitted a BCom mark list purportedly issued by the University of Calicut as proof of his educational qualification. After the United Democratic Front (UDF) came to power in the last local body elections, the panchayat committee refused to extend his contract. Mr. Ganapathy then approached the High Court and obtained an order allowing him to continue in the post until September 2026. The alleged fraud came to light during the verification process for his reinstatement. The new panchayat administration became suspicious because Mr. Ganapathy had submitted only a mark list, rather than an original or provisional degree certificate, to prove his qualification. Growing suspicious, the panchayat authorities sent the mark list to the University of Calicut for verification. The university informed them that the document was fake and that Mr. Ganapathy had not passed the BCom degree. The National Service Scheme unit of SRIHER, in association with Ladies Circle India, Hair for Hope India, and the Adyar Cancer Institute, organised the event, aiming to collect hair from 800 donors in an attempt to set a world record. The donated hair will be used to make wigs for patients undergoing chemotherapy and other cancer treatments. SRIHER Chancellor V.R. Venkatachalam, trustee Samyuktha Venkatachalam, dean K. Balaji Singh, and representatives of the partner organisations were among those present. 53c883e3af2a990d.title: A.P. set for counting of votes in 92 ULBs on November 3
53c883e3af2a990d.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA The State Election Commission (SEC) has made arrangements for the counting of votes in 92 urban local bodies (13 Municipal Corporations and 79 Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats) from 8 a.m. on November 3 (Tuesday). SEC Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha, in a press release, said that counting was being conducted for a total of 3,186 wards, including 804 in Municipal Corporations (MCs) and 2,382 in Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats (M&NPs). The total number of counting centres is 138 — 22 in Municipal Corporations and the remaining in Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats. The counting process will be undertaken by 47,817 supervisors, assistants and staff (28,182 in MCs and 19,635 in M&NPs). A total of 1,372 CCTVs have been installed at strong rooms and counting centres (98 in MCs and 126 in M&NPs). Meanwhile, the SEC reported that the final voting percentage in the 92 urban local bodies that went to polls on November 1 stood at 62.16, with 60,22,411 of the 96,89,061 voters exercising their franchise. 1e06532f2305d2f6.title: TG-Redco for speeding up implementation of renewable energy schemes
1e06532f2305d2f6.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:33 pm IST - HYDERABAD Vice-chairman and MD of TG-Redco Jithesh V. Patil holding a virtual meeting with district managers from Hyderabad on Monday. | Photo Credit: Arrangement Vice-chairman and managing director of the Telangana State Renewable Energy Development Corporation (TG-Redco) Jithesh V. Patil has asked officials to accelerate the implementation of renewable energy schemes across the State and achieve planned targets within stipulated timelines. In a virtual meeting held on Monday with the district managers of the Redco, he stressed the need to identify field-level challenges and resolve them promptly through coordination with the departments concerned. He reviewed the Model Solar Village Programme, installation of rooftop solar power plants, solarisation of agricultural pump sets, PM-KUSUM scheme, energy conservation activities and development of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. He sought details from the officials on the work completed so far, current status and pending issues. Mr. Patil told the district managers to create awareness among eligible consumers about the benefits of rooftop solar under the Gruha Jyothi scheme. He called for district-level action plans to achieve the targets under agricultural pump set solarisation and the PM-KUSUM scheme. On pending approvals and inspections, he instructed officials to speed up the process of obtaining necessary approvals from various departments and complete pending inspections without delay. 6514719c07d112bf.title: Madurai medico detained in Russia for 10 days returns home after MP’s intervention
6514719c07d112bf.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - MADURAI A 21-year-old medical student from Madurai, who was trapped in a Russian detention facility for 10 days amid flight cancellations caused by ongoing war tensions, has returned safely to her hometown following the intervention of Madurai Member of Parliament Su. Venkatesan. Daisy Asha Moraes, a fourth-year student at the South Ural State Medical University in Russia, had planned to return to India on leave for medical reasons. With her visa set to expire on October 20, she booked a flight via Moscow and arrived at the airport on October 18. However, ongoing drone attacks linked to the Russia-Ukraine conflict forced the cancellation of domestic flights, grounding her scheduled journey. When alternative flights failed to materialise immediately, Russian authorities detained her under the classification of overstaying her expired visa, initiating detention proceedings on October 20. Although a local court granted a 10-day grace period, her family faced mounting anxiety that she could be held in detention for up to 90 days. After exhausting other avenues, the student’s father, Arul Moraes, sought the assistance of Mr. Venkatesan. Operating through parliamentary offices in Madurai and New Delhi, Mr. Venkatesan’s team coordinated directly with the External Affairs Minister, senior ministry officials, and the Indian Embassy in Russia. Compiling documentation regarding her medical condition and the war-related flight disruptions, officials presented the case to Russian authorities on October 27, establishing that the student bore no fault in the travel disruption. Originally informed that the student could not leave until November 15, the intervention successfully expedited her departure. Medical assistance and travel arrangements were secured, and Moraes boarded a flight to India on November 1, arriving safely in Madurai. e3eb50752922ec13.title: IRC summit to showcase Telangana’s growth, investment potential: Komatireddy
e3eb50752922ec13.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:36 pm IST - HYDERABAD Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy at a review meeting with senior officials at the Secretariat on Monday. The 85th Indian Roads Congress (IRC) summit, scheduled to be held in Hyderabad from November 19 to 22, should be transformed into a global platform to showcase Telangana’s development, culture and investment potential, Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy said. At a review meeting with senior officials at the Secretariat on Monday, the Minister directed them to make the event a precursor to the ‘Invest Telangana’ Global Summit scheduled to be held in December at Bharat Future City. He said the IRC summit should not remain confined to technical discussions on roads and infrastructure but should also help attract investments, industries and employment opportunities to the State. Officials should prepare a special action plan to connect with potential investors and encourage them to participate in the December global investment summit. Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy would jointly inaugurate the four-day summit at HITEX on November 19. Union Ministers, Ministers from various States, senior bureaucrats, international delegates and experts from the engineering and infrastructure sectors are expected to participate. Mr. Komatireddy, who reviewed the arrangements for nearly three-and-a-half hours, asked officials to establish a special ‘Telangana Pavilion’ at the venue to showcase the State’s history, culture, traditions, arts, tourism destinations and major development projects. Around 400 exhibition stalls would be set up as part of the event. He suggested organising cultural programmes every day, with Telangana artistes reflecting the State’s cultural heritage to the delegates. 3ce124ce86c16ef5.title: Chittoor, Annamayya districts brace for Cyclone Murasu
3ce124ce86c16ef5.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:34 pm IST - CHITTOOR/MADANAPALLE The officials are prepared for any emergency following a high alert for Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu across South Andhra Pradesh, projected to impact Chittoor and Annamayya districts over the next 48 hours. While the core system is projected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, the sprawling outer bands of the cyclone are expected to reach the interior Rayalaseema region. Officials have issued an orange alert for Chittoor district, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall through Monday and Tuesday. Neighbouring Annamayya district, which began the week under a yellow warning, is bracing for an escalation to an orange alert on Tuesday, with expectations of downpours in isolated areas. Officials said that the sudden rain could trigger severe waterlogging in low-lying tracts, spill over swollen streams, and trigger localised flooding in vulnerable rural pockets. Farmers across the Nagari, Chittoor, and Palamaner revenue divisions in Chittoor district and the eastern parts of Annamayya district initiated measures to protect standing paddy, horticultural orchards, and vegetable plots from gusty winds and floodwaters. Officials of the APSPDCL and civic officials were instructed to be prepared in the event of potential snapping of power lines and major roadblocks caused by uprooted trees. Annamayya district Collector Nishant Kumar said that with the crucial 48-hour window under way, the district machinery has swung into action at all vulnerable areas. “Revenue, police, municipal, and disaster response teams remain stationed on high alert in flood-prone zones,” he said. Chittoor Collector Sumit Kumar said that the district administration has issued strict advisories urging residents to stay alert to official weather bulletins. “Above all, the public should be cautious about fast-flowing streams and causeways,” he said. d60cb18c8a85a549.title: Sivaganga woman petitions Collector seeking rescue of husband missing in Dubai
d60cb18c8a85a549.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:40 pm IST - SIVAGANGA Family of the man who is missing in Dubai at Sivaganga Collectorate on Monday. | Photo Credit: BALACHANDAR L A woman submitted a petition at the Sivaganga District Collectorate demanding the rescue of her husband who allegedly went missing in Dubai. According to the petition, Periyasamy, 42, is a native of Ayyampatti near Sivaganga. His wife is Muneeswari, 35 and they have two female children. Two years ago, due to family poverty and after taking loans, Mr. Periyasamy went to Armenia for work. Meanwhile, on October 19, he came by flight from Armenia to Dubai in order to return to his hometown. After that, though he was supposed to come to India, suddenly his family was unable to contact him. Demanding the rescue of her missing husband, Ms. Muneeswari submitted a petition at the Sivaganga District Collectorate a week ago. As no action had been taken so far, she came again along with her children and relatives and submitted a petition at the District Collectorate. a14467189d646d17.title: Telangana Civil Supplies officials uncover rice sale violations, hoarding in Hyderabad
a14467189d646d17.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST - HYDERABAD Diversion of rice meant for Public Distribution System (PDS) was one of the violation detected by Telangana Civil Supplies teams during checks between October 29 and 31. The image is used for representative purposes only. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT Telangana Civil Supplies Department officials uncovered violations in sale of rice at a few outlets in Hyderabad and Rangareddy districts. The violations include weight manipulations by traders by affixing 26-kilogram labels onto bags having only 25 kilograms of rice , and exorbitant prices pasted over the rates printed by manufacturers. The department’s teams lodged complaints at Saroornagar, Jeedimetla, and Alwal police stations, based on which action was initiated, as per official information. This follows surprise checks by the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) along with the Legal Metrology Department across Hyderabad and Ranga Reddy districts between October 29 to 31. The other violations detected include diversion and hoarding of Public Distribution System (PDS) rice, traders operating without mandatory trade, GST, Labour, or FSSAI licenses. The teams have documented the offences on-site by taking videos and photos. The department stated that the vigilance will continue. The State government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) announced a ceiling on maximum retail price (MRP) on three varieties of fine rice in the urban limits , which are most consumed by people. As per the orders, price of a kg of BPT/KNM variety was fixed at ₹66; RNR/Telangana Sona at ₹74 and HMT/JSR variety at ₹79, in Hyderabad and Medchal. d4535bfeee0e14e6.title: Pawan Kalyan directs high alert as Cyclone Murasu nears Nellore coast
d4535bfeee0e14e6.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:38 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan | Photo Credit: File photo Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan has directed officials to remain on high alert as cyclone Murasu approaches the coast, even as the State is yet to recover from the damage caused by cyclone Arnab. At a review meeting with senior officials of the Panchayat Raj and Rural Development and Rural Water Supply Departments on Monday, Mr. Kalyan said the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had warned of extremely heavy rain in Nellore, Prakasam, Markapuram, Bapatla and Krishna districts. In view of the forecast of intense rainfall, he stressed the need to evacuate people living in low-lying areas to safer locations, ensure proper coordination among departments, minimise hardship and prevent loss of life. Officials informed the Deputy Chief Minister that the cyclone was initially forecast to cross the coast between Bapatla and Machilipatnam. However, it had changed course and was now expected to make landfall near Nellore. Heavy rain was already lashing Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla, Tirupati and Markapuram districts under the influence of the cyclone. Six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams had been kept on standby, officials said. They added that other necessary precautionary measures were being taken. 8d7756523fa00748.title: Residents seek closure of Tasmac outlet, illegal recreation club in Keela Arasadi panchayat
8d7756523fa00748.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:43 pm IST - THOOTHUKUDI: Residents of Thuppaspatti and Ayyanarpuram at the Collectorate in Thoothukudi on Monday. | Photo Credit: N. RAJESH Residents of Thuppaspatti and Ayyanarpuram in the district on Monday submitted a petition to the Collector, seeking closure of a newly opened Tasmac outlet and an ‘llegal’ recreation club nearby. The petition was submitted at the weekly grievance redressal meeting chaired by Collector Vishu Mahajan. In their petition, the villagers said the Tasmac outlet and the club in Thuppaspatti-Ayyanarpuram area under Keela Arasadi panchayat were causing several problems. Also, while staging continuous protests demanding the closure of both outlets, anti-social elements were issuing death threats to the protesters. The petitioners said that drunken people made it a regular practice to engage in quarrels in nearby thickets, break and throw liquor bottles and lie around in an intoxicated state. This raised serious safety concerns among women, who left for work at the salt pans early in the morning, and school students passing through the area. The residents urged the authorities to permanently shut down the Tasmac outlet and the recreation club, which were causing inconvenience to the public, and take stringent action against those threatening and intimidating the villagers. In a separate petition, Sudalai of Meelavittan and other villagers said that 70 goats died after allegedly consuming wastewater discharged from a fertilizer godown owned by a private company at Veeranayakkanthattu near Thoothukudi. The animals had been grazing in the area. They sought criminal action against the godown management and adequate compensation for the loss of goats. 668d07ff7e0eaaea.title: Ranji Trophy: Urvil and Vishal boost Gujarat
668d07ff7e0eaaea.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - Ahmedabad Opener Aarya hit six fours and three maximums in his 95. | Photo Credit: VIJAY SONEJI A frustratingly familiar script unfolded again for Kerala at the Narendra Modi stadium here on Monday. For the third time this season, Kerala allowed the opposition’s lower-order to fight back and wrest away the hard-earned advantage. An unbeaten, counterattacking 111-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Urvil Patel (63 batting, 67b, 7x4, 1x6) and Vishal Jayswal (50 batting, 83b, 3x4, 2x6) was the latest to hurt Kerala as Gujarat ended the opening day of the Ranji Trophy Elite Group C match at 300 for five. Soon after tea, Kerala had Gujarat in a spot of bother at 189 for five when Jaymeet Patel (one) was stumped by Mohammed Azharuddeen off Aditya Sarvate. But the visiting side let Gujarat off the hook when it failed to grab the chances and wilted under the calculated assault by Urvil and Vishal. Rohan Kunnummal showed poor judgement while running back and failed to reach a skier from Vishal off Vaisakh Chandran when the batter was on 33. Azharuddeen fumbled when Urvil, on 32, stepped out to attack Sarvate. Urvil and Vishal capitalised on these errors to take their side to a position of strength in the final session. Earlier, Kerala had crawled back into the contest in the post-lunch session, picking up four wickets to reduce the host to 182 for four. The strikes included that of top-scorer Aarya Desai (95, 132b, 6x4, 3x6), who in a hurry to reach his hundred top-edged a wild slog and was caught by Vishnu Vinod off Vaisakh. In the morning, openers Aarya and Abhishek Desai played fluently against the Kerala bowlers who found little help from the track. However, a better disciplined show with the ball in the second session choked the flow runs which forced the Gujarat batters to take the risks, which ultimately led to their downfall. The scores: Gujarat — 1st innings: Abhishek Desai c Rohan b Nidheesh 42, Aarya Desai c Vi
