8cbf0812f433ba6c.title: Namakkal farmers oppose the proposed Sankari-Vellakoil NH project
8cbf0812f433ba6c.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:52 pm IST - Namakkal The farmers in Namakkal have opposed upgrading the two-lane highway at Padaiveedu to a four-lane road under the proposed Sankari–Vellakoil NH 381A project. | Photo Credit: LAKSHMI NARAYANAN E Farmers in Namakkal district have opposed the proposed Sankari-Vellakoil national highway project 381A and want it implemented on alternate routes. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has proposed a 70-km inter-corridor highway connecting NH 81 in Tiruppur district to NH 544 near Sankari in Salem district. The project cost is estimated at ₹ 2,000 crore and the four-way lane is expected to pass through about 19 km in Namakkal district. Farmers have raised opposition, stating that the project would severely affect farmlands, schools, spinning mills, and houses. P. Perumal, general secretary of the Tamil Nadu Vivasayigal Sangam, said the project starts at Padaiveedu town panchayat in Namakkal district and passes through Sowdapuram, Patharai, Pallipalayam Agraharam, Elanthakuttai, Kadachanallur, and Pappampalayam panchayats before entering Erode district. The project envisions laying 150-ft road for 19 km in Namakkal district. This would affect around 200 acres of farmland, schools at Padaiveedu, Uppupalayam, spinning mills, and over 100 houses. Likewise, 18 village roads will have to be destroyed for the project. Two weeks ago, farmers from seven villages submitted a petition against the project at the divisional-level farmers’ grievances meet at the Pallipalayam panchayat union office. Now, farmers from Erode and Tiruppur districts are also in talks to organise protests jointly against the proposed project, Mr. Perumal added. Stating that the project would be mostly beneficial for industries and corporates, Mr. Perumal said the proposed road would facilitate easy movement of containers to Thoothukudi through Dharapuram and Madurai. 783e08fb334bc57d.title: PWD employees stage black badge protest over delayed October salary
783e08fb334bc57d.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:52 pm IST - MADURAI Employees of the Tamil Nadu Government Public Works Department Accounts and Administrative Staff Association staged a State-wide protest on Monday, wearing black badges to condemn the non-disbursement of October salary to over a thousand employees across the Public Works Department (PWD) and the Water Resources Department. The salary delay, affecting personnel from chief engineers down to office assistants, has severely impacted livelihoods as the Deepavali festival approaches, said Abdul Najimudeen, general secretary of the association. Association representatives revealed that the delay stemmed from files pending in the Finance Department and the salary item being disabled in the IFHRMS portal, leaving employees unable to receive timely pay even with government intervention. They noted that pay authorisation bottlenecks—with delays recurring every three to six months—and unapproved temporary posts have created major administrative hurdles, echoing a similar crisis last July when salaries were delayed past the 15th of the month. The association has put forward an eight-point charter of demands, urging the State government to disburse salaries immediately on a war footing and find a permanent solution to departmental issues rather than handling staff livelihoods casually. Key demands include issuing requested transfers pending for the last five months, promoting over 450 junior assistants and typists, regularising temporary workers who have served for over a decade, revoking Government Order No. 69, converting divisional accountant posts into a State service, and filling all vacant positions. Warning that this year’s festival risks becoming a ‘black Deepavali’ for PWD staff, the union announced escalated protests if their grievances are ignored. A zonal-level dharna is scheduled for November 17, followed by a massive hunger strike at the Chennai PWD campus on December 8. Published - November 02, 2026 07:23 pm IST Te

e32d6b6853bbb527.title: Facial recognition attendance system introduced as pilot project in SCCL’s Kothagudem Area
e32d6b6853bbb527.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - BHADRADRI KOTHAGUDEM A facial recognition-based attendance system was introduced on a trial basis in the Kothagudem Area of the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) on Monday. The initiative is part of the SCCL’s efforts to adopt technology in its employee attendance system to enhance transparency. Biometric attendance systems are already in use at some General Managers’ offices in SCCL. However, this is the first time the system is being implemented across the coal mines and departments of an entire area. The initiative is aimed at promoting discipline and punctuality among employees and is expected to improve transparency and productivity, according to an SCCL press release. SCCL has around 40,000 employees, of whom approximately 1,600 work in the Kothagudem Area. The trial run began in the Kothagudem Area as a pilot project on Monday. The system is expected to be extended to mines and departments in other areas in a phased manner. 8568b14a98d223eb.title: Karnataka deploys 500 linemen, equipment to restore power supply in cyclone-hit Andhra Pradesh
8568b14a98d223eb.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:49 pm IST - Bengaluru The State government is providing contingency funds to meet travel, accommodation and other emergency expenses of the deployed personnel. | Photo Credit: File Photo Karnataka has deployed 500 trained power utility workers and specialised equipment to Andhra Pradesh to help restore electricity infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab. The deployment follows a request from the Andhra Pradesh government for manpower and equipment to carry out restoration work in cyclone-affected areas. The Karnataka government has mobilised the teams under the supervision of Energy Minister K.J. George as part of inter-State cooperation. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke to his Andhra Pradesh counterpart N. Chandrababu Naidu over the phone and assured him of Karnataka’s support. “Electricity is an essential service, and restoring it immediately is necessary for the well-being of people affected by the disaster. Karnataka stands firmly with the people of Andhra Pradesh during this difficult time,” the Chief Minister said. Mr. George said Karnataka’s teams would work closely with Andhra Pradesh officials to restore power supply at the earliest through field-level coordination and the deployment of specialised equipment. The State has sent 500 trained linemen, 15 Palfinger trucks equipped with cranes and earth augers, and 25 tractor-mounted drilling machines. The teams were mobilised on an emergency basis and left for Andhra Pradesh on Monday afternoon, reaching the State by midnight. For effective deployment and coordination, each electricity supply company (ESCOM) has appointed a single-point contact officer to liaise with the concerned Andhra Pradesh officials. The linemen have been divided into teams of 10, each led by a junior or assistant engineer. 87ebc376380a8fdf.title: Tight security arrangements for ULB vote counting in Chittoor, Annamayya, Sri Sathya Sai districts
87ebc376380a8fdf.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:36 pm IST - CHITTOOR Elaborate arrangements are in place for counting votes in the urban local body elections across Chittoor, Annamayya, and Sri Sathya Sai districts on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), with officials intensifying security to ensure a tension-free and transparent declaration of results. Annamayya district Collector Nishant Kumar inspected the strong rooms and counting centres in Madanapalle, while Chittoor Collector Sumit Kumar reviewed the arrangements in Chittoor on Monday (November 2). In Sri Sathya Sai district, SP S. Satish Kumar inspected the strong rooms in Dharmavaram and reviewed security arrangements. “Heavy police bandobast has been deployed at counting centres, with special focus on preventing unauthorised entry, maintaining law and order and avoiding clashes between political groups. Strong rooms housing ballot boxes are under round-the-clock security,” said Sumit Kumar. “CCTV surveillance and strict entry regulations will be enforced at counting venues. Candidates and their authorised counting agents only will be allowed inside after verification,” Sri Sathya Sai district Collector A. Shyam Prasad said. e11034b468c1206a.title: Leaders campaign for parishad polls amid heavy rain in Nellore
e11034b468c1206a.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - NELLORE Amidst heavy rainfall and cyclone warnings in SPSR Nellore district, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leaders campaigned for MPTC (Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies) and ZPTC (Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies) elections. Minister of Endowments Anam Ramanarayana Reddy campaigned in Sangam mandal, which falls under his Atmakur constituency. He toured various villages with the alliance candidates and addressed the public. While it was raining heavily, MLA Kotamreddy Sridhar Reddy, along with his younger daughter Sai Vaishnavi, extensively campaigned for the TDP candidates in South Mopur, Mogallapalem, and Kotha Vellanki villages in his Nellore Rural constituency. Similarly, the YSRCP leaders also campaigned for their candidates. Despite the rain, the party workers continued campaigning in Jarugumalli village, which falls under Kothapalem MPTC segment in Kota mandal. Under the guidance of YSRCP leader Nedurumalli Harish Chandra Reddy, the party cadre conducted an extensive campaign throughout the village for MPTC candidate Gali Praveenamma. All six fishermen aboard the vessel were unharmed as the boat grounded near the shoreline. According to the fisheries officials and coastal police, the fishing boat, bearing registration number IND.AP.V5.MM.255 and owned by Korangi Narsinga Rao, had set out on a routine fishing expedition off the Visakhapatnam coast a few days ago. Trouble began at mid-sea when the vessel’s engine developed a technical snag and subsequently ran out of fuel. The crew dropped anchor in an attempt to stabilise the drifting vessel. However, strong tidal surges and turbulent waves caused by the adverse weather conditions along the coast caused the anchor line to snap. Unable to manoeuver the vessel in the swelling waters, the boat along with the crew was carried westward by high-energy waves before the boat ran aground near Rushikonda beach. Recounting the incident one of the crew members said: “We lost power after running out of fuel, and before we could secure the boat, the anchor broke under heavy wave pressure. Fortunately, the ocean tides pushed us towards the shore rather than towards the deep sea.” Beach lifeguards, local fishermen, and Coastal Security Police quickly rushed to the spot on seeing the grounded vessel. Officials confirmed that all six crew members managed to disembark safely without sustaining injuries. Marine police authorities and fisheries department staff arrived at Rushikonda to inspect the vessel for structural damage and made arrangements to tow it once sea conditions improve. 90c3264d8212701c.title: All Souls Day observed in Madurai
90c3264d8212701c.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:45 pm IST - MADURAI Family members on All Souls Day performing rituals at a cemetery in Madurai on Monday. | Photo Credit: G. MOORTHY Hundreds of Catholic families gathered at various city cemeteries on Monday to offer prayers for departed souls in observance of All Souls Day. The solemn occasion is observed with the belief that prayers assist souls in purgatory on their path to Heaven. As a gesture of remembrance, believers cleaned burial sites before lighting candles and placing flowers and wreaths upon the graves of their loved ones. Special masses were also held across local churches. Devotional gatherings and prayers took place at cemeteries in Mahaboobpalayam, Kalavasal, Karpaga Nagar, Thuvariman, and surrounding areas. 00d12a7aa8bf2173.title: Tasmac workers shut shops in Namakkal, Salem
00d12a7aa8bf2173.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:49 pm IST - Salem A total of 155 Tasmac outlets in Namakkal and many outlets in Salem downed shutters on Monday, in protest against the implementation of new Environmental and Social Welfare Cess. Meanwhile, on Sunday evening, three customers went to an outlet at Pillur near Paramathi Velur, returned the empty liquor bottles and demanded money. Due to server issues, the bottles could not be scanned and it resulted in a quarrel between the customers and the salesman, Purusothaman (46). During the quarrel, the three men hit Purusothaman with a bottle and he sustained injuries. He was admitted to Paramathi Velur Government Hospital. Similarly, customers attacked another salesman, Marimuthu, at Nallar outlet and damaged his two-wheeler. In Salem district, acting on complaints that Tasmac workers were collecting excess money for bottles, the officials checked an outlet at Venkatappa Chetty Street at Pal Market on Sunday evening. They found the allegations to be true. Following this, the outlet salesmen Senthil, Pachaperumal, and supervisor Govindan were placed under suspension. c051082588990188.title: Villagers stage protest at Collectorate demanding mobile ration shop
c051082588990188.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST - RAMANATHAPURAM Keelakarai villagers staged a demonstration outside the Ramanathapuram Collectorate demanding the setting up of a mobile ration shop. The Collector assured that action will be taken. More than a hundred villagers and members of the women’s self-help group from Velanoor (South) village in Keelakarai taluk, Ramanathapuram district, besieged the Collectorate, demanding the establishment of a mobile ration shop in their village. They then stated that they intended to submit their family cards along with a petition to Collector M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran at the public grievance redressal meeting. After the Collector assured them that appropriate action would be taken, the villagers returned with their family cards. The villagers stated, “There are 210 family cards in our village. We all purchase essential goods from the ration shop operating in Velanoor North Street, which is located one km away. As Scheduled Caste community people, we face various hardships when we go there to buy goods from a ration shop located in an area where people of another community reside. So, we have submitted petitions multiple times to the District Supply Officer to set up a mobile ration shop in our village once a month. On July 7th, we staged a siege protest at the Keelakarai Tahsildar’s office. During the talks held under the chairmanship of the Tahsildar that day, an assurance was given to set up a mobile ration shop. However, no ration shop has been set up to date. Hence, we came to surrender our family cards to the District Collector. The Collector has assured us that action will be taken.” Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 998ff12a26ed57ad.title: Three rebel AAP MLAs from Punjab join BJP ahead of Assembly polls
998ff12a26ed57ad.summary: In a setback to the Aam Aadmi Party ahead of the Punjab assembly polls, three of its leaders from the state, including Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh and two other legislators, joined the BJP on Monday. Earlier in the day, suspended AAP MLA and former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh said he resigned as a legislator of the Punjab Vidhan Sabha. In a post on Facebook, Singh -- the MLA from Amritsar North seat -- said he has sent his resignation to Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan. Singh, along with Punjab MLAs Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, joined the BJP in the presence of senior leaders at its headquarters here. His resignation from the Punjab Assembly came on the heels of two other AAP legislators -- Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour in Patiala district -- resigning from the party on Sunday.

af8f3d0c3943d793.title: Jagan accuses SEC of complicity in civic poll malpractices, says YSRCP will go to court
af8f3d0c3943d793.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:32 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy staging a protest outside the office of the Returning Officer in Pulivendula on Sunday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has accused the State Election Commission (SEC) of being complicit in the electoral malpractices that took place during the urban local body elections on November 1. Instead of protecting democracy, the SEC acted as per the whims of the coalition government, he said. In an X post on Monday, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said the shocking incidents during the municipal elections, particularly those in Pulivendula, exposed how the SEC stood firmly behind the malpractices. The State Election Commission (SEC), which is meant to protect democracy, has become subservient to @ncbn. The shocking incidents during yesterday's municipal polling across the state, including in Pulivendula, show how the SEC is enabling election irregularities. Yesterday in Pulivendula, YSRCP agents were kept out of 70 of the 80 polling booths. TDP goons brought in from other areas went on a rampage with the support of election officials and the police. They attacked our party agents to stop them from entering polling booths. In some places, they dragged our agents out of the polling stations. These incidents took place with the police's support. Voter slips were snatched from people, polling booths were captured, and votes were rigged and cast repeatedly. The video evidence of these incidents is clear. Agents from all 70 booths came to me personally, showed their agent forms to the officials, lodged complaints and protested. The entire state witnessed what happened. Yet the SEC's response was shocking. Irregularities took place in 70 of the 80 booths, and our agents were attacked and forced out. In these circumstances, how was it fair for the SEC to order repolling in only four booths and then wash its hand

35d271bddf5e0566.title: Cyclone Murasu: List of flights cancelled to and from Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada
35d271bddf5e0566.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:16 pm IST Representational Image | Photo Credit: Velankanni Raj Cyclone Murasu, which has intensified into a ‘Severe Cyclonic Storm’ over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal, has led to flight cancellations on November 2, 2026, owing to adverse weather conditions. Flight services to and from Chennai, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam have been impacted. Chennai International Airport, in a post on social media platform X, said eleven flights have been cancelled to and from Chennai owing to the Cyclone. IndiGo has also confirmed in a post on X that “flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted.” Cancelled departures from Chennai #FlightUpdate | In view of the adverse weather conditions due to #CycloneMurasu, the following flights have been cancelled. Passengers are requested to contact the concerned airline for further information and assistance. #ChennaiAirport #Cyclone #Murasu #MurasuCyclone #CycloneUpdate #CycloneMurasuUpdate #FlightCancellations #Chennai #Airport #AAIAirports @MoCA_GoI | @AAI_Official | @IndiGo6E | @Pib_MoCA | @PIBChennai Also Read: Cyclone Murasu: 12 flight services cancelled at Vijayawada; Visakhapatnam flights hit IndiGo, in its X post, has said that “We are notifying affected customers on the mobile number provided at the time of booking. Customers are advised to check their flight status before proceeding to the airport.We remain in close coordination with the relevant authorities and continue to closely monitor the situation. The safety and well-being of our customers and crew remain our highest priority.” Chennai Airport has requested passengers to contact the airline for more information and assistance. Travel Advisory Due to adverse weather conditions associated with Tropical Cyclone Murasu, flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted. We are notifying affected customers on the mobile number provided at the time of booking. Customers

e562ac62f9dfa78b.title: AMU wants women on campus, not at the ballot box
e562ac62f9dfa78b.summary: Around 4,000 women students at AMU’s Women’s College have been denied voting rights in the Aligarh Muslim University Students’ Union (AMUSU) elections, raising concerns over gender discrimination and unequal representation. 9ef1ec07f605ba03.title: Delhi traders claim ₹10,000-₹11,000 crore loss from INDIA bloc's rally
9ef1ec07f605ba03.summary: Delhi's trading sector suffered an estimated loss of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, Chamber of Trade & Industry (CTI) Chairman Brijesh Goyal claimed on Sunday.Goyal said around 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity of the rally venue were affected, with approximately 2.5 lakh shops remaining closed out of the nearly three lakh shops in these markets.Speaking about the impact on traders, Goyal said the closures were largely due to panic over the expected arrival of a large number of people and vehicles for the rally."Due to the rally held at Ramlila Maidan today, about 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity were affected. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groups-comprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)-about 80% of these shops-roughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000-remained closed today," .

4576f06676c06a16.title: Suspended Punjab AAP leader Kunwar Vijay Pratap quits as MLA ahead of polls
4576f06676c06a16.summary: Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh announced his resignation, citing a push for clean politics and transparent administration | File Image: X@Kvijaypratap In a major political development ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh announced his resignation from the Punjab Legislative Assembly on Monday. Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh was suspended from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on June 29, 2025. In a X post addressed to the people of Amritsar, Singh said he would remain indebted to them "until my last breath" for their love and respect. He called for a collective effort to rise above "the politics of lanes and ribbon-cutting" and to bring Punjab, which he described as "trapped by drugs, extortion, gangsterism and corruption", back to being a progressive state. ਬਹੁਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਿਕਾਰਯੋਗ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਦੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਭੈਣ-ਭਰਾਵੋਂ, ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੀ ਮੈਂਬਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਤੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਇਸਤੀਫ਼ਾ ਦੇ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ। ਮੈਂ ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮਿਲੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਆਖ਼ਿਰੀ ਸਾਹ ਤੱਕ ਰਿਣੀ ਰਹਾਂਗਾ। >ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਸਹਿਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਦੇ ਆਸ਼ੀਰਵਾਦ ਨਾਲ ਗਲੀ-ਨਾਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਿਬਨ-ਕਟਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਪਰ ਉੱਠ ਕੇ ਨਸ਼ਾ, ਫਿਰੌਤੀ, ਗੈਂਗਸਟਰਵਾਦ ਅਤੇ ਭ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟਾਚਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਜਕੜੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਨੂੰ ਮੁੜ ਉੱਨਤਸ਼ੀਲ ਅਤੇ ਮੋਹਰੀ ਸੂਬਾ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਅਸੀਂ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਨੇ ਮਿਲ਼ ਕੇ ਇਕਜੁਟ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਸ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੈ। >ਵੈਸੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਸਾਰੇ ਜਾਣਦੇ ਹੋ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਬਤੌਰ ਵਿਧਾਇਕ ਆਪਣਾ 90 ਪਰਸੈਂਟ ਟਾਰਗੇਟ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਹੈ; ਜੋ ਕੰਮ ਇੱਕ ਵਿਧਾਇਕ ਨੇ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕੌਂਸਲਰ, ਮੇਅਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਂਸਦ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਇਸਤੋਂ ਇਲਾਵਾ ਹਨ। >ਮੈਂ ਇਲਾਕਾ ਵਾਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਕਰਾਏ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਵੇਰਵਾ ਵੀ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਅਖ਼ਬਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਫੇਸਬੁੱਕ ਪੇਜ ਤੇ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਹੈ। >ਮੇਰੀ ਸੱਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੀ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਮਾਈ-ਬਾਪ ਕਲਚਰ ਨੂੰ ਖਤਮ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਜਨਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣਾ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਣਾ-ਸਰੋਤ ਸਮਝ ਕੇ ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ। >ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੈਂ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਅੰਬਰਸਰੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਆਵਾਜ ਬੁਲੰਦ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਸੀਵਰੇਜ ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਸਰਕਟ ਹਾਊਸ, ਕੰਪਨੀ ਬਾਗ, ਗੰਦਾ ਨਾਲਾ, ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ, ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਕਾਲਜ, ਸਰੂਪ ਰਾਣੀ ਕਾਲਜ ਅਤੇ ਬਰਗਾੜੀ ਬੇਅਦਬੀ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਬੇਬਾਕੀ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖੇ। ਇਹ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਵਾਰ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਿ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਹੱਲਾ ਦਾ ਨਾਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਇਲਾਕੇ ਵਾਰ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਵਲੋਂ ਉਠਾਏ ਗਏ। >ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਕੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਦੀ ਸਟ੍

836fbbd76fe0e28f.title: Andhra goes ahead with Kotia local body polls despite Odisha’s plea in Supreme Court
836fbbd76fe0e28f.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:39 pm IST - PARVATIPURAM A resident of Madkar village in the Kotia gram panchayat shows voter cards issued by both the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha governments. Andhra Pradesh is going ahead with local body polls in the disputed villages on November 5. File | Photo Credit: Biswaranjan Rout The Andhra Pradesh government and the State Election Commission are making all arrangements to conduct local body elections in the Kotia group of villages on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, despite strong objections from Odisha. The neighbouring State has approached the Supreme Court to stop the election process in the disputed region. Both the States have been at odds over the jurisdiction of the Kotia group of villages for about seven decades. Both have also been holding local body elections there for many decades. Odisha has objected before: it filed contempt petitions when Andhra Pradesh held polls in the villages in 2021. This time, it filed a fresh contempt petition last month, alleging that the poll notification violates the Supreme Court’s 2006 order directing both States to maintain the status quo. The villages are located 35 km from Salur town of Parvathipuram Manyam district. Since the court has not passed any order on Odisha’s petition, the Parvathipuram Manyam district administration is making all arrangements to hold elections in places like Ganjai Bhadra, Pagalu Chennuru, Pattu Chennuru, Kurukutti, Sarika, Kotia and other villages on November 5, 2026. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which won the Salur Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency and all four Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies in 2021, is keen to win them again with its spirited campaign in all Kotia villages. 7ac472482663b212.title: Cyclone Murasu: Red alert in two Telangana districts, orange in three more on November 3
7ac472482663b212.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:21 pm IST - HYDERABAD Nagarkurnool and Nalgonda districts in Telangana were placed under red alert on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT With Cyclone Murasu likely to make landfall at Andhra Pradesh coast between evening of Monday (November 2, 2026) and early morning of Tuesday (November 3, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for two Telangana districts and an orange alert in three districts for Tuesday (November 3, 2026). According to the IMDs latest bulletin, a red alert — meaning, heavy to very heavy rain with isolated extremely heavy rainfall — was issued for Nalgonda and Nagarkurnool districts. An orange alert — meaning heavy to very heavy rainfall — was issued for Suryapet, Mahabubnagar and Wanaparthy districts. Additionally, a yellow alert — indicating heavy rainfall with thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds — was issued for Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaon, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Rangareddy, Vikarabad, Narayanpet and Jogulamba Gadwal districts. Hyderabad city for the next 24 hours will see a generally cloudy sky. “Moderate to heavy rain or thundershowers by lightning accompanied with gusty winds are very likely to occur in parts of the city towards evening or night. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be 33 C and 23 C respectively’,” as per the bulletin. f0f2e9e125ddf598.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
f0f2e9e125ddf598.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:42 pm IST For decades, three computer scientists built their careers around an idea about the limits of what computers can do. Artificial intelligence may now have shown it to be wrong: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH). The hypothesis holds that some problems are so hard that computers can solve them only by trying nearly every possible answer. Hundreds of studies in computer science and biology rely on it. The claim is the latest in a string of AI results that have shaken academia, setting off soul-searching, most notably among mathematicians, over the value of human expertise and the future of their profession. Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi of the University of California San Diego first proposed the hypothesis around 25 years ago. Ryan Williams of MIT, a leading researcher in the field, had long publicly doubted it. The three are now helping organise an independent review of the claims from the AI companies. Q: How did you feel when you learned that a machine may have overturned this hypothesis? Ryan Williams: I did not fully believe the hypothesis, and I’m on the record as a prominent sceptic. So I felt vindicated. Russell Impagliazzo: I’m afraid I am less cheerful about this than the others. I would have much preferred it to be discovered by a human who could explain their thought process. And I’d like to have shaken the (actual) hand of the person who disproved ETH. Q: What is left for human researchers facing the machine? What would you tell a student? Paturi: These breakthroughs extend the frontier of research, but I believe shaping that frontier and moving it forward remain within human capacity and creativity. I would encourage young students to join. They should learn to use these tools while developing their own judgment. 37099eecc593fabd.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:49 pm IST - New Delhi Image used for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto Activity in the manufacturing sector slowed in October 2026 compared to its level in September, according to a private sector survey. However, new orders rose strongly, driven by orders from abroad rising to their highest level in six months, it said. The private sector HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) fell to 54.7 in October 2026 as compared to 55.1 in September. A reading over 50 denotes expansion, while one below 50 shows contraction in activity. Also Read: Why manufacturing has lagged in India “India’s manufacturing PMI softened to 54.7 in October from 55.1 in the previous month, but remained firmly in expansionary territory and above its long-run average,” Pranjul Bhandari, Chief India Economist at HSBC, said. “Strong international demand pushed growth of new export orders to a six-month high, supporting a robust rise in output.” The report went on to say that growth eased only marginally from September’s seven-month high and remained strong by historical standards. The respondents said that favourable demand trends, new client wins, and successful marketing campaigns were behind the growth in October. “Overseas markets contributed to the upturn, as new export orders increased at the fastest rate in six months,” the report said. “Companies reported gains from a broad range of destinations, including Bangladesh, Canada, Indonesia, Nepal, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, the U.K., U.S. and the UAE.” Even as demand increased, the survey respondents said that cost pressures eased in October. “Although survey members reported higher prices for several materials and energy, the overall rate of input cost inflation retreated to its lowest since February,” the report said. 97c137308f83a282.title: Vasan urges Centre to secure release of T.N. fishermen detained by Sri Lankan Navy
97c137308f83a282.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 04:35 pm IST - CHENNAI G.K. Vasan. File | Photo Credit: M. Govarthan Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Monday (November 2, 2026) urged the Central government to take immediate steps to secure the release of seven Tamil Nadu fishermen recently detained by the Sri Lankan Navy . In a statement, the former Union Minister said the fishermen, who had ventured into the sea for fishing, were arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy and their boats confiscated on Sunday (November 1) morning. He expressed concern over the repeated incidents of arrests, harassment and attacks against Tamil Nadu fishermen by the Sri Lankan authorities. Mr. Vasan called upon the Central government to intervene diplomatically with Sri Lanka, ensure the immediate release of the detained fishermen and secure the return of their boats. c987aed75b01f9ef.title: 37% of pre-SIR Form-6 applications rejected due to absence of declaration form
c987aed75b01f9ef.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:35 pm IST - HYDERABAD A large number of applications for fresh voter registration, submitted through Form-6 before the start of Special Intensive Revision, got rejected because they were not accompanied by a declaration form mandated as a prerequisite for enrolment. The image is used for representative purposes only. Shifting goal posts by the Election Commission of India (ECI) with regard to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the Electoral Rolls have resulted in rejection of tens of thousands of application forms for new voter enrolments in Telangana. A large number of applications for fresh voter registration, submitted through Form-6 before the start of the SIR process, got rejected because they were not accompanied by a declaration form mandated as a prerequisite for enrolment. The declaration form, which was an attachment to the Form-6 exclusively for the SIR process, sought details of the voter or the voter’s parents/relatives from 2002 SIR. In the absence of such details, the applicants were required to submit any of the listed 12 documents as proof of their citizenship. The ECI recently announced that the declaration was not required for submission of Form-6 in States where SIR is not on . It was too late for Telangana, where a large number of voters who had submitted Form-6 before the start of SIR were rejected for lack of the declaration form. As per data obtained from the office of the Telangana Chief Electoral Officer, a total of 5,20,331 applications were received for new enrolments during the pre-SIR period between January 1, 2026 and June 14, 2026. They were not accompanied by the declaration form which was made mandatory only during the SIR process. As per the Registration of Electors Rules, 196, such claims should be exhibited at the office of the Electoral Registration Officer, and disposed of in a week’s time. This was not adhered to, and the forms submitted up to June 14, 2026 are now being processed al

fa68ea5f3342fcdf.title: Cyclone Murasu: Seven fishermen caught in rough seas rescued in Nellore
fa68ea5f3342fcdf.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:10 pm IST - Nellore Fisheries Department officials rescue seven fishermen whose boat was caught in rough seas near Juvvaladinne village in SPSR Nellore district on Monday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement SPSR Nellore district officials have rescued seven fishermen who ventured into the sea near Juvvaladinne village in Kavali constituency on Monday (November 2, 2026) morning. They were brought safely to shore after their boat’s engine broke down at sea. Fishermen had been advised not to venture into the sea in view of Cyclone Murasu. Speaking to the media, District Collector Himanshu Shukla said, “Seven fishermen who had set out for a fishing trip from Juvvaladinne Fishing Harbour noticed changes in the sea conditions while off the coast of Nellore and attempted to return to the harbour. However, their boat’s engine broke down en route, leaving them stranded at sea. Surveillance personnel on duty at the harbour spotted this and immediately alerted the relevant authorities.” Officials and local fishermen pull a boat ashore at Patakadapalem in SPSR Nellore district on Monday after its engine failed in seas made rough by Cyclone Murasu. All seven fishermen on board were rescued. Initially, reaching the boat proved difficult because of the high waves. Ultimately, they managed to bring the boat to the shore at Patakadapalem and ensured that all fishermen were safe. 494bf2da99576b8e.title: Cyclone Murasu: CM directs officials to brace for flood into Bapatla district
494bf2da99576b8e.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:47 pm IST - BAPATLA Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviews preparations for Cyclone Murasu with district officials through a video conference on Monday. Bapatla district is likely to bear the brunt of the storm. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to take all precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property in Bapatla district in view of Cyclone Murasu , which has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. He reviewed the preparedness of district administrations through a video conference on Monday (November 2, 2026), attended by Bapatla Collector Vinod Kumar V. The Chief Minister warned that Bapatla was likely to bear the brunt of the cyclone, since heavy inflows of floodwater were expected through irrigation canals from upstream districts, including Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Markapuram. He asked officials to inspect canal bunds, remain alert for four days of heavy inflows, evacuate people from low-lying areas and establish rehabilitation centres. He also said a special officer would be appointed for Bapatla district. In a review meeting on cyclone preparedness, Mr. Naidu said the District Collectors should be alert to meet any contingency keeping in view the likelihood of heavy rains and gales. 5daf79f1d4fa17b2.title: EVMs vs paper ballots: What makes MLC polls different? | Explained
5daf79f1d4fa17b2.summary: Why are paper ballots still used in MLC elections when India uses Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for Lok Sabha and Assembly polls? The BJP-led NDA’s victory in the recent Legislative Council elections has renewed the political debate over EVMs and paper ballots. But MLC polls follow a different voting system, where voters rank candidates in order of preference. We explain how the single transferable vote system works, why existing EVMs cannot be used for these elections, and which other elections in India still rely on paper ballots.

78d84b6820602584.title: Cyclone Murasu strengthens, heavy rain alerts issued across southern States
78d84b6820602584.summary: Cyclone Murasu has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal and is expected to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole on November 3. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), wind speeds could reach 100–110 kmph, gusting up to 120 kmph. Schools and colleges have been closed in Chennai and Tiruvallur, while heavy rain alerts have been issued in parts of Telangana. The storm comes just days after Cyclone Arnab battered parts of the eastern coast, leaving six dead in Odisha.

08c48fb1267ea4bf.title: New logo, new inaugural venue: Stage set for iconic Kolkata International Film Festival
08c48fb1267ea4bf.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:00 pm IST - Kolkata New logo of 32nd Kolkata Internation Film Festival was designed by Satyajit Ray’s son filmmaker Sandip Ray, and was unveiled on November 1, 2026. With a new logo in black and saffron and a new venue at Victoria Memorial for the inaugural ceremony, the 32 nd Kolkata International Film Festival (KIFF) is all set to lay the carpet for cine-lovers from across the world from December 16 to December 23 this year. The new logo, which was unveiled on Sunday (November 1, 2026) at Nandan by the festival authority, was redesigned by the son of Satyajit Ray, filmmaker Sandip Ray. The latest logo replaces the previous blue-and-white artwork, which was launched in 2015. The first KIFF under the new Bharatiya Janata Party government in West Bengal is witnessing a complete overhaul, with superstar Tollywood Prosenjit Chatterjee as the KIFF chairperson and veteran actor Mithun Chakraborty as the Chief Advisor. Some other prominent faces of the Bengal film industry, including actor Jeet, Hiran Chatterjee, actor-cum-politician Rudranil Ghosh, and Nandan CEO and KIFF Director Sharmistha Banerjee, were also present at Sunday’s (November 1) event. Addressing the event, Mr. Chatterjee said that the inaugural ceremony of the festival will also take place at Victoria Memorial for the first time. The venues that have earlier been used by the previous Trinamool Congress government since 2011 include Netaji Indoor Stadium and Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium while the festival was also organised at Nandan during the COVID-19 pandemic. Nandan was also the traditional venue for the festival in its initial years. According to the officials, superstars Rajinikanth, Akshay Kumar, and Prabhas may make their maiden appearances at KIFF this year, along with a star-studded lineup from the film industries across the country. The guest list for the inaugural ceremony of the festival may also include Sanjay Dutt, Paresh Rawal, Anupam Kher, Johnny Lever, Kangana Ra

911b88855c3e65da.title: Rain begins in north Andhra ahead of Cyclone Murasu
911b88855c3e65da.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 02:06 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Rough waves lash the Palepalem coast near Kothapatnam in Prakasam district on Monday, ahead of Cyclone Murasu’s expected landfall near Ongole. | Photo Credit: Kommuri Srinivas The first rain from Cyclone Murasu has fallen in north coastal Andhra Pradesh, far from where the storm is headed. The central and south coastal districts, which are on red alert, were yet to see any major rainfall on Monday (November 2, 2026). Kakinada (Rural) mandal recorded the most rain between 8.30 a.m. and noon, 51.75 mm at the MRO office gauge, according to real-time data from the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (APDES). Most of the rain fell in Kakinada, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts. Visakhapatnam’s highest reading was 12.5 mm at Gambheeram in Anandapuram mandal. Ongole in Prakasam district, where the landfall is likely to happen, had not recorded any rain as of 10 a.m. The Rayalaseema districts stayed dry. In the 24 hours to 8.30 a.m. on Monday, Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district recorded the most rain in the State, 102.49 mm at the KVBR School gauge. Meanwhile, the severe cyclonic storm over the west-central and southwest Bay of Bengal is moving west-northwestwards at 22 kmph towards the A.P. coast. At 8.30 a.m. on Monday, the storm was located about 160 km east-southeast of Nellore, 180 km northeast of Chennai, 180 km east-southeast of Kavali, 210 km southeast of Ongole and 240 km south of Machilipatnam. Weather experts said the system had moved fast in the morning but may slow down near the coast. The landfall is likely between 11.30 p.m. on Monday and 4 a.m. on Tuesday, according to the India Meteorological Department. Photo: Special Arranagement Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu. The Collector, in a press release here on Sunday, informed that the district administration has made all necessary arrangements to effectively deal with Cyclone Murasu. Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: November 02, 2026 A special control room has been set up at the Collectorate to ensure that people do not face any inconvenience due to the cyclone and to facilitate immediate relief measures. The control room will function round-the-clock. Staff have been deployed to provide necessary information to the public and coordinate relief operations. People can contact the control room for emergency assistance or information on the number 08647 252999 In view of the cyclone warnings, the District Collector urged people to remain alert and avoid going outdoors unless absolutely necessary. 51b6d65215f5069a.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:15 pm IST - KALABURAGI Anish P. More of SRN Mehta State School in Kalaburagi with representatives of the school’s management and teachers after securing fifth place in the State-level under-14 chess championship and qualifying for the national-level competition. | Photo Credit: ARUN KULKARNI Anish P. More, a student of SRN Mehta School in Kalaburagi, has been selected to participate in the national-level chess championship to be held in Madhya Pradesh after securing fifth place in the State-level under-14 chess competition. The tournament was organised by the Department of Public Instruction at Gangavati in Koppal district of Karnataka from October 15 to 17 as part of the 2026-27 academic year’s sports competitions. 1eff5fc8eac5c5a4.title: Coast Guard evacuates fisherman in distress 100 km off Mangaluru coast
1eff5fc8eac5c5a4.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 01:24 pm IST - MANGALURU Indian Coast Guard Ship C-448 reaches Indian fishing boat Shiv Sagar, about 100 km off the Mangaluru coast, to rescue a fisherman in urgent need of medical attention on the night of November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Indian Coast Guard (ICG), District Headquarter 3, Mangaluru, safely evacuated a fisherman in urgent need of medical attention from a fishing vessel sailing about 100 km off Mangaluru coast on November 1 night. The headquarters received a distress call over VHF from Indian Fishing Boat (IFB) Shiv Sagar, operating approximately 54 NM (100 km) off Mangaluru on November 1. They were told that a fisherman had fallen overboard while hauling fishing nets. He was rescued, but required urgent medical attention, and shifting to a hospital. The ICG deployed Indian Coast Guard Ship C-448, which located the fishing boat amid the darkness of the night. The disoriented fisherman, identified as Komara Ramu, was safely evacuated, provided immediate first aid, and transferred to New Mangalore Port Authority jetty. He was subsequently shifted to the nearest hospital for further medical management. IFB Shiv Sagar had sailed out of Old Mangaluru Port three days ago, ICG informed. a00438c594b93c32.title: KBN Hospital hosts workshop on hysterectomy and advanced laparoscopy in Kalaburagi
a00438c594b93c32.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:18 pm IST - KALABURAGI Dignitaries inaugurate the advanced live laparoscopy workshop organised by Khaja Banda Nawaz University and the Karnataka State Obstetrics and Gynaecology Association at KBNTGH in Kalaburagi on October 30, 2026. | Photo Credit: ARUN KULKARNI A workshop on ‘Hysterectomy: Different Approaches and Advanced Laparoscopy’ was conducted at Khaja Banda Nawaz Teaching and General Hospital (KBNTGH) in Kalaburagi on October 30 as part of the conference of the Karnataka State Obstetrics and Gynaecology Association (KSOGA), in collaboration with Khaja Banda Nawaz University. The workshop provided a platform for gynaecologists and medical professionals to interact with experts and gain insights into the latest technologies, techniques and developments in the field. Around 150 delegates from different parts of Karnataka had registered for the programme. Ten surgical procedures performed in the operation theatre were telecast live to the seminar hall, enabling participants to observe the procedures, and interact with experts during the sessions. Highlighting the importance of the workshop, Professor Syed Ashfaq Ahmed said it could bring positive changes to the lives of many women by promoting awareness and knowledge of modern treatment options. He said participants had benefited from direct interaction with specialists and gained valuable information about recent advances in medical technology. He reiterated the hospital’s commitment to providing quality healthcare to all sections of society, particularly the poor and needy. He said the hospital was upgrading its departments with advanced technology to emerge as a leading, well-equipped medical centre in the region. It was also organising free medical screening and treatment camps regularly to protect public health, he added. 351ef5661d84b3fb.title: Hyundai Motor India sales hit record 82,299 units in October, up 17.7%
351ef5661d84b3fb.summary: Hyundai Motor India Limited (HMIL) on Sunday reported its highest-ever total monthly sales, including exports, of 82,299 units in October, a 17.7 per cent year-on-year rise. The milestone was driven by record domestic sales of 62,799 units, a 16.7 per cent rise, and exports grew 21.1 per cent to 19,500 units, the automaker said. Going forward, the newly launched Hyundai BAYON - our Intelligent Utility Vehicle, will provide further impetus to our growth in India as well as across 50+ export markets, reinforcing India's role as a strategic manufacturing and export hub for Hyundai".

7751d2870f6a8c29.title: Escorts Kubota reports 10% decline in October sales to 16,921 units
7751d2870f6a8c29.summary: Escorts Kubota Ltd on Sunday reported a 10 per cent year-on-year decline in total tractor sales to 16,921 tractors in October from 18,798 a year earlier. Its domestic tractor sales fell 10.9 per cent to 16,412 tractors compared to 18,423 units in the year-ago period. However, the company's exports rose 35.7 per cent to 509 units in October against 375 units in the year-ago period. The industry witnessed some moderation in October 2026, impacted by a high base, shift in festive timing and monsoon-related disruptions. Elevated input costs due to geopolitical developments and consequent pricing actions may moderate demand in the near term, the company said in a release.

955a18fec86a349a.summary: Sarda Energy & Minerals has reported a 2.2 per cent decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 320 crore, mainly impacted by lower revenues. However, in April-September, its PAT grew 4.5 per cent to Rs 799 crore from Rs 764 crore in the year-ago period. Sarda Energy & Minerals Limited (SEML) is an integrated energy and minerals company with interests spanning power generation, mining, steel and ferro alloys.

eb1eeb2f5d1fe4a5.title: Gross GST collections rise 23% to ₹2.31 trillion in October on strong sales
eb1eeb2f5d1fe4a5.summary: Gross GST collections increased 23 per cent to over Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, driven by strong mop-up from domestic activities and imports, according to government data released on Sunday. Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16 per cent to over Rs 1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42 per cent to Rs 72,246 crore. The Rs 2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42,935 crore, State GST of Rs 51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over Rs 1.37 lakh crore, data showed. Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 27,934 crore in October. After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26 per cent to over Rs 2.03 lakh crore in October. During April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2 per cent to over Rs 14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13 per cent to over Rs 12.69 lakh crore.

77959aa04b44f5f2.title: I was offered ₹5 crore to make someone Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram president: Rajmohan
77959aa04b44f5f2.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:26 am IST - Chennai School Education Minister Rajmohan. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU Tamil Nadu Minister for Information and Publicity Rajmohan on Sunday alleged that he was offered ₹5 crore as bribe to appoint someone as the president of the Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram. Participating at the Tamil Nadu Day event celebrations at Egmore in Chennai, the Minister said: “I have not revealed this before. [Tamil Nadu Textbook Corporation chief] Layola Mani knows this. A person said, ‘If I am given the post of president of the Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram, I will offer ₹5 crore to Minister Rajmohan’. I smiled and told Layola Mani, even if someone offers ₹500 crore as bribe, I will not give the post to someone who is not suited for it. Without even getting a single rupee from anyone, Pushpavanam Kuppusamy, who is the most suited for the role, was appointed as the president of the association.” According to him, for the first time in Tamil Nadu, every Minister [in the C Joseph Vijay cabinet] hates bribery and corruption. Meanwhile, AIADMK leader D. Jayakumar questioned the identity of the person who allegedly offered to bribe Mr. Rajmohan and said the person should be prosecuted. Speaking to reporters, he said: “There is no doubt that Pushpavanam Kuppusamy is the right person for that post. But, who was the one who came forward through [Chairman of the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation] Layola Mani to offer ₹5 crore? Should that person not be brought before the law?” Mr. Jayakumar added: “If Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay was honest, he should name the person and prosecute him.” Published - November 02, 2026 12:26 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 844d3f04c39fa5a4.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:12 am IST - Bengaluru One-of-its-kind projects in the country, the skydeck received Cabinet approval in August 2024, when Siddaramaiah was Chief Minister and Mr. Shivakumar was his deputy. The project was estimated to cost up to ₹500 crore. The Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) has finalised the land for the 250-metre-high skydeck, one of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s pet projects, and begun preparatory work to invite design proposals. With the project gathering pace, the BDA sources told The Hindu that the value of corner sites in Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout (NPKL), and plots around the identified project site is expected to more than double soon after work begins. This could, however, potentially place an additional financial burden on prospective buyers. One-of-its-kind projects in the country, the skydeck received Cabinet approval in August 2024, when Siddaramaiah was Chief Minister and Mr. Shivakumar was his deputy. The project was estimated to cost up to ₹500 crore. After considering more than five locations and narrowing them down to two, the BDA has finalised 46.25 acres of land falling under Bheemanakuppe survey numbers 104 and 75, and Challaghatta survey numbers 13, 58/3 and 49. The selected land parcels fall within the NPKL in west Bengaluru. P. Manivannan, BDA Commissioner, said that the authority is preparing to invite Expressions of Interest (EoI) for design proposals. “We are looking at getting multiple designs and their cost prospects. Mr. Manivannan said the BDA had also onboarded a transaction adviser. Several aspects of the project, including possession of the land, had also been cleared, he said. 5b5aaf3e99e3b146.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
5b5aaf3e99e3b146.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:53 am IST With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites. The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. 5853f885cfa5693d.title: Alcaraz beats De Minaur to win Vienna Open without dropping a set to clinch fourth title this year
5853f885cfa5693d.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 05:14 am IST - Vienna Spain's Carlos Alcaraz poses with the trophy after winning the men's singles final against Australia's Alex de Minaur during the Vienna Open ATP tennis tournament in Vienna, Austria, on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP Seven-time Grand Slam winner Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open on Sunday (November 1, 2026) and defeat his opponent for the seventh time in as many meetings. Alcaraz has beaten the Australian on grass and clay as well as on indoor and outdoor hard courts. He sealed his latest victory with trademark panache. Alcaraz drew his opponent to the net with a sliced backhand drop shot. De Minaur retrieved it but Alcaraz lobbed him with a backhand and, after the Australian volleyed that shot back near the net, clipped a cross-court forehand that landed just in. The second-seeded Spaniard looked jubilant and cracked a broad smile after clinching his fourth title this year — including the Australian Open for a career Grand Slam — and his 28th overall. The fifth-seeded De Minaur was looking for his second title of the year. He advanced to the final of the ATP 500 event with a semifinal win against Alexander Zverev, who will top the rankings on Monday (November 2, 2026). Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev in the other semi. 0b6e9aeb65c95fdd.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
0b6e9aeb65c95fdd.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:46 am IST Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 30, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries, that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn. 6c515e1ea67140f6.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:18 am IST - CHENNAI The cattle were found crammed inside the container, with little space to stand. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Twenty-five heads of cattle allegedly being transported from Andhra Pradesh to Kerala for slaughter were rescued by the police near Pazhavali, near Maraimalai Nagar, on Saturday evening.. The complaint was filed by Sai Vignesh, president of Almighty Animal Care Trust, who said that he noticed cow dung and urine leaking from a container truck near Maraimalai Nagar, and alerted the police through an emergency helpline. The police intercepted the vehicle near Pazhavali after a chase. The cattle were found crammed inside the container, with little space to stand. Their nose ropes had been tied to bars on the roof, and several animals had sustained injuries. The vehicle allegedly lacked adequate ventilation and provisions for food and drinking water. Following the intervention, all 25 cattle were handed over to Gosamrakshana Gaushala for medical treatment and care. Mr. Vignesh also lodged a formal complaint with the police seeking action against those responsible. 810a887f6caf2122.title: Lifter Usha tops her 61kg group, Nirupama finishes disappointing 4th in Group C at World Championships
810a887f6caf2122.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 05:46 am IST - Ningbo (China) Indian weightlifter Usha topped Group D, while compatriot Nirupama Devi endured a disappointing outing to finish fourth in Group C of the women's 61kg competition at the IWF World Championships in Ningbo on Sunday (November 1, 2026). The 23-year-old Usha lifted a total of 212kg — 93kg in snatch and 119kg in clean and jerk — to finish ahead of all the lifters in her group and several competitors in the higher Group C as well. Nirupama, who has moved down from the 63kg weight class, managed a total of 211kg (91kg+120kg), one kilogram short of Usha's effort despite being placed in Group C owing to her higher entry total. Following the completion of Groups C and D, Usha was placed third overall while Nirupama was fifth. Their final standings will be updated after the completion of Group A. Usha started with a successful 90kg snatch before failing to lift 93kg in her next attempt, but the Indian regained her composure to clear the same weight in her third and final snatch attempt. In the clean and jerk as well, Usha managed to complete two of her three attempts. After successfully lifting 115kg and 119kg, she faltered in her final attempt of 121kg. On the other hand, Nirupama just managed to register a total after completing the minimum two successful lifts. She started with a failed attempt at 91kg in snatch but managed to lift the weight in her second attempt before failing to clear 93kg in her third. In the clean and jerk, she lifted 120kg before failing in both attempts to heave 124kg. At the World Championships, Group A comprises lifters with the highest declared entry totals — the combined weight they intend to lift in the snatch and clean and jerk — while Groups B, C and D feature athletes with progressively lower entry totals. The World Championships is one of six events in the first period of the Olympic qualification system for the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Published - November 02, 2026 05:46 am IST Term

b1ed1a0c8ea58afc.title: GVMC polls record 51% turnout with Bheemunipatnam leading at 65%
b1ed1a0c8ea58afc.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 12:09 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Voters wait in a queue to exercise their franchise at a polling booth in Peda Jalaripeta, in the East Assembly Constituency during the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation elections in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU Barring a few alleged irregularities and violations of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC), the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) election elections passed off peacefully on Sunday. The city registered a voter turnout of 51.47%, according to preliminary figures released by the election authorities at 9:30 p.m. The final polling percentage is yet to be released. The turnout this time was considerably lower than the 59.41% recorded in the previous GVMC elections held in 2021. Of the 18.37 lakh registered voters across the city, 9,45,915 exercised their franchise. They included 4.55 lakh men and 4.90 lakh are women. Nearly 8.91 lakh voters stayed away from casting their votes, according to the preliminary report. Ward No. 105 in Aganampudi recorded the lowest turnout of 28%, while Ward No. 5 in the Bheemunipatnam Zone registered the highest at 74.69%. Among the zones, Bheemunipatnam topped the list with a turnout of 65.90%, followed by Anakapalli at 65.54%. Gajuwaka, which has the highest voter population of around 2.98 lakh, recorded a turnout of 54.10%, while Aganampudi registered 53.46%. The South Zone, which includes One Town recorded a turnout of 51.24%, followed by the West Zone with Gopalapatnam, Simhachalam, and Malkapuram registering 51.21%, and Madhurawada with 50.81%. The East Zone registered 50.55%, while Pendurthi recorded 48.93%. The North Zone, which includes prominent residential localities such as Seethammadhara and Balayya Sastry Layout, witnessed the lowest turnout among these zones at 44.24%. Polling began on a sluggish note, particularly in the densely populated urban areas. The first two hours, between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m., witnessed a turnout

2aff8262e3f0b1de.title: Asian Champions Trophy: Harmanpreet’s hat-trick helps India down Malaysia
2aff8262e3f0b1de.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:09 am IST - Jalandhar Harmanpreet, centre, converted two penalty corners and a penalty stroke. | Photo Credit: X@TheHockeyIndia It was expected to be India’s toughest test of the tournament and the match between the two highest ranked sides in the competition lived up to its billing. Malaysia tested the host before India prevailed 4-2 to remain the only unbeaten side at the Asian Champions Trophy here on Sunday. The penultimate day of the league competition at the Olympian Surjeet Stadium also confirmed the semifinalists with Japan and Korea completing the line-up. The rematch between the Asian Games finalists was a much closer affair but it was also more tactical as well. A lot of play was confined to the midfield with neither team being in complete control but neither willing to pull back either. India took an early lead when Harmanpreet Singh converted the team’s first penalty corner in the third minute but then missed a couple of chances up front. With both teams well matched in every department, it was more a battle of attrition than one of skills. Compared to the final in Nagoya, Malaysia was more compact and read the Indian team better, anticipating the overlapping and passes and using short passes to try and break the flow. On the other hand, India found its own way around, pressing harder off the ball and being inventive with the passing. Both coach Craig Fulton and captain Harmanpreet admitted that the finishing needed to be clinical. “We created chances, it is up to us to make use of them,” Fulton agreed. Harmanpreet got a hat-trick, converting another PC in the 33rd and a penalty stroke in the 58th. Malaysia equalised through Akhimullah Anuar to be level at half time, then Shello Silverius pulled one back in the final seconds. A part of it will be placed at the disposal of Sir Frederick Nicholson, who is expected here from Europe in March next, to carry on further research work of the best and the easiest methods of utilising the fruits for jams. There are approximately 7,000 lbs. of jams in the factory which will be sold before the buildings are handed over to the Sub-Collector for his office and Court. Falkowska won 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 but the teenager made her sweat for more than two hours under the floodlights on Saturday evening. The Pole initially overpowered Jensi, but in the second set the Indian could read Falkowska’s serve. Falkowska tried surprising Jensi with drop shots and the Indian responded with impressive court coverage. Facing a left-handed player, quite uncommon in the sport, added to the tension Falkowska was feeling. “In the second set, Falkowska was unable to handle the shots hit into her body,” said Jensi. The Pole, however, gathered her composure and edged the teenager in the decider. 60b87fabad4ffcec.title: Marquez wins in Malaysia to stand on brink of MotoGP world title
60b87fabad4ffcec.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 05:32 am IST - Sepang, Malaysia Ducati Lenovo Team's Marc Marquez celebrates after winning the MotoGP race of the Malaysian Grand Prix at Sepang International Circuit, Sepang, Malaysia on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters Marc Marquez moved to the brink of an eighth world title with an imperious victory at the Malaysian MotoGP on Sunday (November 1, 2026). The Ducati star romped to a dominant win in 40min 14.236sec, finishing 4.172sec ahead of Red Bull’s Pedro Acosta as his younger brother Alex Marquez came third, almost six seconds adrift. Marquez, who is now 44 points ahead of his closest rival Jorge Martin, has seven victories to his name this season. It was also his third triumph in Malaysia in the MotoGP class, having last won in Sepang back in 2018. With Aprilia’s Martin missing the Sepang weekend with a broken wrist, his fellow Spaniard Marquez can seal the championship next weekend in Qatar. Marquez wasted no time in snatching the lead from his brother as the riders came into Turn 1 from the start, and the siblings briefly traded places before the older Marquez just edged ahead in scorching conditions. Saturday’s sprint race winner Acosta tailed both the Marquez brothers closely in third, with Italian Marco Bezzecchi in fourth and Japan’s Ai Ogura in fifth. Championship leader Marquez, 33, began to pull away from the chasing pack to develop a 1.7 sec advantage over his brother, who was valiantly defending his second spot against Acosta. Acosta would be rewarded for his persistence as the Red Rull rider snatched second place from Alex Marquez in Lap 10. At the front Marquez coasted to victory unchallenged to continue his purple streak in the second half of the 2026 season. After Qatar there are just two weekends left in the campaign. 6fdc3913b4479f9d.title: 800 houses in Division 59 of Kochi Corporation to get sewerage connection by December
6fdc3913b4479f9d.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI The Kerala Water Authority's sewage treatment plant at Elamkulam in Kochi. STPs had been proposed in three divisions, including Edakochi North. | Photo Credit: file photo Around 800 houses in Division 59 (Edakochi South) will be connected to the sewerage network linked to the 1.1-MLD sewage treatment plant (STP) in the first phase of the project by December. With the project nearing completion, half of the houses in the division will be connected to the new STP, which is expected to cover around 1,800 households. “The construction work on the STP has been completed. The installation of electro-mechanical components remains, and the work is progressing,” said a KWA source. The sewage pipeline to be laid within the division will have a total length of 18 km. “Of this, only 200 m of the pipeline remains to be laid. 56be8f59dd04b474.title: Science Snapshots: November 1, 2026
56be8f59dd04b474.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:00 am IST A view of the Rub al-Khali quarter of the desert in Saudi Arabia in 2007. | Photo Credit: Javierblas (CC BY-SA) Even in a desert, early humans sought more than water More than water alone guided humans in the ancient Arabian Peninsula. Scientists earlier believed human populations expanded across ‘Green Arabia’ wherever lakes formed. But after surveying a 1,500-km stretch in the Rub’ al Khali desert, researchers found evidence of 55 extinct lakes but no stone tools or signs of life. Since early humans relied on stone tools for survival, the team concluded human migration was guided by the availability of both water and toolmaking stones. 12a9b6d4922e2a92.title: ‘Murasu’ strengthens into Severe Cyclonic Storm
12a9b6d4922e2a92.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:01 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal. A scene at Marina Beach on November 1 | Photo Credit: Velankanni Raj B Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours on Monday (November 2). As per observations made by the IMD at 2.30 a.m., the storm lay centered over the same region, which is about 260 km east-northeast of Chennai, 290 km east-southeast of Nellore, 320 km south-southeast of Machilipatnam, 310 km east-southeast of Kavali, 330 km southeast of Ongole and 470 km south of Vishakhapatnam. The system may continue to move northwestwards and cross south Andhra Pradesh coast, near Ongole, as a Severe Cyclonic Storm with wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph gusting 120 kmph. The rainfall activity has begun in parts of the State as of 6 a.m. Extremely heavy rainfall alert has been issued for the five districts of Eluru, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla and SPSR Nellore, and very heavy rainfall is likely in the districts of NTR, Eluru, East and West Godavari, Palnadu, Chittoor and Tirupati for Monday, November 1. 5d36295c43003d6a.title: New HMT watches celebrate Kannada identity with regional design elements
5d36295c43003d6a.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:07 am IST - Bengaluru Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy and BJP leader R. Ashok unveiling the ‘HMT Kannadiga’ wristwatches, in Bengaluru on Sunday. | Photo Credit: ALLEN EGENUSE J. Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy on Sunday unveiled a new collection of watches by Hindustan Machine Tools (HMT), named “HMT Kannadiga”, to mark the 71st Karnataka Rajyotsava. The watches will soon be available at the HMT stores in the city. Hundreds of people thronged the HMT grounds in north Bengaluru. However, much to their disappointment, the watches were not yet available for purchase. The new collection comprises four different variants, although the design remains the same. The watches come with different strap and chain options. To emphasise the essence of the language, the dials feature Kannada numericals. A Gandabherunda emblem highlights Kannada pride, while the yellow-and-red Kannada flag and the series name, “HMT Kannadiga”, underscore regional identity. The watches are estimated to be priced at ₹3,500 and ₹3,600, placing them in the HMT’s premium segment. Meanwhile, pictures of the watches released on Saturday have been widely shared on social media and among groups of watch aficionados. According to officials, the watches will feature modern technology and a radium glow. The strap variants will be fitted with genuine Italian leather straps. A team of 16 employees from Alorica Ecospace had come on a holiday to Koje resort near Dubbanshashi beach near Gokarna. They entered the sea waters in the morning but were caught in the strong waves. 967d6c8c641288c5.title: GST decriminalisation decisions mark shift to trust-based governance: CII
967d6c8c641288c5.summary: Industry body CII on Sunday described the GST Council's decisions to decriminalise certain offences and rationalise enforcement powers as a significant institutional reform, saying the move marks a shift towards trust-based economic governance and offers a model for India's next generation of economic reforms. On the decisions taken at the GST Council's October 8 meeting, CII said the consensus-driven approach showed how the Centre and states could work together on difficult reforms to improve the relationship between the government and businesses. CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee said, "The GST Council's decisions deserve special recognition as a landmark institutional reform. We deeply appreciate the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in advancing this transformation, and the constructive role of state governments in achieving consensus on an issue involving sensitive questions of enforcement, revenue protection and taxpayer .

ad386963cafc689e.title: ‘Cyclone Murasu’: Palnadu District Collector declares November 2 holiday for schools, colleges over
ad386963cafc689e.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:06 am IST - NARASARAOPET (PALNADU DISTRICT) Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu. The Collector, in a press release here on Sunday, informed that the district administration has made all necessary arrangements to effectively deal with Cyclone Murasu. A special control room has been set up at the Collectorate to ensure that people do not face any inconvenience due to the cyclone and to facilitate immediate relief measures. The control room will function round-the-clock. Staff have been deployed to provide necessary information to the public and coordinate relief operations. People can contact the control room for emergency assistance or information on the number 08647 252999 In view of the cyclone warnings, the District Collector urged people to remain alert and avoid going outdoors unless absolutely necessary. 5105340bf45a0333.title: Solex Energy eyeing US market for international debut, says chairman
5105340bf45a0333.summary: Eyeing a footprint in the global renewable energy market, homegrown Solex Energy plans to establish solar module and cell manufacturing capacities in the US as part of its USD 1.5 billion investment roadmap through 2030. In an interaction, the company's Chairman Chetan Shah said that while the US remains the largest global solar market, steep anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports leave India as the sole viable supplier of low-cost alternatives. When asked whether Solex Energy is exploring expansion in the US, he replied in the affirmative. Sharing the rationale behind the move, he said Solex Energy is targeting the US market for expansion primarily to capitalise on the massive global demand for clean energy components while positioning itself as a reliable, cost-effective alternative to Chinese suppliers. "The US is a high-potential market. While many Indian corporates are already present there, a healthy number of business houses, including us, are also looking to invest there,"
