76859e4a55e99067.title: A.P. seeks assistance from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka for cyclone power restoration
76859e4a55e99067.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 11:56 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought assistance from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to mobilise personnel and machinery for restoring electricity infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh in anticipation of damage from Cyclone Murasu. Mr. Naidu spoke to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Sunday and requested them to extend support by deploying the necessary manpower and equipment for restoration works in cyclone-hit areas. Both Chief Ministers responded positively and assured him of all possible assistance. Mr. Naidu said officials of Andhra Pradesh would coordinate with their counterparts in the two States to facilitate the deployment of personnel and machinery. Meanwhile, electricity department personnel from Telangana are already engaged in restoring infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab. The State government has also kept teams that completed restoration works in the Arnab-affected areas on standby for deployment in regions likely to be affected by Murasu. The move is aimed at ensuring the availability of additional manpower and equipment to tackle possible damage to power infrastructure, particularly the uprooting of electricity poles. f71560495f0d02ac.title: Coal India's October coal output rises 19.3% to 67.2 million tonnes
f71560495f0d02ac.summary: Coal India Ltd (CIL) on Sunday said its coal production rose 19.3 per cent year-on-year to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October. The state-owned miner had produced 56.4 MT in the same month last year, according to provisional data filed with the stock exchanges. Offtake in October stood at 70.3 MT, up 18.7 per cent from 59.2 MT a year ago. For the April-October period of 2026-27, CIL's production inched up 0.7 per cent to 388.2 MT from 385.5 MT in the year-ago period. Offtake during the seven months grew 9.2 per cent to 454.6 MT from 416.2 MT. Among the subsidiaries, Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) recorded the highest production in October at 20.8 MT, up 25.3 per cent. South Eastern Coalfields Ltd (SECL) produced 14.3 MT, a rise of 17.4 per cent. Western Coalfields Ltd (WCL) posted the sharpest growth, with output rising 64.7 per cent to 5.9 MT. Eastern Coalfields Ltd (ECL) produced 4.6 MT, up 27.9 per cent, while Central Coalfields Ltd (CCL) output rose 26.1 per cent to 7.3 MT. Bh

8e4125e2684ee9b7.title: Maruti Suzuki posts record sales in Oct with 25% growth despite high base
8e4125e2684ee9b7.summary: India's largest passenger vehicle maker Maruti Suzuki on Sunday posted its highest-ever monthly sales in October with 25 per cent year-on-year growth in total dispatches to 2.76 lakh units, despite a high base in the year-ago period. Domestic passenger vehicle dispatches rose over 20 per cent to 2.12 lakh units, while total domestic dispatches, which include Super Carry and sales to other OEMs, grew around 19 per cent to 2.26 lakh units, according to an exchange filing. The strong growth despite a high base in the comparable period reflects robust demand in the market amid peak festival season. 23cc6e362a2ff3f6.summary: Three leading global beverage companies - Carlsberg, Pernod Ricard and The Coca-Cola Company - are advancing their plans for potential listings of their Indian businesses, albeit at different stages, as they prepare to tap the domestic capital market and join the growing pipeline of large offerings. 38bf1aaa55fa7ee9.title: Honda Motorcycle's total wholesale sales rise 13% to 734,000 units in Oct
38bf1aaa55fa7ee9.summary: Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India on Sunday said its total wholesale sales, including domestic and exports, rose 13 per cent year-on-year to 7.34 lakh units in October. The automaker sold 6.50 lakh units in October 2025. Domestic sales grew 11 per cent to 6.64 lakh units from 5.98 lakh units, while exports increased 35 per cent to 69,735 units from 51,644 units. The Japanese automaker's total sales in April-October this year grew 15 per cent to 41.74 lakh units from 36.44 lakh units in the year-ago period. Domestic sales increased 13 per cent to 37.08 lakh units, and exports climbed 28 per cent to 4.65 lakh units.

5ad53c8ff0730c64.summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles on Sunday reported a 23 per cent rise in total sales to 75,426 units across domestic and international markets in October. The company registered total sales of 61,295 units in the year-ago month. Domestic passenger vehicle sales increased 21 per cent to 73,894 units last month from 61,134 units in October 2025, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPVL) said in a statement. International business passenger vehicle sales jumped manifold to 1,532 units in October compared to 161 units a year ago, it added.

14e8bffd818c6f8d.title: Govt to meet liquor firms as bulk Scotch tariff row threatens UK trade pact
14e8bffd818c6f8d.summary: Representative image from file. India's government will hold talks with liquor companies on Monday after domestic firms joined Diageo and Pernod in expressing alarm about a federal investigation into bulk Scotch ​imports, according to four sources and an industry letter. In the first major dispute ​linked to a historic India-UK trade pact implemented in July, New Delhi has told major companies ‌that bulk Scotch imports are not eligible for the tariff reduction to 75 per cent from 150 per cent agreed in the deal. The International Spirits & Wines Association of India, a group representing Pernod and Diageo, has privately warned New Delhi that the move to exclude bulk Scotch imports could undermine the pact. The Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies (CIABC) has now joined the protest by flagging a hit to domestic manufacturing, according to an October 27 confidential letter to the government that Reuters is reporting for the first time. Around 80 per cent of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk to be used to make popular brands, and India's $65 billion alcohol industry had hoped the cut in tariffs would bolster business. Top Indian commerce ministry officials will on Monday ‌hold closed-door talks with several senior executives of foreign and domestic liquor companies to discuss the issue, said the four people who have direct knowledge of the meeting. The ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours on Saturday. Britain has said it is working with India on the issue, and Scottish government has raised the treatment of bulk Scotch with New Delhi, Reuters has reported. India has not commented on the matter. Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during years of protracted negotiations on a UK-India free trade deal, though ​India, a whisky-loving nation, ultimately agreed to halve taxes on certain Scotch imports. d8b69d301d1d9e4d.title: Odisha launches search for 12 missing after rain-triggered landslide
d8b69d301d1d9e4d.summary: The Odisha government launched a search operation for 12 people who went missing after a rain-triggered landslide struck a village bordering Ganjam and Kandhamal districts a day ago, officials said on Saturday. Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil said altogether, 170 personnel of the National Disaster Response Force, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and Special Operation Group have been engaged in the operation to locate the missing people. "A hilltop village was home to 26 people. Thirteen of them managed to escape from the landslide, while 13 others went missing. One of the missing people has been traced, and others are still untraceable. The search operation has been going on since Friday night," Patil told reporters here on Saturday. The landslide at Gidipabali village under the Baibali panchayat in Ganjam's Bhanjanagar block was among the 10 such incidents that occurred during incessant rain triggered by cyclone Arnab. a6153da1392c8551.summary: Simplified GST registration for small sellers on e-commerce platforms, unified documentation for GST registration, faster refunds, and a Rs 10,000 threshold for issuing GST notices are some of the Goods and Services Tax process reforms that are likely to be rolled out from November 1, an official said on Thursday. The 57th GST Council meeting on October 8 approved a host of reforms in GST processes, primarily covering registration, returns, refund and adjudication. Officials said some of the changes approved by the Council that can be implemented through administrative processes will be brought into effect in phases from November 1, 2026. The changes which require an amendment to the GST law would be implemented from April 1, 2027. The notifications and circulars on the relevant process reforms have already been approved by the legal department and are likely to be issued on Friday, an official said. 97ee2683aa8ef35f.summary: Keeping in view raw material requirements of domestic textile industry, the Centre has extended the existing customs duty exemption on cotton imports until December 31, 2026, the textile ministry said on Saturday. The extension has been notified by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, dated October 30. b4a8952ccceb3461.summary: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, an accomplished fighter pilot with over 3,500 hours of flying experience on over 20 types of aircraft, on Saturday assumed charge as the new Chief of Air Staff. He succeeded Air Chief Marshal A P Singh who superannuated from the force after a 43-year-long illustrious career. The IAF accorded a ceremonial guard of honour to Air Chief Marshal Singh at the Race Course Air Force Station before he handed over the baton to Dixit. Air Chief Marshal Dixit, known for his strategic planning and who played a key role during Operation Sindoor, was serving as the Vice Chief of the force. In a distinguished career spanning four decades, Air Chief Marshal Dixit has held a variety of Command, Staff and Instructional appointments. Born on December 9, 1966, Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit was commissioned into the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force on December 6, 1986. Consolidated total income rose 22 per cent to Rs 417 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 341 crore a year earlier. Sequentially, net profit jumped 47 per cent from Rs 118 crore in the June quarter, while total income increased 22 per cent from Rs 341 crore. For the first half of FY27, consolidated net profit grew 20 per cent to Rs 291 crore, while total income rose 19 per cent to Rs 758 crore. "We are monitoring the system's progress and will issue further updates as it evolves," she said. f3b18465c001da4f.title: How were the States formed and how has the Indian map changed since 1947?
f3b18465c001da4f.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 12:38 pm IST File photo of a 1955 conference of Chief Ministers to discuss the recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission. THE HINDU PHOTO ARCHIVES The story so far: On the “appointed day”, as Independence Day was referred to in the Indian Independence Act, 1947, British paramountcy lapsed in India, leading to the formation of two independent dominions- India and Pakistan. Pre-independence India consisted of state units, provinces and more than 550 scattered princely states. Nearly 114 of these, through the Instrument of Accession, had already joined India before August 15. The rest had the choice of joining either India or Pakistan, with most deciding to accede to the former. From then to now, as India completes 79 years of independence and has 28 States and eight Union Territories, the internal boundaries of the country have undergone several changes with States being reorganised in multiple phases, with different factors behind the redrawing of the map. 7764aadbd610fe2b.title: Depression intensifies into deep depression over Bay of Bengal
7764aadbd610fe2b.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:09 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Fishing boats berthed at the Visakhapatnam fishing harbour following a weather warning advising fishermen not to venture into the sea due to a Depression over the Bay of Bengal around November 2. | Photo Credit: V. Raju The depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal intensified into a deep depression in the early hours of Sunday (November 1, 2026). According to observations recorded by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) at 5.30 a.m., the system was centred about 700 km east-southeast of Chennai, 770 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 770 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 810 km east-southeast of Ongole. The system is expected to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a cyclonic storm over the southwest and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal during the next six hours. It is likely to further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal on November 2. The development comes days after severe cyclonic storm Arnab hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on October 28. So far, the State, where polling for the municipal elections is under way in 92 urban local bodies, has not reported any significant rainfall. b5a5d1d8c6202dec.title: Commercial LPG prices hiked ₹10/cylinder; ATF hiked ₹1.37/litre
b5a5d1d8c6202dec.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 11:41 am IST - Delhi Image used for representative purposes only. | Photo Credit: PTI In the run-up to the festive season, oil-marketing companies increased prices of the commercial variant of the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders by nearly about ₹10 per cylinder across the country on Sunday (November 1, 2026). Further, prices of the 5 kg free-trade LPG (FTL) refill – primarily catering to migrant workers – increased by nearly ₹2.5 per cylinder. Prices of the domestic variant remained unchanged. Other than the bottled hydrocarbon gas, Sunday also had the prices of aviation turbine fuel (ATF) for domestic carriers surging by ₹1.37 per litre to ₹138.5 for every litre. This was the fourth such hike in jet fuel prices since it was last slashed in July. The latest hike has made the 19-kg cylinder in Delhi ₹10 more expensive and would now be sold at ₹2,820. The 5-kg FTL now costs ₹782 per refill in the national capital. Mumbai also woke up to a nearly similar hike. Prices of the 19 kg cylinder were hiked ₹10.5 for every cylinder to ₹2,775. Kolkata had the steepest upward revision. The cylinder became ₹17 more expensive and is now priced at ₹2,971. While in Chennai, prices increased ₹11.5 per cylinder to ₹2,994.5. Though Sunday’s standalone hike is marginal, it is the third consecutive hike since July and August, when prices of the 19 kg cylinder were cumulatively slashed by ₹380 per cylinder. Prices of the commercial variant have cumulatively increased by about ₹85 per cylinder refill across the three tranches since then, which includes the latest hike. Prior to the reduction in July and August, prices had cumulatively increased ₹1,345 for each cylinder across four tranches since March 7. The hike comes amidst a rise in projected under-recoveries for LPG in November and December. 01fce450362ae0c4.title: Seven Rameswaram fishermen detained by Sri Lankan Navy near Katchatheevu islet
01fce450362ae0c4.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 10:33 am IST - RAMESWARAM This image is used for representational purpose only. | Photo Credit: L. Balachandar In a fresh incident, seven fishermen from Rameswaram and Thangachimadam in the Ramanathapuram district were arrested on charges of poaching in international waters by Sri Lankan Navy personnel in the early hours of Sunday (November 1, 2026). According to Tamil Nadu Fisheries Department officials, Sri Lankan Navy personnel apprehended seven fishermen who were fishing between the Katchatheevu islet and Mannar North at around 1 a.m. on Sunday (November 1, 2026). They were taken, along with the trawler, to a naval port in the island nation. Fisheries Department officials issued 398 tokens on Saturday (October 31, 2026), and the fishermen were scheduled to return to the shores on Sunday evening (November 1, 2026). Seven of them were detained. Officials gave the names of the seven fishermen as Placius (41), Alagu Pandi (22), Antony Pitchai (33), Rabin (21), Nelson (58), Arulananda Xavier (65) and Sahaya Anand (34). Fishermen leaders have condemned the incident and urged the governments to get them released at the earliest. “We will convene a meeting of all fishermen associations in the coastal district and decide the next course of action,” the fishermen leader said, adding that with the Deepavali festival around, such an incident has come as a rude shock. 50bb05ef00ed760e.title: Tamil Nadu to set up 26 POCSO Act courts and four NDPS courts
50bb05ef00ed760e.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:34 pm IST - Chennai File photo of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. | Photo Credit: The Hindu Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered the establishment of 26 courts under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, and four courts under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, to expedite the trial of cases registered under these laws. A State government press release issued on Sunday (November 1, 2026) said during a review meeting on cases registered under the POCSO Act, the Chief Minister had stressed the need to ensure justice for victims by speeding up trials. He had also sought details on the need for additional courts. Accordingly, the government had decided to establish more courts. Already, 22 courts dealing with POCSO Act cases and four special courts will start functioning soon. The government said the Chief Minister had ordered the establishment of 12 special courts and 14 additional courts at a cost of ₹46.59 crore, taking into account the volume of cases registered under the Act. With the addition of these courts, there will be 52 special courts across 47 police districts. They are expected to expedite the delivery of justice and help prevent the recurrence of sexual offences against children, the government said. The release said, 11 special courts were already functioning to deal with cases registered under the NDPS Act. Four more courts will be established, one each in Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur and Vellore, and an additional court in Chennai. 08dd114c78b20be8.title: Four held from Malda as West Bengal STF busts interstate drug network
08dd114c78b20be8.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 01:08 pm IST - Kolkata Four people were arrested after the Special Task Force (STF) of the West Bengal Police busted an inter-State drug network in Kaliachak in Malda district on Saturday (October 31, 2026) night. According to officials, the operation was part of the STF’s ongoing crackdown on narcotics syndicates. On Saturday (October 31), an STF team intercepted a vehicle on National Highway 12 near Madhughat in Kaliachak and recovered 2.688 kg of morphine, estimated to be worth around ₹3 crore. Four key operatives, including the main supplier, Sahibar Ali, were arrested. All four are residents of Malda. A case has been registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act at Kaliachak police station. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari praised the officers for acting swiftly on a tip-off about the smuggling operation. “Let me remind the drug smugglers, racketeers and syndicate operators: they will be dealt with an iron fist, as our Government maintains an uncompromising Zero Tolerance Policy against drug peddling to safeguard the future of our Youth and strengthen our collective resolve under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan,” he said. Earlier, on October 21, an STF team raided a location in Baishnabnagar in Malda district and seized 505 g of morphine. A 26-year-old man, Sahinur Ali, a resident of Kaliachak, was arrested. The investigation found that the narcotics had been sourced from Ershad Alom of Thoubal in Manipur for Habibur of Sujapur Danga in Malda. They seized 90 kg of ganja, estimated to be worth approximately ₹44.5 lakh, ₹5 lakh in unaccounted cash and three vehicles. Two of those arrested were from Odisha and had allegedly come to deliver the contraband, while the others were the intended recipients. 60972eae64070a92.title: US judge dismisses Trump's multibillion-dollar defamation suit against WSJ
60972eae64070a92.summary: A federal judge has thrown out President Donald Trump's multibillion-dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to wealthy financier Jeffrey Epstein. US District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the suit with prejudice on Saturday, ruling that the president did not prove the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice. The ruling said the lawsuit was "grasping at straws" as it attempted to "manufacture" flaws in the Journal's investigative reporting. When a case is thrown out "with prejudice," it cannot be refiled again and the dismissal is permanent and incontrovertible. The lawsuit was over a story the Journal published last year describing a sexually suggestive letter that the paper said bore Trump's name and was included in a 2003 album compiled for Epstein's 50th birthday. 17224b0d06a5d6de.title: Plea in SC seeks to verify Ram temple stands on land adjudicated in dispute
17224b0d06a5d6de.summary: A plea has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking the constitution of a committee or a commission to determine whether the Ram temple at Ayodhya stands on the exact premises and land which was adjudicated by the apex court in its 2019 verdict. In a landmark judgment delivered on November 9, 2019, a five-judge constitution bench of the apex court had paved the way for the construction of the Ram Temple by a trust at the disputed site at Ayodhya. It had directed the Centre to allot an alternative five-acre plot to the Sunni Waqf Board for building a new mosque at a "prominent" place in the holy town in Uttar Pradesh. In a unanimous verdict, the top court had ruled that the 2.77 acres of disputed land where the demolished Babri Masjid once stood would remain with a central government receiver and be handed over to a trust within three months for construction of the temple. The plea filed in the apex court has sought a direction for an independent survey or demarcation of the premises

d23611f94bb09390.title: MeitY launches DEPA handbook to enable secure data sharing for AI training
d23611f94bb09390.summary: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has launched a handbook on Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI training, an official release said Saturday. The handbook outlines a techno-legal framework that allows institutions to collaborate on data for AI training while keeping control of their data. IT Secretary S Krishnan unveiled the handbook, which was developed with support from the iSPIRT Foundation, at a roundtable in Bengaluru. "The framework combines contractual permissions, controlled computing environments and privacy-enhancing safeguards. It also incorporates data provenance, enabling the origin, permissions and use of data to be traced throughout the training process, supporting accountability and transparency," the release said. As AI becomes central to economic and social development, access to diverse, high-quality data is critical. 00acd14ca3d9f6fc.title: Andhra civic polls: TDP, YSRCP workers clash in Pulivendula; 22.08% turnout by 11 a.m. | LIVE
00acd14ca3d9f6fc.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 01:09 pm IST Election staff leave for their assigned polling stations with election materials and other essential equipment ahead of the November 1, 2026, municipal elections in Vijayawada. Personnel were deployed to various polling stations to ensure the polling process ran smoothly and in an orderly manner. | Photo Credit: G.N. Rao W orkers of the ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) clashed in Pulivendula, the home turf of YSRCP chief and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, during Andhra Pradesh’s urban local body elections on Sunday (November 1, 2026). Stones were thrown in some wards before the police brought the situation under control. Polling elsewhere, so far, has been largely peaceful, State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha said. The overall turnout in the State reached 22.08% by 11 a.m. Smaller towns are voting faster than the big cities: Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district had recorded 60.92%, while Visakhapatnam, the largest corporation, was at 13.34%. Voting for 100 urban local bodies, 13 municipal corporations and 87 municipalities and nagar panchayats, began at 7 a.m. It will end at 5 p.m. Votes will be counted on November 3. Also Read: Arrangements in place for polling in 222 wards across NTR districts Eight municipalities and nagar panchayats are not voting at all: Allagadda, Dachepalli, Darsi, Gurajala, Kamalapuram, Piduguralla, Proddatur and Rayachoti. Their chairpersons and ward members were all elected unopposed. The polls were originally due on October 28. They were put off on the Supreme Court’s directions after complaints that candidates had been prevented from filing nominations. State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and Secretary A. Mallikarjuna reviewed polling across the State through webcasting on Sunday. Some 13,500 CCTV cameras have been installed at polling stations, following the Supreme Court’s directions. 8a44c3e8b4b62d58.title: Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul on his memoir ‘Without Fear or Favour ‘and the executive’s growing influence over the collegium system
8a44c3e8b4b62d58.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 08:59 am IST Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul Judge of Supreme Court of India, in New Delhi. | Photo Credit: Sandeep Saxena Few judges have offered as candid an account of the inner workings of India’s higher judiciary as former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul. In his memoir, Without Fear or Favour (Juggernaut), he reflects on a judicial career spanning over two decades, offering a ringside view of the politics surrounding judicial appointments, the executive’s growing influence over the collegium system, and the quiet power struggles simmering beneath the judiciary’s institutional facade. The memoir also offers a rare glimpse into the deliberations preceding some of the apex court’s most consequential judgments in recent years and the dilemmas confronting judges when called upon to reconcile competing interests. In an interview at his residence in New Delhi, the veteran jurist reflects on the need for systemic reforms and the challenges of preserving judicial independence. 5ad7bef16bff48b4.title: Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre launched in Chennai
5ad7bef16bff48b4.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:55 am IST - CHENNAI The Centre aims at combining traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic tools and medicines and AI-driven health assessment to develop individualised approaches to diabetes management. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement An Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre, which adopts an interdisciplinary approach to diabetes management, blending traditional Ayurvedic knowledge, modern medicine, and artificial intelligence, was inaugurated at Dr. RK Diabetic Foot and Podiatry Institute here on Saturday. The Centre aims at combining traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic tools and medicines and AI-driven health assessment to develop individualised approaches to diabetes management, said the Institute’s founder and director, Rajesh Kesavan. A clinical study involving about 100 patients has reported promising outcomes, with a 50% improvement in diabetes management and reduction in blood sugar spikes. At the centre, dietary interventions will be customised based on individual body composition and metabolic profiles for diabetes management. An AI kiosk will facilitate AI-based health assessments. Ayur AI founder Bala Pesala said the holistic intervention aims at achieving diabetes remission. Samir Kumar Brahmachari, former Director General, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, and Bandi Venkateshwarlu, assistant director, Regional Ayurveda Research Institute, Ministry of Ayush, also spoke. c26e86f97531b3ec.title: VIS–The Hindu U-15 inter-school football tournament draws to a close
c26e86f97531b3ec.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:31 am IST - Chennai: Students of Velammal Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Mogappair, receiving the trophy and cash prize. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT The third edition of the Vellore International School (VIS) U-15 inter-school football tournament, in association with The Hindu, concluded at the VIS campus near Kelambakkam on Saturday. The tournament witnessed participation from 64 teams representing schools across Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Vellore, and Tiruvannamalai. It also featured around 14 government and government-aided schools. Young footballers demonstrated their technical abilities, tactical understanding, as well as sporting discipline through a series of competitive encounters. Velammal Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Mogappair, emerged as the champions for the second consecutive year. Don Bosco Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Egmore, secured the second place, while Dr. Guruswamy Mudaliar Thondaimadala Thuluvala Vellala Higher Secondary School, Sowcarpet, finished third. The winning teams received cash prizes – ₹1,00,000 for the champions, ₹75,000 for the runners-up, and ₹50,000 for the second runners-up. Individual honours were also awarded to outstanding performers. VIS Chennai Chairman and VIT vice-president G.V. Selvam said, “We began the tournament with just schools from Chennai. This year, we have extended it to six northern districts of Tamil Nadu. Next year, we hope to extend it to other States as well.” Chief Guest Sayed Sabir Pasha, Technical Director of the All India Football Federation, said that while hosting a tournament with 64 schools is a great achievement, the tournament should grow further and feature more schools. 6380088cf6d071d2.title: IIM-Bangalore records 100% summer placements, with median stipend at ₹2 lakh per month
6380088cf6d071d2.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 01:18 am IST - Bengaluru The Indian Institute Of Management-Bangalore. | Photo Credit: File photo The summer placement for the 2026-28 cohorts at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM-B) concluded with all 608 participating students securing offers from 128 organisations during the placement week from October 26-29. Consulting accounted for a little over half the recruitments at 50.7% of all offers, according to a release from IIM-B. The median stipend for the batch was ₹2 lakh per month and the average ₹1.95 lakh per month. A record number of offers were made by Accenture Strategy, at 123. The process saw strong recruiter participation across consulting, finance, product management, sales and marketing, general management, and analytics domains. “The cycle also saw increased hiring by leading technology companies, along with a rise in first-time recruiters, who accounted for approximately 40% of participating organisations,” said the release. Tapas Ranjan Pati, head of Career Development Services, stated, “Management Consulting emerged as the most preferred domain, accounting for more than 50% of the offers, followed by Finance/Investments and Product Management Roles. Legacy recruiters, including global FMCG giants and leading Indian conglomerates, continue to recruit in significant numbers.” The placement committee said that the season witnessed strong participation from legacy and new recruiters, with approximately 40% being first-time recruiters. dd44aa9a5a1e9c68.title: Rajasthan IPS officer removed after ACB probe ordered against IAS husband
dd44aa9a5a1e9c68.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:52 am IST - JAIPUR The Rajasthan government on Saturday placed an Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, Prashakha Mathur, on awaiting posting order (APO) after an investigation by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) was approved against her husband and senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Shikhar Agrawal. Mr. Agrawal, who was also sent on APO earlier this week, is facing charges along with his family members of purchasing 40 villas in luxury resorts operated by a private firm in Udaipur and Alwar districts by allegedly abusing his position and influence and extending “undue benefits” to the firm. While Mr. Agrawal was serving as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries) and additionally held charge of four public sector corporations, his wife Ms. Mathur, a 1995-batch IPS officer, was posted as Additional Director General in charge of Planning, Modernisation and Welfare. The ACB has alleged that Mr. Agrawal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates and special concessional packages to the firm. The alleged purchases of villas were made in the names of Mr. Agrawal and Ms. Mathur, their two sons, and Mr. Agrawal’s parents-in-law. The ACB has registered a Preliminary Enquiry (PE) and launched an investigation into the allegations of abuse of official position, conflict of interest, and extending undue benefits to the firm in question. ACB Director General Govind Gupta said the properties were allegedly purchased at prices substantially below their market value. The ACB’s probe will examine whether the alleged benefits caused substantial financial losses to the State government and whether Mr. Agrawal and his family members acquired assets disproportionate to their known sources of income. c5fef672503edc6f.title: Two persons held for possession of country-made guns, explosives
c5fef672503edc6f.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:44 am IST - VELLORE Two persons, including a farmer, were arrested for possession of two country made guns and crude bombs near Pallikonda and Pernambut towns in Vellore on Saturday. Forest officials identified the arrested persons as U. Chandru, 21, a tribal from Irular community, and G. Srinivasan, 39, a farmer. Initial inquiry revealed that Srinivasan has been cultivating paddy and groundnuts on his two acre farmland. Forest officials said that, based on a tip-off, a special team conducted searches at his house and farmland, and found country made guns, explosives, nets, torchlights, and batteries. Forest officials said that Srinivasan procured guns from his contacts in Kerala. He used pellets to hunt monkeys, rabbits, and spotted deer in forests surrounding Jawadhu Hills. In a separate incident, forest officials arrested Chandru, who was allegedly loitering with a country-made gun in the area. The team nabbed him during a regular patrol and seized the country-made gun, pellets, and explosives. Forest officials said both arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. Further probe is under way. Published - November 01, 2026 12:44 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 2fb7b8f01c577d93.title: New bridge to be opened near Sholinghur to replace British-era structure
2fb7b8f01c577d93.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:43 am IST - RANIPET Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the under-construction bridge across in the presence of S. Selvarani, Project Director (PD), DRDA (Ranipet), and Prabhakaran, Executive Engineer (EE), DRDA (Ranipet). | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT A new ₹3.85 crore high-level bridge across the Rendadi Water Supply Channel near Ponnai River, at Sekkadikuppam village near Sholinghur town in Ranipet will be opened for public use by December this year. Officials of the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA), which executes the work, said that the new facility was a long-standing demand of at least eight surrounding farming villages across the water channel. The new bridge will replace the British-era causeway, which was damaged during 2021 floods in the water channel, fed by Ponnai river. The new bridge will provide easy access to villagers in Ranipet and Thiruvallur districts. “The new bridge will help farmers to transport farm products to common markets in surrounding big towns. Buses will also be operated to reach remote villages,” S. Kannan, Assistant Engineer (AE), DRDA (Sholinghur), told The Hindu. On Saturday, Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the under-construction bridge in the presence of S. Selvarani, Project Director (PD), DRDA (Ranipet), and Prabhakaran, Executive Engineer (EE), DRDA (Ranipet). “During monsoon, residents could not cross the water channel due to chest-deep water. The new bridge will be a lifeline for residents as ambulances and government buses can reach remote villages in the region,” said T. Perumal, a farmer. DRDA officials said that the new bridge will replace the dilapidated causeway, which was demolished for the work, to connect surrounding villages with towns like Sholinghur, Arakkonam, Tiruvallur, and Tiruttani. 2a5f565e213d767f.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:27 am IST - CHENNAI Teams of Chennai Metrowater officials on Saturday launched the second phase of a rainwater harvesting awareness campaign across the city. A press release said 79 multi-storied buildings across various zones of the city were covered as part of the campaign. Residents were urged to maintain their RWH structures to facilitate better groundwater recharge during the Northeast monsoon. The campaigns will cover more buildings every Saturday. The water agency has also written to various commercial buildings, including theatres, and educational institutions, highlighting the significance of maintaining RWH structures. As on October 26, the teams had covered 81 multi-storied buildings across the city zones, the release said. 89c635675562c8c6.title: K.V. Thiruvengadam memorial oration delivered in Chennai
89c635675562c8c6.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:31 am IST - CHENNAI The first of the events planned for a year-long celebration of renowned clinician and teacher, the late K.V. Thiruvengadam in his birth centenary year, was held on Saturday, a press release said. The Padmashri Prof. K.V. Thiruvengadam Memorial Oration was delivered at Sree Balaji Medical College and Hospital, by S.R. Chandra, former professor and head of neurology, NIMHANS, Bengaluru, on ‘The Patient Speaks, the Doctor Thinks and the Research Begins’, offering a compelling perspective on the centrality of clinical reasoning, attentive history-taking and thoughtful patient evaluation in medical diagnosis. This was held alongside Medcon 2026, a national conference on movement disorders. The event was organised by the Padma Shri Prof. K. V. Thiruvengadam Centenary Celebrations Committee, under the aeges of the RVR Foundation. The oration was followed by the Prof. S. Sethuraman Memorial Oration, delivered by A. Muruganathan, former professor, The Tamil Nadu Dr. MGR Medical University and director, API Physicians Research Foundation, on ‘Blood Pressure and Movement Disorders: The Bi-directional Link’. About 300 medical professionals participated in the conference, said V. Ramachandra, scientific chairman of the conference. Other sessions included talks on the basal ganglia, radiodiagnosis in movement disorders, managing early Parkinsonism, management of advanced Parkinsonism and surgeries and their effect on movement disorders. a9300ec6c74c318c.title: Two arrested for attempting to determine sex of foetus in Tirupattur
a9300ec6c74c318c.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:38 am IST - TIRUPATTUR Two persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur district on Saturday for conducting a sex determination test and attempting abortion of a foetus. Police identified the arrested persons as K. Indrarani, 60, and S. Geetha, 45. They are residents of Chittoor district in Andhra Pradesh. Initial inquiry revealed that V. Jagadeesan, 34, and his wife J. Pavithra, 28, both wage labourers, have two daughters. As Pavithra became pregnant again, the couple reportedly got in touch with Indrarani and Geetha through agents to conduct a sex determination test, and found that the fetus was a girl. As the couple did not want a third girl child, they allegedly sought help from Indrarani and Geetha to abort the foetus. Subsequently, the accused came to Jagadeesan’s house in Girisamudiram village on Saturday. Based on a tip-off, a team of health officials led by N. Kalu Sivalingam, District Health Officer (DHO) and S. Aravind, health officer, inspected the house and found medical equipment. Police said, along with police personnel from Vaniyambadi Taluk, the team conducted an inquiry with the suspects, who confessed that they were roped in by the couple to abort the foetus. Police said a case was registered under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971. Later, two suspects were lodged at a sub-jail in Tirupattur town. Further probe is under way. 503a66fb1ea7f878.title: CM approves 2,345 additional posts in Delhi Fire Services
503a66fb1ea7f878.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:33 am IST Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has approved the creation of 2,345 additional posts across various categories in the Delhi Fire Services (DFS), strengthening Delhi’s firefighting and emergency rescue services, the CM’s Office (CMO) said on Saturday. The Chief Minister said it was essential to strengthen the fire service in line with the city’s growing needs to ensure the safety of Delhi’s residents and save lives. Under the restructuring, the number of posts will be increased across various ranks and categories, including Deputy Chief Fire Officer, Divisional Officer, Assistant Divisional Officer, Station Officer, Sub-Officer, Leading Fireman, Fire Operator, Peon and Gardener, as per the CMO. “This will increase the availability of personnel at every level, from senior supervisory positions to frontline staff engaged in firefighting and rescue operations. It will also help streamline the department’s organisational structure, ensure better discharge of responsibilities at different levels and improve its efficiency during emergencies,” the CMO said in a statement. Ms. Gupta said that Delhi’s rapidly growing population, expanding urban areas, densely populated settlements, high-rise buildings, industrial establishments and complex infrastructure were creating new challenges for firefighting and emergency services. “Every minute matters in the event of a fire or any other disaster. Adequately trained manpower, a strong leadership structure and the ability to respond quickly play a decisive role in protecting people and their property,” she said. e9ec351dddf4cdf9.title: Devotees worried over conduct of Kandasashti festival at Kandakottam temple
e9ec351dddf4cdf9.summary: Updated - November 01, 2026 01:35 am IST - CHENNAI Devotees of the Sri Muthukumaraswamy Temple, popularly known as Kandhakottam in Rattan Bazaar in Park Town, are worried about the conduct of the Kandasashti festival this year. "Usually, tickets for the Laksharcharnai during the annual festival are sold just after Vijayadasami. Till date, the administration has not started selling tickets. Every year around 35,000 tickets each priced at ₹300 are sold to devotees who want to participate in the archanai that is slated to start on November 10. There is no sign of the conduct of the festival so far," said A. B. Srinivasan, a 65-year-old devotee. Saravanan, another devotee, said that this year would be the 99 th consecutive year of the Kandasashti festival during which grand concerts would be held. "Participants of the archanai would be given prasadam, including a bucket. Tenders for procuring various items, such as pandals, coconuts, bags, and flowers are yet to be called for. We hear that the executive officer has gone on leave and another person has taken charge," he said. The over 500-year-old shrine, is a scheme temple, meaning it belongs to a particular community — in this case, the Berri Chettis. A five-member team was chosen from the community as trustees last year and they have also been in charge of the daily administration of the temple. "He has gone to the bank and taken signatory powers without informing us. We seem to have absolutely no powers in the day-to-day running of the temple. The court had directed the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department to interfere only if there was any problem relating to the conduct of the temple. 398c7ff5a8c2a714.title: Cab driver arrested for abusing elderly woman and throwing her luggage on road
398c7ff5a8c2a714.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:51 am IST - CHENNAI A 37-year-old cab driver was arrested for abusing and threatening an elderly woman and throwing her luggage on the road after a dispute over the fare in Elephant Gate. According to the police, Shreyas, 21, a college student residing on Thirupalli Street in Sowcarpet, lodged a complaint with the Elephant Gate police station. According to his complaint, on October 28, his uncle, aunt and grandmother booked a cab through a private taxi app to travel from Chromepet to Sowcarpet. His uncle and aunt got down at Elephant Gate, while his grandmother asked the driver to drop her off at their house on Thirupalli Street. However, the driver allegedly dropped her about 200 metres from the house. When the fare displayed on his mobile phone was ₹488, the driver demanded more money. Even after the woman paid him ₹500, he allegedly threw her luggage on the road, verbally abused her, and threatened to kill her before leaving the spot. Based on Shreyas’s complaint, the Elephant Gate police registered a case under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act, and launched an investigation. The police arrested Mohammed Shahjahan, a native of Papanasam in Thanjavur district. 04172c2e83a2497a.title: Sinkhole at Kolathur due to Chennai Metro Rail’s tunnelling work
04172c2e83a2497a.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:42 am IST - CHENNAI An autorickshaw partly fell into a sink hole at Srinivasa Nagar in Kolathur due to Chennai Metro Rail’s tunnelling work for the phase II project on Saturday night. According to officials of Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL), around 8.30 p.m., a stationary autorickshaw partially slipped in as a sink hole occurred. Since the driver was not inside the autorickshaw, no one was injured in the incident. Tunnelling work has been under way in this location to build an underground network as part of corridor 5 (Madhavaram to Sholinganallur via Kolathur) for the Phase II project. “The workers poured concrete and have carried out repair work at the location. This could have happened due to settlement from the tunnelling work,” an official said. 6b4c9c8ff29a02f3.title: Isro's GSLV successfully places NVS-03 satellite into 'designated' orbit
6b4c9c8ff29a02f3.summary: India's independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday as ISRO successfully launched its navigation satellite NVS-03, which was placed into the designated injection orbit by a GSLV rocket. The second-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 with indigenous and procured atomic clocks has a wide array of applications including civilian use like real time tracking of trains, vehicles, and shipping vessels. Further, the NavIC constellation is an important component of the 'one nation, one time' project, ISRO chief V Narayanan said after the successful mission launch. The NVS-03 satellite is all set to complement three other navigational satellites in operation including the NVS-01 and it will strengthen infrastructure for a robust IST with the government recently notifying the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026. 84c2008d60e1c7c2.summary: Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL), the country's largest city gas distributor, reported a sharp 93.5 per cent decline in standalone net profit for the September quarter as a substantial increase in input gas costs eroded margins, offsetting higher sales volumes and revenue. Net profit fell to Rs 24.38 crore in the second quarter of 2026-27 from Rs 372.51 crore a year earlier, despite an 8 per cent increase in sales volumes and a 26 per cent jump in gross turnover. The company said its average daily gas sales crossed the 10 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) mark for the first time, rising to 10.06 mmscmd in the July-September period from 9.31 mmscmd in the corresponding period last year. Gross sales turnover increased to Rs 5,999.13 crore from Rs 4,431.63 crore, reflecting higher sales as well as the impact of increased gas prices. Prior to this appointment, Nayak held the position of Executive Director (Finance) at REC Ltd. Nayak has over three decades of rich and diverse experience, the statement said. He has served as Chief Financial Officer of erstwhile REC Transmission Projects Company Limited, a subsidiary of REC. His experience spans over the power sector and resource-intensive industries, including mining and metals. He also brings substantial expertise in domestic and international resource mobilisation, strategic treasury management, corporate finance, taxation and legal affairs, project appraisal and monitoring, lending operations, loan recovery, and stressed asset management. Nayak holds a Master's degree in .

b4d11997adf86a36.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
b4d11997adf86a36.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:06 am IST Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation , during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams , that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse. Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. f96ca61442a25a78.title: Japan’s Omron Healthcare opens first India manufacturing facility near Chennai
f96ca61442a25a78.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:09 am IST - CHENNAI Japan’s Omron Healthcare on Friday formally inaugurated its first India production facility in Gummidipoondi near Chennai. The new unit, spread over an area of 258,333 square feet at Origins by Mahindra industrial estate in Puduvoyal, has been built within three years of the Japanese firm signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government in 2023. Designed to produce about 300,000 blood pressure monitors annually, the company plans to increase its production capacity tenfold to make 30 lakh units annually in the next two years. Omron will manufacture three models of blood pressure monitors at the new facility. The firm is also looking at exporting blood pressure monitors manufactured at the new factory to the European market by next year. “We plan to make Chennai a base not just for the Indian market but also develop it as a base for exports,” Ayumu Okada, president and CEO, Omron Healthcare Company Limited, said. Muneo Takahashi, Consul General of Japan in Chennai said: “Tamil Nadu has become an important destination for Japanese investment, supported by its strong industrial base, skilled human resources and excellent infrastructure.” Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guidance said: “In 1972, Omron‘s founder joined hands with Dr. Yutaka Nakamura — a doctor known as the father of Japan’s Paralympic movement — to open Omron Taiyo in Beppu. It was Japan’s first welfare factory run and staffed by people with disabilities. People called it “the factory with wheelchairs.” And a second such factory followed in Kyoto in 1985.” Omron‘s commitment to employing persons with disabilities in this plant (Chennai) reflects exactly that value. It will inspire industries across our State to see ability first, he added. Nagaprasanna says that the court will pass orders on head of the SIT by considering the names of four senior officers suggested by the State government in terms of the order passed by the apex court on an appeal filed by the government. The State government on Friday issued a notification declaring the Special Investigation Team (SIT), which has been constituted by the High Court of Karnataka to probe cases related to alleged irregularity and corruption in recruitment process in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), to be a police station under Section 2(1)(u) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). c1472de631cd1612.title: Heavy polling in second phase panchayat elections for Sarpanch, Ward Panch in Rajasthan
c1472de631cd1612.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:25 am IST - JAIPUR Women voters walk towards a polling station to cast their votes during the second phase of the Panchayat elections (Sarpanch) in Ajmer. | Photo Credit: ANI A heavy polling took place in the second phase of village panchayat elections for Sarpanch and Ward Panch in 22 districts of Rajasthan on Friday (October 30, 2026). While 45 Sarpanches were earlier elected unopposed, as many as 3,626 village panchayats went to polls and 1.06 crore voters exercised their franchise. The highest voter turnout was recorded at 84.37% in Jaipur district’s Rampura Dabri. Voters arrived at polling booths in large numbers, enthusiastically, with elderly people and women seen standing in queues to exercise their right to vote. People turned up to vote despite light rain and drizzle at places such as Kotputli-Behror, situated on the Jaipur-Delhi national highway, and the Malakhera area in Alwar district. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended, while the results were expected to be declared by late night. Residents of Karanpur village in Dausa district’s Mahwa area boycotted polling in protest against the delimitation exercise, while the villagers at Dausa’s Pyara Ka Nagla and Jalore’s Bawatra and Dayalpur did not turn up for voting in protest against the change of their panchayats. Rajasthan gram panchayat polls: second phase held amid reports of minor clashes, protests Rival groups of villagers in Kotputli-Behror’s Majra Aheer and Jodhpur’s Sangariya Phata clashed over allegations of bogus voting. Police intervened at both places and brought the situation under control. 0c619ef70855dd06.title: Delhi BLOs to record reasons for removing names of eligible voters
0c619ef70855dd06.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:30 am IST - NEW DELHI Details of an elector being recorded at a special camp in New Delhi. | Photo Credit: SUSHIL KUMAR VERMA Booth Level Officers (BLOs) in Delhi have been asked to record why eligible electors were earlier marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD), and why those traced during re-verification are unwilling to submit Form 6 to get their names back on the rolls as new voters, The Hindu has learnt. The instructions come amid the ongoing re-verification of 47.56 lakh names dropped from the draft roll published on August 31 after being placed in the ASDD categories. On Thursday, the Election Commission of India (ECI) pushed the deadline for publishing Delhi’s final electoral roll to December 22, marking the fourth such revision. As per the revised schedule, the deadline for filing claims and objections has been extended by 26 days, from October 30 to November 25, giving eligible electors more time to seek inclusion in the final roll during the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) drive. The disposal of claims and objections will have to be completed by December 15. A new ‘Remarks’ column has been added to the BLO mobile application to record details of the re-verification exercise. This field will be used to record why an elector was placed in the ASDD categories during the enumeration phase, whether the person was found residing at the registered address and, if eligible, why the person was reluctant to submit Form 6. The column will also be used to record cases in which an elector is found at the registered address but has already enrolled in another constituency. BLOs have been provided with the ASDD lists, along with the corresponding addresses, and instructed to conduct door-to-door visits to verify the voters’ details. 60f4661931bde0bf.title: Keralam Chief Minister calls for protecting Vembanad lake system
60f4661931bde0bf.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan releases B. Madhusoodana Kurup’s book, ‘Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of South India’, by handing over copies to former Fisheries ministers K. Babu and S. Sarma at a function held in Kochi on Friday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has called for steps to protect the ecology of the Vembanad lake system, which has come under severe stress due to a host of factors including climate change. Mr. Satheesan was speaking at a commemorative function organised here to pay tributes to noted fisheries expert B. Madhusoodana Kurup who passed away recently. Kurup, who co-authored the book, ‘Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of South India,’ with Sileesh Mullasseri, had brought out issues facing the lake ecosystem, which has shrunk to 10,000 sq. km. from its original extent of 40,000 sq. km. Anthropogenic activities and impacts of climate change have adversely affected the lake system, which is spread over three districts of the State and sustains the lives of millions. He had also put forth a series of projects for the revival and protection of the lake, Mr. Satheesan said. The Chief Minister suggested setting up a chair at the Kerala University for Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos) in Kurup’s name to take forward the academic and research activities initiated by him. Kurup was the founding Vice-Chancellor of the university. Mr. Satheesan released the book by handing over copies to K. Babu and S. Sarma, former Fisheries ministers. Fisheries Minister V.E. Abdul Gafoor presided. Mayor V.K. Minimol, T.J. Vinod and Mohammed Shiyas, MLAs; K.V.P. Krishnakumar, councillor, Kochi Corporation; A. Bijukumar, Vice-Chancellor, Kufos; M. Junaid Bushiri, Vice-Chancellor, Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat); and P.C. Hari Govind, Registrar, Cusat, spoke. Publish

05beb36896da58a1.title: Fiscal deficit rises to ₹7.14 trillion or 42.1% of FY27 target in first six months
05beb36896da58a1.summary: New Delhi: India's fiscal deficit widened in the first six months of FY27, as capital spending and subsidy outlays continued to rise. Fiscal deficit, or the gap between government expenditure and receipts, stood at ₹ 7.14 trillion at the end of September, latest data from the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) showed. This amounts to 42.1% of the full-year budget estimate, higher than 36.5% in the corresponding period of the previous year. At the end of August, the fiscal deficit had stood at 41.9% of the annual target. The higher proportion of the budgeted fiscal deficit already incurred in the first half of FY27 indicates mounting pressure on the government's fiscal balance, with expenditure growing faster than the pace of deficit accumulation seen in the year-ago period. The Centre has budgeted a fiscal deficit of ₹ 16.96 trillion, or 4.3% of GDP, for FY27. It is relying on robust tax collections and higher non-tax revenues in the coming months to meet this target. The fiscal deficit is typically financed through borrowings. The widening gap assumes significance as the government has cut its FY27 market borrowing by nearly ₹ 1.2 trillion and now plans to raise ₹ 7.86 trillion through dated government securities in the second half of the fiscal year, as Mint reported on 25 September. The Centre now expects to borrow ₹ 15.995 trillion through dated securities during FY27, compared with ₹ 17.2 trillion estimated in the Union budget, according to the finance ministry 's borrowing plan released in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on 25 September. “The impact of higher subsidy outgo as well as front-loading of capex has led to a much higher H1 fiscal deficit compared to previous fiscal year, with the increase being 4.6 percentage points. f0b2416c0355ccd3.title: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood damages roads, washes away bridge in Bhutan
f0b2416c0355ccd3.summary: Updated - October 31, 2026 03:06 am IST - GELEPHU (BHUTAN) A road blocked with mud and debris in the aftermath of a flood, in Punakha, Bhutan. | Photo Credit: Reuters GELEPHU (BHUTAN) A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in Shintapu Tsho in the Laya area of northwestern Bhutan’s Gasa district on Thursday night (October 29, 2026) triggered flooding along the Mochhu, damaging roads, bridges and public infrastructure in two districts. Officials on Friday (October 30, 2026) said no human casualties have been reported, but there are growing concerns over a large artificial lake formed near Taktsemakhang, about 2,000 feet downstream of Laya. The accumulation of water at the confluence of the flood-affected channels of Mochhu (river) has raised fears of another sudden outburst, which could be disastrous for downstream areas. Officials said they could not immediately assess the GLOF impact on Thursday night (October 29, 2026). Royal Bhutan Army personnel stationed at Taktsemakhang and people near Gasa Tshachu, a hot spring, were instructed to evacuate to a safer location. “Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay is in Laya to assess the artificial lake at Taktesakhang, while Industry, Commerce and Employment Minister Namgyel Dorji is monitoring the situation in Punakha,” a Department of Local Governance and Disaster Management official said. Punakha and Thimphu districts are south of Gasa, which borders the Tibetan Autonomous Region. These and other neighbouring districts were put on high alert for potential danger from the GLOF-induced artificial lake. According to disaster management officials, Gasa Tsachu, one of Bhutan’s popular hot spring destinations, suffered extensive damage due to Thursday’s (October 29, 2026) GLOF. Floodwaters washed away almost all public facilities in the area. 2bb490adffdd451a.title: High Court directs BU to collect charges from autonomous colleges only within parameters of UGC regulations
2bb490adffdd451a.summary: Updated - October 31, 2026 07:01 am IST - COIMBATORE Image used for representational purposes only | Photo Credit: The Hindu Bharathiar University was directed by the Madras High Court on Thursday, through an interim order, to collect charges from autonomous colleges only within the parameters of UGC regulations. 8fe951e2cb488efa.title: Man sets house ablaze; firefighter injured in cylinder blast
8fe951e2cb488efa.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:45 am IST A 30-year-old man, described as an alcoholic, allegedly set his house on fire in northwest Delhi’s Jahangirpuri on Friday, triggering a massive blaze in which an LPG cylinder exploded and a firefighter sustained 25% burn injuries, police said. The police received a PCR call at 11.26 a.m. about a fire on the ground floor of a house in Jahangirpuri. Bharat (30), who lived with his mother, Raj Rani, allegedly set the house on fire. His mother was also present at the house when the incident occurred, the police said. While the fire brigade team was engaged in extinguishing the blaze, an LPG cylinder exploded, injuring Ankit (32), an Assistant Fire Officer with the Delhi Fire Service. He sustained burns to his face, hair and both hands, the police said. Ankit was initially taken to Babu Jagjivan Ram Memorial Hospital, where his injuries were assessed at around 25% burns. He was subsequently referred to the burn ward of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences for further treatment. Fire department officers said the blaze involved household articles and an LPG cylinder on the ground floor of the three-storey building. The police have registered an FIR against Bharat under Section 36(g) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for mischief by fire. Further investigation is under way. 223fe5e935582c5d.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:09 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM District Collector and District Election Officer M. Abhishikth Kishore on Friday issued a series of directions and appeals ahead of the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections, with polling scheduled to be held from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Sunday. The 120 wards have 18,37,901 voters and 1,990 polling stations, of which 1,581 are in government buildings and 409 in private ones. Of these polling stations, 104 have been classified as sensitive and 570 as hyper-sensitive; none is critical. The arrangements include 14,334 polling personnel, 201 routes, 61 sectors, 10 distribution centres, and 4,378 ballot boxes. Reviewing the distribution centre on a technical college campus at P.M. Palem, Mr. Kishore directed officials to finish preparations well in advance and plan an orderly issue of material. Material for each station is to be sorted beforehand with identification labels, and the checklist is to be verified at the time of issue. With campaigning having ended at 5 p.m., he reminded parties, candidates, and agents that the silent period is in force. Public meetings, rallies, processions, and campaigning through loudspeakers or on social media in violation of the rules are prohibited. Political functionaries and party workers who are not voters in the GVMC limits must leave the city, and the police will check hotels, lodges, guest houses, and kalyana mandapams. Liquor outlets will be closed, and distribution of cash, liquor, or gifts to voters will invite legal action. The Collector urged every voter to carry one of the 12 identity documents prescribed by the State Election Commission. Voters will be given a pink ballot paper for the mayoral candidate and a white one for the corporator, and both are to be dropped in a single box. 74f97baf653e9aa4.title: Environmentalists express ‘serious concerns’ over Yamuna riverfront project
74f97baf653e9aa4.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:30 am IST A former Union Ministry Secretary and other environmentalists on Friday wrote to Union Jal Shakti Minister C. R. Patil and others, raising “serious concerns” over the proposed riverfront development project along the Yamuna in Delhi. They urged the authorities to ensure that no project compromises the integrity of the river, its floodplain and the national capital’s long-term flood security. The letter said several media reports over the past week had quoted Water Minister Pravesh Sahib Singh as announcing the initiation of the process for an MoU with the Sabarmati Riverfront Development Corporation Limited (SRFDCL) for a Sabarmati-style riverfront development project along the Yamuna in Delhi. “We wish to underline that replication of a Sabarmati-like riverfront development plan cannot resolve the crisis of Yamuna pollution, floodplain mismanagement and flood threats; it will only worsen the situation. The Government first needs a scientifically sound plan to restore the river’s environmental flows, reduce pollution load, protect its floodplain and understand the causes of its changing flood behaviour,” the letter said. The letter was signed by Shashi Shekhar, former Secretary at the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation; Bhim Singh Rawat of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP); environmental activist Bhavreen Kandhari; and others. The signatories urged the Central government Ministries concerned and the Delhi government to ensure that no project compromises the Yamuna’s integrity, its floodplain and the national capital’s long-term flood security. “Public resources should be directed towards addressing the causes of the river’s degradation and flood risks, rather than undertaking large-scale riverfront development plan,” the letter said. 17f0ee319a7537c7.title: TNUHDB identifies 20 sites for reconstruction across State; appeals to residents of dilapidated tenements to vacate
17f0ee319a7537c7.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:17 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board (TNUHDB) has identified 20 locations across the State for reconstruction of ageing tenements during 2026-27 and plans to build greenfield resettlement sites in Perambur and Madurantakam. TNUHDB Chairperson Ku. Pa. Krishnan, in an interaction with journalists on Friday, said that the reconstruction projects involve demolishing existing ageing tenements and constructing new housing units at the same locations. Residents can return after the work is completed. The Board has identified a total of 70 sites for reconstruction across the State, which will be taken up in phases, he said. The TNUHDB also appealed to residents of 23 dilapidated sites to temporarily vacate their houses in view of the ongoing northeast monsoon. Of the 23 tenements identified in its safety advisory, 14 fell within the locations proposed for reconstruction this year, for which a Government Order is to be issued in the coming week. The remaining nine have been additionally prioritised for safety during the monsoon in view of their dilapidated condition. The 23 tenements include Srinivasapuram, V.O.C. Nagar, Old Block Vyasarpadi, Nagooran Thottam, Annathai Kuppam, Nallankuppam (Old), N.V.N. Nagar (Phase-II), West Cemetery Road, Pallakumaniyam and Kabali Thottam, and Rukmani Nagar. Mr. Krishnan said the Board was willing to undertake reconstruction of structurally weak buildings but residents’ cooperation in vacating the premises was essential. Citing Srinivasapuram, where tenements constructed in the 1970s had deteriorated over the years, he said the Board was ready to rebuild the houses and hand them back to the residents. Two new settlement sites will come up in Perambur and Madurantakam, with Mullai Nagar identified as the location for the Perambur project. Both projects are expected to have over 450 housing units. A G.O. will be issued in the coming weeks, said Ramana Saraswathi, Managing Director

f77cd49b7d46836b.title: Probe into synagogue arson in Keralam’s Kochi intensified: Chennithala
f77cd49b7d46836b.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 07:00 am IST Central agencies are currently gathering information related to the case. The probe into the alleged synagogue arson case has been intensified by constituting a special investigation team (SIT) under the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Ernakulam Central, in accordance with the directions of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (Kochi City), Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said. He was replying to a submission on the matter raised in the Assembly by T.J. Vinod, MLA. Mr. Chennithala said the Ernakulam Central Police had registered a case under Section 326(g) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita against Ebin B. Paul, a native of Ikkaranad. The Minister further said that Sections 15 and 16 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) had also been added to the case after investigators obtained information suggesting possible extremist links of the accused. Central agencies are currently gathering information related to the case. c2e2ddbb5421332d.title: Future Group's Biyani brothers face lenders' ₹800 crore recovery push
c2e2ddbb5421332d.summary: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. The Delhi High Court has sought details of assets held by Future Group promoters Kishore Biyani and his brother Rakesh Biyani as lenders move to recover nearly ₹ 800 crore in dues linked to personal guarantees given for loans to group companies. A bench of Justice Vinod Kumar on Friday issued notices to the brothers and directed them to file affidavits disclosing their assets, including bank accounts and shareholdings, within a week. The court will hear the matter next on 19 November. The petitions have been filed by Catalyst Trusteeship Ltd and Phoenix ARC Ltd under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The lenders have sought directions requiring the promoters to disclose their assets and financial interests, furnish security for the outstanding amounts and refrain from selling or transferring assets that could affect recovery. They have also sought details of the brothers' personal and beneficial assets, including bank accounts, investments, securities and interests in companies and limited liability partnerships (LLPs). The lenders have expressed concerns that assets could be transferred or disposed of before their claims are resolved. The dispute involving Kishore Biyani dates back to December 2017, when L&T Finance extended loans totalling ₹ 375 crore to Future Entertainment Pvt Ltd, backed by his personal guarantee. After the Covid-19 pandemic hit the company's business, the loans were restructured in June 2021 to around ₹ 262.2 crore, with Biyani providing a fresh personal guarantee. The lenders allege that a promised investment of ₹ 250 crore by Future Brands Ltd in Future Entertainment was never made. They also claim that insolvency proceedings against another Future Group company triggered a default under the loan agreement. 9fee95d175e27217.title: ‘Show me one Muslim minister at Centre, BJP-ruled States’: J&K Deputy CM
9fee95d175e27217.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 01:50 am IST - Srinagar J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary. File | Photo Credit: Imran Nissar As the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) launched a meme war at the ruling National Conference (NC) over recent Cabinet expansion and protests within the party, J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Thursday (October 29, 2026) said the BJP, “which has no Muslim minister in the Centre or BJP-ruled States, has no right to criticise the NC”. The BJP’s official handle on Instagram, with 338K followers, in J&K released a series of memes, showing J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah fighting own MLAs like Mubarak Gul and Abdul Majeed Bhat Larmi by editing the shots from gory Bobby Deol-starrer movie ‘Animal’. In another meme, the BJP edited characters from the comedy drama ‘Panchayat’ to show the heartburn the Cabinet expansion caused within the NC legislators, saying “endgame of the NC begins now”. Countering the criticism and BJP spokesman Sunil Sethi’s description of “National Conference as Muslim Conference” over dropping a Hindu minister, Deputy CM Choudhary asked the BJP to identify one Muslim minister in the BJP Cabinet. “Is there any Muslim who is a minister at the Centre or BJP-ruled States in the country. If it is about ‘Sab Ka Sath, Sab Ka Vikas’, why is there no Muslim minister in the BJP?. The party spokesman has no right point fingers at the NC,” said Mr. Choudhary. The J&K Deputy CM also objected to BJP criticism over no Hindu representation in the Omar Abdullah cabinet. “I am a Jat from Rajouri’s Nowshera. Am I not a Hindu or Sanathani? Whatever I have become is because of Maa Vaishno and Maa Durga. The BJP needs to clarify if Jatts qualify to be Hindus or not. It should also tell us which ‘baradari’ are Hindus in J&K,” said Mr. Choudhary. J&K witnessed a Cabinet expansion on October 27, with four new faces joining the Omar Abdullah cabinet. 59026cdb53592953.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 05:48 am IST - Srinagar The elections to District Bar Association Anantnag in south Kashmir held on October 27 has been declared “null and void” by the District Magistrate over alleged “violations of official orders and non-fulfilment of mandatory requirements”. In an order, the District Magistrate said these elections “have been conducted in blatant violation of the orders, without fulfilment of the prerequisite conditions, without any intimation to this office and without any permission from this office”. “The election has been conducted in violation of the provisions of Societies Registration Act 1860 (As applicable in Jammu and Kashmir) and Indian Trust Act 1882. The elections conducted by the organisation operating under the name and style of District Bar Association Anantnag, held on 27-10-2026, are hereby declared null and void, ab initio and non-est in the eyes of law,” reads the order. It also mentioned that the election process of the District Bar Association, Anantnag, was prohibited under order Dated 02-01-2025 until “submission of Certificate of Registration; Constitution or Memorandum of Association of the organisation; bye-laws governing the functioning of the organisation; list of current executive members and members of previous 10 years, including their full names, designations, permanent residential addresses, and actives mobile contact numbers and detailed account statements along with a summary of financial transactions and any relevant banking details. Around 700 lawyers are enrolled in the Bar in Anantnag. The elections were held for the posts of president and secretary. “These elections were held after proper permission and observation of the authorities. It’s wrong to term these elections illegal,” said a senior lawyer, on condition of anonymity. He said the District Magistrate notification came in at night. “The elections were held with the intention to benefit lawyers and maintain decorum and dignity of courts.
