0e6480d9e5de07db.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
0e6480d9e5de07db.summary: Updated - October 30, 2026 01:10 am IST At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries. Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap

42c3ff6548496dc5.title: Hike to help farmers, says CM; Ashok accuses govt. of placing burden on people
42c3ff6548496dc5.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 01:05 am IST - Bengaluru While Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar defended milk price hike by ₹8 on Thursday, saying that the decision was taken to support dairy farmers, Leader of Opposition R. Ashok accused the State government of placing an additional financial burden on the people. He also warned the Congress government of a protest. After the Cabinet meeting that approved the hike, the Chief Minister said, “The hike has been made to prevent losses to farmers.” He pointed out that input costs, price of packaging of milk, transportation have all increased in the past one year. “There was a demand to increase the price by ₹12 to ₹15. We made this decision after consulting with everyone,” he said. He also highlighted that all MLAs had demanded a milk price hike across party lines in both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council, cutting across partylines. Meanwhile, Mr. Ashok questioned whether increasing the cost of essential commodities and imposing additional taxes was the Congress government’s “guarantee to the people of Karnataka”. He said that while people were already struggling with rising prices, the government appeared focused on further burdening their pockets. 066662ee7d0b0eb3.title: Manisha Bhanwala becomes third Indian woman to reach World Wrestling Championships Final
066662ee7d0b0eb3.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 06:19 am IST - Sports Bureau Manisha Bhanwala (59kg) was the third Indian woman to enter the final at the World wrestling championships in Astana on Thursday (October 29, 2026). Manisha, who returned from the Asian Games without a medal in 57kg and jumped to the non-Olympic weight category at the Worlds, shocked World championships bronze medallist Laurence Beauregard by pinning the Canadian in the second period. Then she beat Mongolian Olympian Bolortuya Khurelkhuu 6-0 and pinned Kazakhstan’s World under-23 bronze medallist Altyn Shagayeva to reach the title clash. In the final on Friday (October 30, 2026), Manisha will face USA’s Pan-American champion Abigail Elizabeth Nette. Earlier, Neelam Sirohi (50kg) and Kajal Dhochak (76kg) secured silver medals for the country. Ahilya Shinde (55kg) was beaten 9-6 by Turkey’s Tuba Demir in the last-eight stage. In men’s freestyle, Vicky (97kg) was defeated 12-2 by Japan’s Asian champion and Worlds bronze medallist Arash Yoshida in the quarterfinals. The Indian made it to the repechage round to stay in the race for a bronze medal. Asian Games champion Sujeet Kalkal (65kg) had disappointment in store as lost 3-3 on criteria to Abdulmazhid Kudiev in the quarterfinals. Sujeet had rallied from 2-9 down to beat the Tajikistan wrestler in the Asiad final. d3b27918b25b2260.title: A security deal, but not the end of the Arctic contest
d3b27918b25b2260.summary: Updated - October 30, 2026 01:16 am IST ‘The way Denmark, the U.S. and Greenland manage this balance will shape the island’s future’ | Photo Credit: REUTERS The agreement signed between the United States, Denmark and Greenland on September 22, 2026, marks an important moment in the changing geopolitics of the Arctic. Greenland is an autonomous part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Under the 2009 Self-Government Act , it has extensive control over its domestic affairs, while foreign, defence and security policy remain with Denmark. Greenland came into the news this year because of the Trump administration’s repeated interest in gaining control over the island. What began as a territorial controversy gradually became a wider debate about sovereignty, security and the future of the Arctic. The agreement, signed at the United Nations, expands the American military presence in Greenland while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenland’s right to self-determination. It brings, at least for now, an end to the unusual tensions between Washington and Copenhagen over the future of the strategically important island. The agreement’s entry into force is subject to the completion of the necessary parliamentary procedures in Denmark and Greenland. ac34abaa11a727b9.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 01:03 am IST - VELLORE With the onset of Northeast monsoon, Vellore and Tiruvannamalai Corporations will soon install an additional 3,000 new LED street lights in these towns to ensure the safety of residents, especially at night during monsoon. Corporation officials said that a joint coordination meeting with key stakeholders, including Tangedco, the Revenue Department, police and residents’ welfare associations, was held at the civic body’s headquarters in these towns. In Vellore town, the meeting was chaired by Corporation Commissioner A. Catherine Saranya. “The meeting assumes significance as Tangedco was given adequate time before the start of heavy rains to address major complaints related to street lights,” K. Balasubramanian, Commissioner, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, told The Hindu. Some of the major complaints reported by residents to civic officials were the snapping of electrical cables that are connected to street lights in these towns due to strong winds. Another complaint was the dangling of electrical wires on key stretches during monsoon. Corporation officials requested Tangedco officials in these towns to provide a separate electrical phase from transformers in each area to operate street lights alone. “Such an arrangement (separate electrical phase) will allow working of street lights even during unscheduled power cuts during rains. In Tiruvannamalai, 13,700 street lights and 50 high mast lamps are run by the civic body. Of these, around 20 % of the total lights are run through solar power. On average, around ₹30 lakh is spent on electricity charges by each of these civic bodies every month. 63e0a48f83bad2a4.title: Ex-Mayor Bhagyalakshmi appeals to voters to give her another opportunity
63e0a48f83bad2a4.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:52 am IST - VIJAYAWADA YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) Mayoral candidate Rayana Bhagyalakshmi on Thursday appealed to voters to give her another opportunity to serve as Mayor, adding that the city had witnessed significant development during the party’s previous five-year tenure. Addressing the media in Gandhi Nagar, Ms. Bhagyalakshmi said the party was committed to accelerating urban development and remaining accessible to the public. She urged voters to elect her and the party’s corporator candidates in the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation elections. Alleging that the coalition government had failed to deliver on its promises, she questioned the development works undertaken in Vijayawada over the past three years. She claimed that the previous YSRCP government had improved water tanks, drainage systems, parks, community halls and the Ajit Singh Nagar dumping yard. She also cited the construction of a retaining wall in Krishnalanka as a major achievement. YSRCP NTR district president Devineni Avinash said Ms. Bhagyalakshmi had discharged her responsibilities as Mayor with commitment and helped the city secure awards during her tenure. He appealed to voters to support all 86 YSRCP corporator candidates. Former Minister Vellampalli Srinivasa Rao alleged that the coalition government had failed to take adequate measures to address Vijayawada’s civic problems, including flooding and drainage issues. He claimed that the previous YSRCP government had undertaken significant development works and expressed confidence that his party would win the municipal elections. 7e803788dc597d52.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
7e803788dc597d52.summary: Updated - October 30, 2026 01:02 am IST The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. 7e803788dc597d52.headline_en: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
7e803788dc597d52.raw_facts: Updated - October 30, 2026 01:02 am IST The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases. The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutor

85958afbde1720ce.title: India remains growth engine; Super El Nino impact yet to materialise: IMF
85958afbde1720ce.summary: The IMF on Thursday said the impact of weather events such as the Super El Nino was yet to materialise for India, which remains the engine of growth for the world economy. The IMF listed lower crop yields, increased food price inflation and its impact on the purchasing power of households in India due to the Super El Nino. "So these are risks that we see that India faces, but right now those risks have not materialised," IMF Communications Director Julie Kozack told a press conference here. She said the IMF will reassess India's growth projections in the January World Economic Outlook update after the risks posed by the weather event materialise. Earlier this month, the IMF raised India's growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7 per cent, from the 6.4 per cent and 6.7 per cent projections respectively made in July. "So, we see it really as a risk going forward, and of course depending on whether that risk materialises, we will reassess our growth projections

64348e28d88bca8d.title: Chennai Corporation considers new feasibility study for rope car project
64348e28d88bca8d.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:48 am IST - Chennai The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) is planning to prepare a fresh feasibility report for a rope car service connecting the Marina and Besant Nagar beaches, after the project was found unfeasible along the Marina Beach. At the Council meeting on Thursday, Anna Nagar councillor T.V. Shemmozhi enquired about the status of the Marina Beach rope car project, pointing out that a feasibility study, which estimated the project cost at ₹74 crore, had already been completed. Mayor R. Priya responded that the initial feasibility study had not been approved as it had raised safety concerns over potential overcrowding, and the proposal had been referred to another team for reconsideration. Mr. Shemmozhi said he had repeatedly raised the proposal since his maiden speech at the Council. He added that the rope car service could develop Chennai into a major tourist destination. Notably, on May 25, 2025, when Mr. Shemmozhi demanded that the Marina project be taken up with the government for implementation, the Mayor had said the feasibility study was under way. b45c92f6f1809c05.title: SI arrested for alleged theft of seized drug from police station
b45c92f6f1809c05.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI A sub-inspector (SI) attached to the Ernakulam Central police station was arrested for allegedly stealing suspected MDMA seized in connection with a Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) case and kept at the station. The officer was identified as Anas S. Thaufeeq, a native of Thiruvananthapuram. The Central police registered a case against him shortly after he was suspended based on a Special Branch report. He had earlier been part of the anti-drug awareness campaign conducted under ‘Operation Toofan’. He was booked under Sections 306 (Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master) and 238 (causing disappearance of evidence) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 21(c) (punishment for offences involving a commercial quantity of manufactured drugs) of the NDPS Act. The first information report was registered on a complaint by an officer in charge of the strong room at the station. Suspected drugs seized in various narcotics cases were stored in the strong room before being moved to the godown at the district headquarters camp for disposal. The accused allegedly entered the strong room without permission where a packet containing 87.37 grams of suspected MDMA seized by the Elamakkara police was being kept. The accused allegedly stole the packet and tampered with the evidence, resulting in a difference in the quantity of the drug. An investigation is under way to ascertain the motive behind the officer’s actions. The authorities are further looking into whether he received assistance from anyone else at the station. 3f04f33e57a2e858.title: A hundred years ago | Depression in cotton industry
3f04f33e57a2e858.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 04:45 am IST Bombay, Oct. 29: Representatives of the Ahmedabad Millowners’ Association were examined by the Tariff Board (Cotton Textile). Replying to the Chairman, they stated that during the last two or three weeks the condition of the textile industry had changed for the worse. Owing to the heavy drop in cotton prices, cloth merchants had lost their confidence. The purchasing power of the agriculturists was also going down and the phenomenal fall in American cotton prices had accentuated depression in the cotton industry, but did not affect textile industries of America and Japan to any extent. On the other hand, they were making profits. The drop in cotton prices during the last two or three years had been gradual, and it was admitted that the bumper cotton crop of America accentuated the depression. c63f246d28a29ff8.title: Who is Anil Menon? NASA astronaut on fourth spacewalk, ranks behind Sunita Williams among Indian-origin space walkers
c63f246d28a29ff8.summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon is undertaking his fourth career spacewalk alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The mission marks the 100th US spacewalk at the International Space Station (ISS), with the duo working to install a new roll-out solar array on the orbital laboratory. With his fourth spacewalk, Menon ranks second to veteran NASA astronaut Sunita Williams among Indian-origin astronauts by number of spacewalks. Williams has completed nine spacewalks, totalling 62 hours and six minutes. Before the October 29 mission, Menon had completed three spacewalks, accumulating 19 hours and 20 minutes. The latest mission is part of the continuing maintenance and upgrading of the ISS, where spacewalks are used to install equipment, repair systems and improve the orbital laboratory’s capabilities. Menon has a background spanning medicine, engineering, aviation and human spaceflight operations. Before joining NASA’s astronaut corps, he worked as a flight surgeon for both NASA and SpaceX, helping prepare crews for missions and develop medical systems to support astronauts in space. According to his official NASA biography, Menon was selected for the agency’s 2021 Astronaut Candidate Class and reported for duty in January 2022. He subsequently completed initial astronaut training to prepare for space missions. Menon was born and raised in Minneapolis, Minnesota, to Ukrainian and Indian immigrants. He is married to Anna Menon, and the couple have two children. NASA astronaut Anil Menon has a background spanning medicine, engineering, aviation and human spaceflight. 01b741194d692039.title: Trial Index of Services Production shows sustained momentum in August
01b741194d692039.summary: New Delhi: India’s services activity remained broad-based in August, with 17 of 19 sub-sectors recording growth and 13 posting double-digit increases, indicating sustained momentum in formal-sector services despite mixed signals from manufacturing and external trade, showed the Centre’s fifth trial Index of Services Production (ISP) on Thursday. The 19-sector index covering about 60% of the services sector provides a new monthly gauge of activity in a sector that accounts for more than half of India's economy. The overall ISP will be brought out later after studying the stability and resilience of sub-sectoral ISPs and improving the overall coverage of services, the ministry of statistics and programme implementation said in a statement. Top sub-sectors that reported continued strong growth in are accommodation and food (11.9%), retail trade (19.9%), repair services (17.6%), administrative and support services (13.1%), banking (14.9%), professional, scientific and technical services including research and development (14.2%), IT and computer -related services (13.8%) and real estate (17.6%). While rising energy prices due to the West Asia war have continued to keep air transport services growth in the negative zone at -9.6%, growth of arts, entertainment and recreational services also remained in the negative zone at -4.7%. Growth in other transport services—railways, roadways, and waterways—also remained in the single digits at 3.7%, 9.4%, and 9.5%, respectively. Postal and courier services and information and broadcasting services, which were in the negative zone in earlier months, showed sustained growth of 13.2% and 7.2%, respectively. Repair services, where growth contracted in July, also made a smart recovery, registering double-digit growth in August. While retail trade saw high double-digit growth in August, the wholesale trade growth remained relatively lower at 102%. Telecommunication, warehousing and support activities for transportation expanded by 11.8%

e0c2d90163cf612c.title: Blast in explosives godown in Vellore; three vehicles damaged
e0c2d90163cf612c.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 01:00 am IST - VELLORE The building collapsed to the ground, and three vans parked near the building were damaged. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Three vans were burnt and a calf was killed after an explosion in an explosives godown at Arjunapuram village near Gudiyatham town in Vellore on Thursday. The police said that S. Padmanaban, 42, runs a stone quarry operator in K.V. Kuppam area. He has a vast open land in Arjunapuram village where he stored raw materials to make explosives in a licensed godown in the land. The explosives are used for blasting in stone quarry units. Police said that a special police team attached with Katpadi police seized raw materials used to manufacture fire crackers from a house in Katpadi recently. The seized raw materials were stored at the private explosives godown in Arjunapuram village near Gudiyatham to prevent any untowards incidents. Around 50 kg of raw materials to manufacture explosives were stored in the godown. Police said around 2 a.m, residents heard an explosion from the godown. The building collapsed to the ground, and three vans parked near the building were damaged. Based on an alert from residents, K.V. Kuppam police and experts from the explosives unit at District Police inspected the spot. A case was registered. A probe is underway. 4eaefb546687e028.title: Students take part in stroke awareness programme
4eaefb546687e028.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:44 am IST - CHENNAI Students of Bhavan’s Rajaji Vidyashram in Chennai, formed the letters ‘FAST’, an acronym for face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty, and time to act immediately. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement Apollo Hospitals, Chennai, and Apollo Shine Foundation organised a stroke awareness programme to highlight the importance of recognising its symptoms and seeking immediate medical attention. Minister for School Education Rajmohan and P.G. Subramanian, principal, Bhavan’s Rajaji Vidyashram, Kilpauk, participated. Ilankumaran Kaliamoorthy, Chief Executive Officer, Apollo Hospitals, Chennai Region, said schools provide an opportunity to introduce important health messages to young people, who can also share them with their families. Srinivasan Paramasivam, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon, Apollo Hospitals, Greams Road, raised the need for regular health checks and appropriate management of conditions such as high blood pressure, a major risk factor for stroke. 90d34315d695cdbc.title: ACB, Food Safety and Drug Control teams inspect NIMS amid corruption allegations
90d34315d695cdbc.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:37 am IST Officials of the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), Food Safety and Drug Control departments conducted simultaneous inspections at Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Punjagutta, on Thursday following allegations of corruption and irregularities. A team of around 10 ACB officials, led by Central Investigation DSP Lakshmi Kanth Reddy, inspected records at the hospital’s administrative section as part of the probe. Meanwhile, four food safety inspectors inspected the NIMS canteen, while another team of four drug inspectors checked the surgical stores. The drug inspectors examined medicines, medical equipment and records pertaining to their storage. The food safety officials focused on the canteen, while the ACB team scrutinised administrative records in connection with the allegations of irregularities. A detailed statement from the ACB on the inspections is expected to be released on Friday. 6705c3e1d83169bc.title: SC pulls up RBI over cyberfrauds, seeks strict liability for losses
6705c3e1d83169bc.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday pulled up the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) over cyberfrauds, saying banks must compensate victims for losses when their employees are found to be involved. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant noted that digital arrest scams persisted despite public awareness campaigns, media coverage and earlier judicial directions. The court was hearing a suo motu case on the issue. The court questioned why the banks should not be held accountable for the losses suffered by their customers, when the financial institution can waive loans worth crores as a one-time settlement. “Banks can waive thousands of crores in loans by entering into so-called one-time settlements for ₹ 5 crore or ₹ 10 crore. Why should they not be accountable to these victims?” Attorney general R. Venkataramani opposed implementing such a rule, stating that the liability of banks needs to be addressed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The court’s observations came after senior advocate N.S. Nappinai, assisting the bench as amicus curiae, flagged the continued prevalence of digital arrest scams. She referred to a recent incident in which a woman allegedly lost ₹ 2.5 crore. In such scams, fraudsters impersonate police officers, government officials or judicial authorities and threaten victims with arrest to force them to transfer money. The bench also told the banks that the customers have given them access to their account details and transaction history, and they must act as a “protective umbrella” for them. They also raised the question of why banks do not take the necessary steps as soon as suspicions arise or a money-related message appears. “What we are shocked about is why people are not realizing? What is wrong with the victims? Are they not normal people? This is everywhere in the media,” the bench observed. The bench also raised issues of bank employees being involved in such frauds. India has since 2024 alleged ‌Volkswagen undervalued auto imports for years and paid below the full tariff rates. Volkswagen, which has a roughly 2% market share in the world's third biggest car market, denies the allegations, and has previously said the case is a matter of "life and death" for its India business, and is "impossibly enormous". The dispute over India's biggest ever import tax demand restarted last week ‌after the High Court in Mumbai said in August it would hear Volkswagen challenge afresh as judges failed to pass a ruling in time. "No other company has challenged this," he said. Volkswagen ​is ‌accused of declaring its imports as individual auto parts and paid 5% to 15% ‌tariff, though it was bringing in "almost the entire car" in unassembled condition for which it should have paid a 30-35% tax rate, India has alleged. 563c6e928ac6f1e1.title: West Asia conflict drives 15-20% rise in corporate working-capital demand at banks
563c6e928ac6f1e1.summary: Working-capital demand from banks has increased significantly due to the ongoing conflict in West Asia. Higher raw-material costs and elongated shipping timelines have led to greater funding needs for corporates. Mid- and large-sized companies reported a 12-20% increase in working-capital requirements. Several private sector banks have recorded strong growth in corporate lending during the recent quarter. This momentum was driven primarily by working capital needs and refinancing efforts.

0b3c624948d3e1e9.title: SFI alleges reservation violations in PhD seat intake at JNU
0b3c624948d3e1e9.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 04:35 am IST The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) on Wednesday alleged that Jawaharlal Nehru University’s (JNU) PhD Admission Prospectus 2026–27 falls short of the prescribed reservation quotas for Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST) and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD). It called on the university to rectify the shortfall in the seats advertised for the current admission cycle. Speaking at a press conference, JNUSU Vice-President Gopika Babu said that against the total regular intake of 711 PhD seats in the 2026–27 prospectus, the statutory reservation of 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes should translate into approximately 53 seats. However, only 38 seats have been advertised, a shortfall of around 15. Similarly, against the mandated 15% reservation for Scheduled Castes, approximately 107 seats should be reserved, whereas only 103 have been advertised. The discrepancy also extends to Persons with Benchmark Disabilities, for whom only 17 seats have been earmarked against a minimum requirement of approximately 36. “These figures point to serious deficiencies in the university’s implementation of reservation norms,” Ms. Babu said. The SFI said that following its complaint dated September 29, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) issued a notice to the JNU Registrar on October 8, directing the administration to submit the relevant facts and details of the action taken. After the administration failed to respond by the stipulated deadline of October 23, the Commission issued an ultimatum on October 27, asking JNU to respond or take action within seven days. The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) has also taken cognisance of the matter, the students said. “These developments expose the JNU administration’s failure to address a matter concerning the constitutional rights of students from historically marginalised communities,” the SFI said. c73a18e687ff6fe7.title: TNCC president asks Karnataka government to respect Cauvery Water Management Authority order
c73a18e687ff6fe7.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 01:00 am IST - Chennai B. Manickam Tagore | Photo Credit: B. Thamodharan Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president B. Manickam Tagore urged the Congress government in Karnataka to recognise the merit of the petition filed by the Tamil Nadu government in the Supreme Court and immediately come forward to make up the outstanding water deficit at Biligundulu in accordance with the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s order and release the full 3,000 cusecs of water daily. In a statement, Mr. Tagore said that the livelihood of Tamil Nadu’s Delta farmers should be ensured and that the Samba crops that sustains Cauvery delta farmers should be protected. The Karnataka government has a legal obligation to release without obstruction the rightful share of water to be provided to Tamil Nadu, in accordance with the order issued by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA). Although the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee and the Cauvery Water Management Authority had ordered the release of water at the rate of 3,000 cusecs per day until November 6, the shortfall of 3,851 cusecs at Biligundulu during the initial days has caused considerable fear and concern among Delta farmers, he said. He urged that all parties must fully respect and act in accordance with the Supreme Court’s judgments and the directions of the Cauvery Water Management Authority. In a letter to the President, he said that when two Election Commissioners themselves said that decisions were being taken without their knowledge and described them as unauthorised and illegal, it is clear the institution is in need of protection. He alleged that the deletion of electors in Tamil Nadu and several other States had taken place in a manner and on a scale that had skewed the results in several constituencies, weakened one political party, and strengthened another. “The Election Commission of India (ECI) built, over seven decades, a reputation that was the envy of democracies across the world. That reputation belongs to the people of India and not to any individual who holds office in it,” he said in the memorandum. He also demanded the cancellation of the SIR in its entirety in all States. 217f259f7848c873.title: Textile ministry reopens PLI scheme, halves turnover threshold to ₹100 cr
217f259f7848c873.summary: New Delhi: The textiles ministry will reopen the application portal for its production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for textiles from 1 November to 31 December, lowering the minimum turnover requirement for the scheme’s second category to ₹ 100 crore from ₹ 200 crore to widen participation of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The fourth round of applications aims to boost domestic manufacturing of man-made fibre (MMF) apparel, MMF fabrics and technical textiles, attract investments, generate employment and strengthen India’s position in global textile value chains, the ministry said in a statement on Wednesday. The ministry has also extended the scheme’s tenure until the fiscal year 2033-34 for companies approved under the fourth round. The longer timeframe is intended to give new participants greater certainty in investing in and scaling up manufacturing capacity. The government seeks to leverage its free trade agreements (FTAs) to expand exports of labour-intensive goods, including textiles and apparel, to a wider range of partner countries. Lowering the turnover threshold could bring more domestic manufacturers within the PLI scheme and help strengthen India's export competitiveness. “Reducing the turnover criteria for the textiles PLI scheme demonstrates the government's responsiveness to the ground-level realities of growing manufacturers. This step will encourage mid-sized units and proactive SMEs to invest with confidence, expand their capacities, and contribute meaningfully to the country’s manufacturing growth story,” said Vinod Kumar, president, India SME Forum. “The amendment’s success will depend on effective implementation, clear eligibility guidance, timely approvals, access to affordable finance and practical support for enterprises preparing their applications,” he added. Second, can crystallised electoral rolls be unsettled in subsequent elections by deleting names on suspicion? These questions arise in the context of the electoral rolls in Bihar, published on January 6, 2025, following the ECI’s Special Summary Revision (SSR). On June 24, 2025, the ECI decided to undertake a fresh SIR , beginning with Bihar. Thus, every electoral roll in Bihar between January 1, 2003 (the date of the last SIR in Bihar), and January 6, 2025 (the date of the last SSR, in Bihar), was, in effect, called into question by the ECI. This was unnecessary, as the ECI, in any case, periodically updates the electoral rolls efficiently. This unusual exercise effectively called into question the electoral rolls used in every election held in Bihar between 2003 and 2025. baffb8fac0b11512.title: India-New Zealand trade ties set to scale new heights

This extraordinary partnership showed what co-operation, trust and determination could achieve, and we are once again set to see the India-New Zealand partnership scale to new heights with the entry into force of the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA). The India-New Zealand relationship has always been cordial and extends beyond diplomatic ties. Their people share the same passion for cricket, place a high value on domestic traditions and share strong people-to-people ties. In fact, New Zealand is also home to a large Indian diaspora, strengthening relations between the two countries, be it in business, education or cultural exchange. The implementation of the FTA provides another opportunity to leverage these ties for a stronger economic partnership. Moreover, this FTA is among the recently signed modern FTAs of India which will strengthen its foothold and economic engagement in the Indo-Pacific. The complementary nature of the two economies will help in creating greater opportunities for both countries, not just in trade but also in investments and other areas of economic co-operation. India-New Zealand bilateral merchandise trade, which is at $1.2 billion, is way below potential. India caters to just 1.9% of New Zealand’s merchandise imports worth $47.5 billion, while China accounts for an over 22% share and Australia, the United States, South Korea and Japan together account for another 33% share. 5b156470f8e79ecb.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
5b156470f8e79ecb.summary: Updated - October 29, 2026 01:30 am IST Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments. Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. 101d47c14420a9a8.title: A hundred years ago | Japan becoming a second-rate power
101d47c14420a9a8.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 04:10 am IST New York, October 26: The newspapers here published a remarkable story sent from Brussels on the authority of highly placed diplomatic officials, according to which it is apparent that Japan is reverting to the status of a second rate power. Consequently the importance of Britain’s imperial defences is being minimised at the discussions of the Imperial Conference in London. It is emphatically stated in the reports that are published that it will be utterly impossible for Japan to regain her status owing to the serious decline in her trade, the enormous havoc wrought by the severe earthquakes that devastated Japan, the labour agitations that are menacing her powers as a manufacturing country and her financial troubles which are believed to be heavy. 0ac8682804248381.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
0ac8682804248381.summary: Updated - October 29, 2026 01:22 am IST Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics. Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. 32e02ed1cbc8803a.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 05:00 am IST Security personnel outside Jamia Millia Islamia University in New Delhi on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SUSHIL KUMAR VERMA Delhi Police on Wednesday detained two members of the National Students’ Union of India from outside the Jamia Millia Islamia campus, where public assembly has been banned under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita. The police action comes amid an ongoing hunger strike by students demanding the restoration of their students’ union, which was dissolved in 2006. NSUI identified the detained students as Faizan, president of its Jamia unit, and Zishan, a former national head of its social media wing. They were taken to Fatehpur Beri before being brought back to the Jamia Nagar police station. af122f8b40f2637a.title: Air Force Golf Course shut as Centre moves to reclaim prime land in Lutyens’ Delhi
af122f8b40f2637a.summary: Updated - October 29, 2026 06:21 am IST - New Delhi The Air Force Golf Course, which houses a sports complex, swimming pool and other recreational facilities, remained closed on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) as the Centre expedited efforts to reclaim prime land parcels in the surrounding area. A senior Defence Ministry official confirmed that a survey of the land had been completed and notices had been served. The complex will remain closed until further notice, the official said. The closure has also led to the cancellation of a farewell golfing event planned for outgoing Indian Air Force (IAF) Chief Air Marshal A.P. Singh. The event was scheduled to be held at the venue ahead of his retirement on October 31. The golf course is located in the vicinity of the Delhi Race Club and Jaipur Polo Grounds, both of which have also come under the government’s land reclamation drive. The Land and Development Office (L&DO), under the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), has been seeking to reclaim prime land parcels near the Prime Minister’s official residence that were earlier leased out or allegedly encroached upon. In August, the department evicted the Delhi Race Club from its 53-acre premises on Lok Kalyan Marg, citing the requirement of the land for an unspecified public purpose. It also reclaimed the Jaipur Polo Ground from the India Polo Association, citing broader public purposes, governance and defence infrastructure projects. The department has additionally initiated eviction proceedings against the Delhi Gymkhana Club to reclaim its 27-acre premises, citing the requirement of land for defence infrastructure. bbb79f4520b1f420.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 01:00 am IST The lawyers were protesting over the alleged mistreatment of their colleague by Justice Ajay Bhanot of the Allahabad HC. | Photo Credit: video grab Chaos erupted in one of the courtrooms at the Allahabad High Court on Wednesday as protests against a judge escalated, with advocates allegedly throwing furniture towards the dais. The conduct of the lawyers prompted the court to consider disciplinary and contempt proceedings against those involved. A Bench of Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal was hearing a bail application when slogans and commotion from the adjoining corridor interrupted the proceedings. After being informed that the lawyers were protesting over the alleged mistreatment of their colleague, the judge expressed concern over the disruption caused to litigants and the functioning of the court. The protest reportedly stemmed from allegations that a lawyer had been mistreated by Justice Ajay Bhanot. Terming the conduct of the lawyers as “wholly unjustified” and “contemptuous”, the Bench observed that litigants approach the court seeking judicial relief and should not suffer because of disagreements between lawyers and a particular judge. “Registrar (Protocol) is directed to get the CCTV footage of camera installed outside of Court No.66, identify the advocates involved in the incident and submit a report to this court by next date of listing. After identifying the advocates, the matter may be referred to the Bar Council of U.P. for initiation of disciplinary proceedings as well as initiation of contempt proceedings against them,” Justice Deshwal ordered. bf5fd2ef65548963.title: 20 units of illegally mined sand near Ambur seized
bf5fd2ef65548963.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 01:02 am IST - TIRUPATTUR Mounds of mined sand in Machampattu village on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement More than 20 units of river sand that was illegally mined from the dry Malattaru River was found at Machampattu village on Wednesday. Revenue officials said that based on information from farmer and social activist J. Paranthaman, a team of revenue officials and the police inspected a private open land near the river, where huge quantities of river sand were stored in the open. “Based on preliminary assessment, we have found over 20 units of river sand illegally kept in the private land. We have sealed the premises for further inspection by the Water Resources Department (WRD) team, for public auction of the seized sand,” S. Devi, Tasildar (Pernambut), told The Hindu. A farming village, Machampattu forms part of Pernambut Panchayat Union in Vellore district. Most of the farmers depend on the river for domestic consumption and irrigation purposes. “Over the years, illegal sand mining has turned the perennial river into a seasonal waterbody. Illegal sand mining in the river also depleted groundwater in surrounding farming villages,” Mr. Paranthaman said. Along with the local police, revenue officials led by tahsildar Devi had inspected the site where they found a large quantity of river sand stored in the open. Revenue officials said that as per norms, mining of river sand, including for government purposes like construction of school buildings and Anganwadi centres, is prohibited in the State. For government infrastructure works, sand could be procured at designated government sand quarries in the district. Revenue officials said that the revenue earned in the public auction will go to the State exchequer. Legal action will also be taken on the landowner, identified as Navin, for illegal mining of river sand. A probe is under way. 9790e23ee54fad38.title: Persons with disabilities can now travel for free in government buses with UDID card
9790e23ee54fad38.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 12:58 am IST - Chennai Persons with disabilities and their companion can now travel free of charge in government buses with their Unique Identification Card (UDID). The Welfare of Differently Abled department issued a government order for persons with disability with over 40% disability to travel n the city ordinary, express buses, low-floor buses, deluxe buses excluding air-conditioned buses of the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations and in the ordinary fare buses excluding air-conditioned buses of the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations in the suburban (Mofussil) and hilly areas. It comes into force from October 28. This had been a long pending demand of various disability associations for free travel in buses. The order further noted that the current bus travel concessions for persons with disability including the 75% travel concession, will continue as usual. “The free bus travel concession card obtained in the financial year 2026-2027 will not be valid when this scheme is implemented. The bus operator should issue a free travel ticket to them when they travel,” the order stated. The announcement of the scheme was made in the State Budget in the Legislative Assembly in August, 2026. The Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Minister K. Jegadeshwari expanded it to persons with disabilities and their companions with a UDID card. Welcoming the move Nethrodaya founder C. Govindakrishnan said, “We can now travel in all these buses without a pass and with just a UDID card. We are thankful to the Chief Minister for the initiative.” The Hindu published an article on the issue on October 25, 2026. 138d27b4a389e14e.title: Delhi L-G, Mandaviya inaugurate inter-university sports cup
138d27b4a389e14e.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 04:30 am IST The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) and several government universities have joined hands to organise an inter-university sports tournament featuring five disciplines, following an initiative by Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu to promote team sports among students, according to a release from Lok Niwas on Wednesday. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya, Mr. Sandhu and Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood inaugurated the DDA-University Sports Cup 2026 at Roshanara Club on Tuesday. Organised by Delhi Technological University (DTU) in collaboration with the DDA, the tournament is being held at the DTU Sports Complex from October 28 to November 2, the release stated. According to Lok Niwas, students will compete in men’s and women’s categories in hockey, football, kabaddi, basketball and cricket. The participating universities include DTU, Netaji Subhas University of Technology, Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi, Indira Gandhi Delhi Technical University for Women, Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University, Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, Ambedkar University Delhi, Delhi Teachers University, and Delhi Sports University. Addressing students and athletes at the inauguration, Mr. Mandaviya described the initiative as “a significant step towards building a culture of sports and fitness among the youth” and urged young sportspersons to pursue excellence with discipline. He also referred to India’s ambition to host the 2036 Olympics and its successful bid to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030. Mr. Sandhu said, “The tournament will bring Delhi’s universities together on a common platform and encourage sportsmanship and team spirit. As the Prime Minister has said, sports teach us not only to become champions, but also to become better competitors. Sports are an important part of education, teaching young people to work together and accept victory and defeat alike.” F

It weakened into a severe cyclonic storm around 8.30 am, with wind speeds dropping to 110-120 kmph. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu held a telephonic conversation with Union Minister Amit Shah, briefing him on the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab across the State. According to an official release, during the conversation, the Chief Minister detailed the prevailing situation in the affected districts, including Visakhapatnam, Konaseema, Kakinada, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, and Krishna. Informing the Union Home Minister about preliminary loss estimates, Mr. Naidu stated that agricultural crops covering over 70,000 hectares have been inundated due to the cyclone. He added that horticultural crops spread across more than 10,500 hectares have also suffered heavy damage, alongside widespread destruction to residential houses, road networks, and electricity poles. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said 17 districts of Odisha had been affected by heavy rainfall triggered by severe cyclonic storm Arnab, which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast early in the day. f52a2e5a18a99318.title: Hero MotoCorp Q2FY27 results: Net profit soars 42% to ₹1,861 crore
f52a2e5a18a99318.summary: India's largest two-wheeler maker Hero MotoCorp on Wednesday reported a 42 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated profit after tax for the second quarter of the current fiscal. The company's consolidated profit for the quarter came in at Rs 1,861 crore, against Rs 1,308 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing. 84ddd5a26ceb3cef.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI In view of Deepavali falling on November 8 (Sunday), the Tamil Nadu government has declared a holiday for government offices, State public sector undertakings, schools, colleges, and other educational institutions on November 9 (Monday). According to a government order (G.O.) issued by the Public Department, the holiday has been declared to allow people to travel to their native places to celebrate Deepavali with their families. Further, the government has announced that November 28 (Saturday) will be a working day to compensate for the holiday. As November 9 has not been declared a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, the State government has directed district Collectors to make arrangements for the functioning of treasuries and sub-treasuries with a limited number of employees. 599ccb85e851d798.title: U.P. approves robotics park and AI hub in Greater Noida
599ccb85e851d798.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 11:30 pm IST - Lucknow To be developed across approximately 69.52 acres, the park will play a key role in providing integrated facilities for robotics companies, technology start-ups, research institutions and industries, according to the U.P. government. | Photo Credit: file photo The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet on Tuesday approved the establishment of a robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) park in Greater Noida spread over 69.52 acres, estimated to generate more than 1 lakh direct and indirect jobs and add ₹2,000 crore annually to the State’s economy. “In a major step towards establishing Uttar Pradesh as a leading hub for advanced technology, industrial innovation and robotics manufacturing, the Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, on Tuesday approved a proposal to set up PRAGATI (Platform for Robotics and AI Growth Through Technology and Innovation) Park in Greater Noida. To be developed across approximately 69.52 acres, the park will play a key role in providing integrated facilities for robotics companies, technology start-ups, research institutions and industries,” read an official statement issued by the State government. 64a16fe7ecfacd7b.title: The SIR and its error margin
64a16fe7ecfacd7b.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 01:07 am IST ‘The Special Intensive Revision exercise has removed more than 13 crore names from the rolls since June 2025. Over a quarter were claimed dead or duplicated, while most were marked as absent or shifted’ | Photo Credit: The Hindu For nearly a month, Indians across the country have courted the ire and might of the state over a question no citizen in a democratic nation should have to ask. Their anger stems from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise which has removed more than 13 crore names from the rolls since June 2025. Over a quarter were claimed dead or duplicated, while most were marked as absent or shifted. At one booth in Delhi’s Bela Estate, officials cut 728 out of 729 voters , citing address proof discrepancies. Who decided that so many names should come off the rolls and on what basis? While the political answer is being debated on the streets and in Parliament, it is clear that the SIR has changed how a voter’s place on the roll is decided. In 1995, the Supreme Court held that a name already on the roll should be presumed to be there legally. The SIR replaced that presumption with a data-matching exercise. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has relied heavily on software for a public task where a single error costs a citizen their vote. Rolls from the last intensive revision (mostly in 2002) were hastily digitised from Bengali, Kannada, and other regional languages, auto-transliterated by the machine into English, and matched against new enumeration forms. Then a second layer of “logical discrepancies,” such as a parent-child age gap of less than 15 years, was applied. Shivakumar on Tuesday sought cooperation from MLAs and MLCs from Bengaluru to break what he called the “garbage mafia” in the city, even as the Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited (BSWML) is re-tendering 16 of 21 waste management packages. Mr. Shivakumar held an all-party meeting at his official residence, Krishna, to discuss garbage management and development projects in the city. However, R. Ashok, Leader of the Opposition, who recently alleged irregularities in garbage management tenders, didn’t attend the meeting. Mr. Ashok had accused the government of favouring an ineligible company and demanded a high-level probe into the matter. He said that one of the ₹133-crore tenders floated by the GBA had been awarded to a private company despite the firm failing to meet the eligibility criteria. Meanwhile, Tuesday’s meeting saw discussion about the recent cancellation of tenders. Mr. Shivakumar briefed the meeting on the BSWML’s plan to restructure waste management by awarding 33 contracts for waste collection in 27 Assembly constituencies. The move is aimed at increasing the waste collection capacity in the city and ensuring seamless transportation, he said. The new tenders would provide for the collection of up to 9,000 tonnes of waste. GPS tracking would be mandatory for all waste collection vehicles, and only new vehicles would be permitted under the contracts, he said. According to BSWML officials, only five contractors accepted the waste management tenders. Karee Gowda, Chief Executive Officer, BSWML, told The Hindu that the rest have been demanding a nearly 30% premium on the actual contract value. 9c874c8f5b77aa3c.title: Fouled waters: On Rajasthan’s river pollution
9c874c8f5b77aa3c.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 01:15 am IST The Supreme Court has pulled up, once again, the Rajasthan government over industrial effluents flowing into the Jojari river and the deadly risk it poses for the people depending on it. The problem is decades old — public interest litigation in the Rajasthan High Court alerted State machinery to the problem in 2011 — indicating an oversight by the State bordering on the systematic. The Jojari, the Luni, and the Bandi are seasonal rivers in the State’s arid western region, flowing through Jodhpur, Balotra, and Pali districts. This region has also evolved as a textile-dyeing and steelworking hub, and untreated or insufficiently treated effluents from these factories have run directly into the rivers and soil, endangering the health of around 20 lakh local residents. The region also suffers rampant illegal sand mining in riverbeds. The sewage treatment plants have been able to accommodate only around half of the sewage generated in the three urban centres, according to the State’s submissions to the Court in 2025, even as the Court recorded substantial underutilisation at common effluent treatment plants. The combination is suggestive of industrial sources bypassing treatment facilities, poor connections between the sources and the facilities, and/or insufficient capacity at particular sites or in specific periods. The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. 47b7d989794ec645.title: Asian Champions Trophy: India slams 13 past hapless Bangladesh
47b7d989794ec645.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:17 am IST - Jalandhar Harmanpreet Singh drew first blood for India. | Photo Credit: X@TheHockeyIndia For a city hosting its first-ever international hockey tournament, the result of India’s opening match in the Asian Champions Trophy (ACT) against Bangladesh was the perfect initiation. But less so for coach Craig Fulton and the team’s long-term plans. With local boys among the scorers and India stamping its authority in the 13-0 win on Tuesday, the result ensured the full house had enough reasons to celebrate. Mandeep Singh — among the five players who began on this very ground of the Olympian Surjit Singh Stadium — struck three of those and created as many. Captain Harmanpreet Singh, another local hero, started the rampage in the second minute and India was up by four in the first 15 minutes and six at half-time. Jarmanpreet Singh and Amit Rohidas, in defence, and Nilakanta Sharma, in the middle, were also impressive. Nilakanta even scored against an opponent that barely challenged the Indian might. Nilakanta, later, announced that he will retire at the end of the tournament. The highlight of the day was the drone show featuring the State, its culture, sporting history and legacy and sparkling under the night sky. The results: India 13 (Harmanpreet Singh 2-pc, 44-pc, Mandeep Singh 3, 10, 54, Shilanand Lakra 15, Abhishek 18, Nilakanta Sharma 26, Dilpreet Singh 43-pc, 44, Jugraj Singh 46-pc, Hardik Singh 60, 60) bt Bangladesh 0; Malaysia 5 (Abu Kamal Azrai 4, 14, Akhimullah Anuar 14, Faizal Saari 34-ps, Azimuddin Kamaruddin 35-pc) bt China 4 (Yaqi Wang 11, Moda Ne 12, Benhai Chen 27-pc, 44-pc); Japan 3 (Kentaro Fukuda 14, Ryoma Ooka 36, Kazumasa Matsumoto 52) bt Korea 2 (Han Sangjun 15, Jeong Junseong 59). 833c8524532cb779.title: Fifty years ago | ITDC plan to build hotels abroad
833c8524532cb779.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 03:45 am IST New Delhi, October 27: Indian Tourism Development Corporation, world’s second biggest public sector undertaking of its kind running a chain of hotels, motels, travellers lodges, beach resorts and forest lodges in the country is planning to set up initially about half a dozen ‘Indian restaurants’ at ‘strategic’ places in the world. According to Lt. Gen J.T. Sataravalla, Chairman and Managing Director of ITDC, now that the Corporation has already built up the necessary hotel infrastructure at important tourist centres within the country, it wants to popularise the famous Indian dishes to the foreigners at these restaurants abroad and also attract them to visit India. The location of these Indian restaurants abroad has not yet been finalised but they will be set up at some of the important world capitals. Some of them are likely to be located in the oil-rich Gulf countries. The managers of these restaurants will be specially trained in marketing Indian tourism abroad. The ITDC, which expects to earn Rs 7 crores of foreign exchange during 1975-76, has already entered the field in giving technical assistance abroad in running hotel industry. It is setting up an Indian restaurant at Prague with Czech collaboration. 5714814b4ebd740c.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 05:00 am IST - CHENNAI Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited and Apollo Foundation celebrated the impact of the ‘Total Health’ model at Aragonda in Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Prathap C. Reddy, founder-chairman, Apollo Hospitals Group, on Tuesday stressed the need to take healthcare to the last mile and urged people to make health a priority. Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited (AHEL) and Apollo Foundation celebrated the impact of the ‘Total Health’ model in Aragonda, Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh. It began with a rural hospital and evolved into an integrated approach to community development, bringing together healthcare, preventive health, education, nutrition, safe drinking water, skill development and livelihood opportunities to impact over 483 million people. Total Health, a Corporate Social Responsibility initiative of AHEL, was launched by the foundation in Aragonda in 2013. The occasion also marked completion of 1,000 total knee replacements at Apollo Hospitals in Aragonda. Taking part in the event, Dr. Reddy said that Total Health has made a significant impact in people’s health. Noting that his intention is to bring healthcare to the people, to the last mile, he said that the hospital at Aragonda has completed 1,000 total knee replacement surgeries without infections. He recalled that, during an earlier tenure of Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Apollo took over the management of the District Hospital in Chittoor, which is now a 800-bed facility. District hospitals providing best care for the public will enable last mile healthcare, he added. Dr. Reddy also emphasised on preventive healthcare, urging people to make health a priority and undergo health check-ups. 3d6fcfb9adea7ad0.title: WPL auction: Sneh among biggest names in the fray
3d6fcfb9adea7ad0.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:28 am IST - Kochi: Sneh Rana has been released by Delhi Capitals. | Photo Credit: File photo: K.R. DEEPAK By the time the first name comes up at the WPL’s mini-auction on Wednesday, the third ODI between India and Zimbabwe would have reached somewhere around the halfway mark in Vadodara. India’s middle-order batter Tejal Hasabnis is likely to be curious about what is happening at Grand Hyatt here. She is one of the 146 players who will go under the hammer. In the only chance she got in the Zimbabwe series, she may have lasted only five balls, but last month she had done really well for India-A against the touring Australia-A. So Tejal should interest some of the franchises. There could be even more interest in Sneh Rana, the off-spinning all-rounder released by Delhi Capitals. Sneh is, in fact, among the biggest names at this auction. Others include Australia’s T20 World Cup-winning captain Sophie Molineux, her compatriots Grace Harris and Jess Jonassen, Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu and England opener Sophia Dunkley. Among the capped Indian players are G. Kamalini, Kiran Navgire, Uma Chetry, Taniya Bhatiya, Saika Ishaque, Asha Sobhana, Priya Mishra, Titas Sadhu and Saima Thakor. There are some interesting names among the uncapped Indians, too. Like the 16-year-old Ira Jadhav, who last year smashed an unbeaten 346 off 157 balls for Mumbai against Meghalaya in the Women’s Under-19 One-Day tournament. There are only 27 available slots — including 20 reserved for the Indians. Going into the auction, UP Warriorz could well be a bit more excited, and anxious, than the other four franchises. Warriorz have the biggest purse of ₹3.75 crore. That is a lot more than Gujarat Giants (1.25 crore), Royal Challengers Bengaluru (1.15 crore), Delhi Capitals (1.1 crore) or Mumbai Indians (90 lakh). It would be fascinating to see how Warriorz try to turn the auction into a mega opportunity. Published - October 27, 2026 09:28 pm IST Terms & conditi

3acdfc41d1732b5e.title: India’s ‘balancing act’ risks eroding Russia’s trust
3acdfc41d1732b5e.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 01:32 am IST ‘India’s public appeal to Russia to end the endless war in Ukraine can be read as a counter-signal to Washington’ | Photo Credit: Reuters The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31-September 1, 2026, and the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, 2026, were remarkable. Iran received considerably more attention and support from members of both the groups, far more than anticipated. More consequential, however, was the shift in India’s stance on the United States-Israel war against Iran and Russia’s war in Ukraine. Traditionally, the SCO and BRICS summits have offered the three major powers — Russia, India and China — an opportunity to demonstrate their mutual solidarity. For Russia, it is a platform from which it can signal to the West that it is not isolated and still has powerful allies. The expansion of the SCO and BRICS under China’s leadership showcases its growing power to the West. For India, the SCO and BRICS have been useful for demonstrating its strategic autonomy. India has sought to remain welcome in both western and non-western forums, from the G-7 to the SCO and BRICS. a840cc2528aeffa9.title: Sreedharan tells Keralam govt. to ‘ignore’ technical panel’s objections over high-speed rail project
a840cc2528aeffa9.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:29 am IST - Kozhikode Technocrat E. Sreedharan addressing the media in Kozhikode on October 27. | Photo Credit: K. Ragesh Technocrat E. Sreedharan has said that the Keralam government should “ignore” and “overrule” the objections raised by the expert committee which studied the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation’s (DMRC) high-speed rail project proposal connecting Thiruvananthapuram and Kannur. He was addressing the media after delivering a talk on the subject organised by the Malabar Chamber of Commerce here on Tuesday (October 27). The expert panel was constituted by the government to examine the technical, financial and environmental aspects of the project. Transport Secretary K. Biju was its convener, and J. Vinayan, C. Veeramani and Sreedhar Radhakrishnan were members representing the subjects railways, finance and environment, respectively. The committee found the DMRC’s report to be “incomplete” and suggested a detailed examination of the technical, financial and environmental feasibility of the project. Replying to a question, Mr. Sreedharan, however, said that the committee had “no expertise” on the subject and that it had only one railway expert. “They did not properly study the proposal. There were no detailed discussions either. They were asked to focus on five core issues, but they looked at only one. I think the government should ignore and overrule the panel’s report and go ahead with the DMRC proposal. The government has no other way,” he said. Asked if the government was sitting over the proposal because of his political links with the BJP, Mr. Sreedharan said he did not think so. d7c98fa1838bef1b.title: Three girls missing in Tiruvannamalai
d7c98fa1838bef1b.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 12:18 am IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Three schoolgirls were reported missing after they did not return home from school in Thandrampattu village near Chengam town in Tiruvannamalai on Monday. The police said A. Mahalakshmi, 15, A. Maheshwari, 14, and R. Nithya, 13, had left their house after their parents scolded them for not going to school for nearly a month. The police said that as the girls’ parents stayed in Kerala for work as wage labourers, they visited home occasionally. The three children were under the care of Unnamalai, 65, who stayed at a rented house in Thandrampattu village. Two siblings Maheshwari and Maheshwari study in class X and IX respectively at the Government Girls Higher Secondary School, while Nithya is a class VIII student at the Government High School in the village. The police said that the three girls were upset after their parents scolded them over phone for not going to school. Around 4 p.m , they left home in uniforms and did not return. A case was registered by Thandrampattu police. Special teams were formed to find the children and a probe is under way. 663259d5338ee00e.title: BJP government spending 'unprecedented resources' to malign Rahul, says Priyanka
663259d5338ee00e.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 12:40 am IST - New Delhi Congress General Secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. File photo: AICC via PTI Lok Sabha member from Wayanad and Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) said it took “immense courage, tenacity and the perseverance of a true warrior” to stand against an “onslaught of lies”, a day after her brother and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was acquitted in a defamation case by a court in Uttar Pradesh. Responding to Mr. Gandhi’s post on X, in which he wrote “Satyam Shivam Sundaram”, Ms. Vadra accused the government of using “unprecedented resources” to malign her brother. “This government has spent unprecedented resources on a filthy campaign to malign my brother, to defame him and slap bogus cases on him simply for fearlessly telling the truth. It takes immense courage, tenacity and the perseverance of a true warrior to stand against an onslaught of lies, the way he has,” she said. “One by one the chips will fall. The truth will emerge clear and strong. This is just the beginning,” Ms Vadra added. Mr. Gandhi was acquitted by the MP-MLA court in Sultanpur on Monday (October 27, 2026) in a defamation case arising from his remarks against then BJP president Amit Shah in 2018. A day after the court verdict, he invoked a Sanskrit phrase “ Satyam Shivam Sundaram ”, which signifies truth, auspiciousness and beauty. 15ae79d77327fa8f.title: Radhatri Nethralaya conducts workshop on first aid for firecracker-related eye injuries
15ae79d77327fa8f.summary: Updated - October 27, 2026 11:46 pm IST - CHENNAI Participants at the workshop organised by Radhatri Nethralaya in T. Nagar on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Radhatri Nethralaya conducted its 14 th annual workshop on first aid for firecracker-related eye injuries at its T. Nagar branch on Tuesday (October 27, 2026). The workshop was attended by 65 students and 30 teachers from 20 schools in Chennai. A press release said Medical Director Vasumathy Vedantham led the hands-on session, during which students enacted various scenarios involving firecracker-related eye injuries and learned first-aid measures. The participants received certificates, first-aid kits, and pamphlets to distribute in their respective schools, the release added. Philanthropist and entrepreneur Subash Chand Ranka was the chief guest. Praveen Krishna, medical director, Radhatri Nethralaya, said thousands of students had benefited from the workshop over the past 14 years. d0f0c499730df824.title: Cyclone Arnab leaves parts of Visakhapatnam in darkness
d0f0c499730df824.summary: Updated - October 27, 2026 11:44 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Vehicles navigate a waterlogged Railway Station Road in Visakhapatnam amid heavy rain on Tuesday. K R Deepak | Photo Credit: KR DEEPAK Prolonged power interruptions following ‘Cyclone Arnab’ have caused considerable hardship to residents in several parts of Visakhapatnam, with people in Kancharapalem and Akkayyapalem reporting outages lasting several hours. According to complaints by residents of Kancharapalem, they said: “Electricity supply was disrupted since 5 a.m. on October 27, leaving several neighbourhoods, including Kapparada, Babuji Nagar, Indira Nagar, Sanjeevayya Colony and adjoining hill-slope settlements, without power for nearly 18 hours.” The prolonged outage added to the anxiety of people living in vulnerable hillside areas amid the cyclone threat. The absence of electricity affected routine activities, with elderly persons, children and other residents facing difficulties. Residents alleged that repeated attempts to contact the electricity department had failed to elicit a response. They also complained that the toll-free helpline and local electricity office telephone numbers were not functioning effectively, leaving them uncertain about when the power supply would be restored. Similar complaints emerged from Akkayyapalem, Madhurawada and a few other localities, where residents reported power outages for several hours on Tuesday. They alleged that complaints had not resulted in prompt action and appealed to officials to expedite restoration work. The outages have also raised questions among residents about the resilience of the city’s power distribution network during extreme weather events. Residents sought clarity on the proposed underground cabling works, reportedly estimated at ₹800 crore, and the extent to which such infrastructure had been implemented in the affected localities. 73dea3f01655703d.title: ACB arrests Mirchowk inspector, home guard in ₹3 lakh bribe case
73dea3f01655703d.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:46 am IST - HYDERABAD Mirchowk Inspector of Police M. Kondal Rao and Home Guard Abid Ali. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested Mirchowk Inspector of Police and a Home Guard on Tuesday for allegedly demanding ₹6 lakh and accepting a part payment of ₹3 lakh from a complainant in return for closing a case against his father. According to the ACB, City Range-1 officials caught M. Kondal Rao on October 27 after he accepted the bribe through Home Guard Abid Ali. The ₹3 lakh in tainted currency was recovered from the possession of the home guard, the agency said. The ACB said the alleged bribe was demanded in return for doing an official favour, including closing the case registered against the complainant’s father, avoiding coercive action, and providing future support. The agency said the two police personnel had acted improperly and dishonestly to obtain an undue advantage. Both were arrested and are being produced before the Principal Special Judge for SPE and ACB cases at Nampally for judicial remand. The case is under investigation. The ACB has withheld the identity of the complainant for security reasons. The agency urged people facing demands for bribes from public servants to contact its toll-free number, 1064, for action under the law.
